name: Silvesterlauf Salzgitter
organizer: Move SZ - Wir fördern Sport e.V.

The event offers various running and walking distances for different age groups and ability levels. The race is a sporting highlight and a meeting place for runners and spectators who want to end the year on an active note together. Alongside the sporting competition, there is a team classification and an awards ceremony that gives special recognition to the children’s races.

Children’s race over 1.2 km for age groups 2013 to 2019

name: Silvesterlauf Magdeburg
description: The Magdeburg New Year's Eve Run is a traditional popular sporting event that has been held on the last day of the year for over 50 years. It brings together runners of all ages and ability levels in the city of Magdeburg. The event is known for its family-friendly atmosphere and its sporting end to the year, with over 900 participants crossing the finish line. The run is part of the Magdeburg City Rankings and is very popular in the region.

1.5 km children's run for the youngest participants

name: Silvesterlauf Berlin
description: The Berlin New Year’s Eve Run on December 31 gives runners the chance to end the year on an active note. The event offers three different distances (4 km, 6 km and 10 km) through the scenic Grunewald, with challenging sections such as Drachenberg and Teufelsberg rewarded with great views over Berlin. Alongside the sporting experience, fun takes centre stage, particularly with the option to run in costume and prizes for the best costumes. At the finish, all finishers receive a delicious Pfannkuchen as a sweet keepsake to hang around their neck.

Fantastic views across Berlin before the turn of the year
A choice of distances: 4 km, 6 km and 10 km
additional: The start and finish are near Mommsenstadion (Waldschulallee 34, 14055 Berlin). The race pass and race number will be sent by email in advance. Race materials can be collected on site from 10:00 a.m. on the event day. Timing is provided by a disposable transponder attached to the race number. The time limit is 1 hour 30 minutes. Water, tea and Pfannkuchen are available at the finish. Only reusable cups are used. Changing facilities are available at Mommsenstadion, but there is no bag drop. Results and certificates are available online that evening. Distances vary between 2, 4, 6 and 10 km; a run for all age groups; start and finish at Mommsenstadion; refreshments include Pfannkuchen, with awards for the top finishers and the most original costumes.

name: Silvesterlauf Neuss
description: The Silvesterlauf Neuss is an established 10 km race that starts at 12:00 on December 31, 2026, at the Uedesheimer Deichtor. The course offers beautiful views of the Rhine as it passes through the Rhine meadows and Uedesheim fields, making it a perfect sporting end to the year. The event is suitable for all runners, from beginners to professionals, and combines a sporting challenge with a festive year-end atmosphere. The race also supports Aktion Luftballon, the support association for the children’s clinic at Lukaskrankenhaus Neuss, through fundraising.

Start at the Uedesheimer Deichtor with views of the Rhine
Run through the Rhine meadows and Uedesheim fields
additional: A supporting program in the start/finish area at the Deichtor creates a pleasant year-end atmosphere. The race raises funds for Aktion Luftballon, the support association for the children’s clinic at Lukaskrankenhaus Neuss. Record participation in 2025, with 1,040 registrations and 859 finishers. The event begins at 12:00 on December 31, 2026, at the Uedesheimer Rhine embankment and features a 10 km course. Training plans are also available, and the event is known for its friendly atmosphere and scenic running route.

name: Silvesterlauf Zossen-Ludwigsfelde

The event begins at Zossen Town Hall Square with a ceremonial start at 9:00 a.m. and the official start at 9:15 a.m. on the outskirts of Zossen. The route follows firmly frozen paths that are easy to run on in good weather. At the finish in Ludwigsfelde Forest Stadium, participants receive a commemorative medal and a prosecco as a reward.

name: Silvesterlauf Gießen
description: The traditional Sparkasse Gießen New Year’s Eve Run takes place on 31 December 2026 in Gießen-Ost and offers runners a varied event with four distances: a schoolchildren’s race, 5 km, 10 km and a half marathon. The start and finish are at Karl-Reuter-Weg, and all finishers receive a medal sponsored by Autohaus Erben. In addition to the races, there are awards and ceremonies for walkers and Nordic walkers, as well as a team competition with attractive prizes.

Four distances: schoolchildren’s race, 5 km, 10 km and half marathon

name: Silvesterlauf Schwalmstadt
description: The New Year's Eve Run in Schwalmstadt-Ziegenhain is a traditional race that has taken place every year on December 31 since 1970. The event offers a short 2.7 km race for children and young people, as well as a long 8.1 km race for adults. The race marks the end of the Schwalm-Eder Cup series and is known for its musical program, with samba rhythms by Sola Quente accompanying runners along the course. The event is organized by a dedicated team from TuSpo Ziegenhain and is a popular way for many track and field athletes to end the year.

The course runs through Schützenwald, with parking nearby

name: 12. Silvesterlauf an der Leine
description: The Silvesterlauf an der Leine in Hanover is a popular end-of-year race that traditionally starts at 1:00 p.m. on December 31. The event offers a 7.7 km loop on mostly paved paths along the Leine, through the Steintormasch, to the Wasserkunst and back along the Ihme. The race is organized by Hannoverscher Radsportclub (HRC), Bladerunner and Trimindous UG, and is known for its friendly atmosphere, with mulled wine and bratwurst after the race. Every finisher receives a wheat beer glass featuring the event design as a keepsake. There is also a walking category, making the event appealing to a range of participants.

name: Oudjaarsrun
description: On 31 December 2026, LSV Invictus will organize the second edition of the Oudjaarsrun in Appelscha, a sporting event to end the year actively. Participants can choose between two distances: 5 km and 10 km. The course is fully paved and runs through the beautiful Drents-Friese Wold National Park, with the start and finish in the center of Appelscha. After the finish, there will be an opportunity to celebrate the sporting year with music and a convivial atmosphere in the Steegdenhal.
course_highlights: Fully paved course
Run through Drents-Friese Wold National Park
Start and finish in the center of Appelscha, on Boerestreek

Ample parking is available for participants and visitors. Start times are 11:00 and 11:10. Parking is available at Pretpark Duinenzathe and in the center of Appelscha. Participants can choose between 5 km and 10 km. Festive gathering in the Steegdenhal.

name: Oliebollenloop
description: The Oliebollenloop is the final sporting challenge of the year in the north, held on 31 December in and around Gorredijk. The race offers 4-mile and 10 km distances, with separate starts for solo runners and businesses. There is also a kids’ run with three distances for different age groups. The route is safe from traffic and well marked, and a delicious reward awaits afterwards: oliebollen.
course_highlights: 4-mile and 10 km courses through Gorredijk with aid stations
Low-traffic route with traffic marshals for safety
Kids’ run with distances of 600m, 900m and 1600m for different age groups
additional: Kids’ run start times: 600m at 10:45, 900m at 11:00, 1600m at 11:15. 10 km starts at 12:05, 4 miles at 12:20. Business run available for teams of 3–5 participants; finishing time is based on the first 3 finishers. No race-day registration. Register online until 30 December at 22:00 or until the limit is reached. Entries in October and November receive a free Craft Oliebollen running shirt. Bib transfers are possible via the platform until 13 December at 23:59. Registration is online until 30 December; no race-day registration is available. Start times are around 12:00, with the start location at Sportcentrum Kortezwaag. Parking advice: cycle or carpool; road closure from 11:00.

name: Sylvestercross
description: The Sylvestercross is an annual running event in the Lange Duinen of Soest, known as the most beautiful cross-country race in the Netherlands. The event takes place over two days, with atmospheric Sylvester by Night runs on 30 December and various fun runs and official races on 31 December, including cross-country races for different age groups and ability levels. Since 2025, the Sylvestercross has held bronze status in the World Athletics Cross Country Tour, making it an important event for competitive runners. The course features challenging routes through dunes and woodland, with special loops for young runners and recreational runners, as well as a new 21.5 km trail run.
course_highlights: Course in the Lange Duinen of Soest, through dunes and woodland
Four different loops ranging from 400 metres to 3,300 metres
New Sylvester Trail Run of 21.5 km along the former forest marathon course
additional: The Sylvestercross includes various races for different age groups and ability levels, including a relay cross-country race and a G-cross. The relay cross-country race is a team event with 4 participants, each running one 1,900-metre loop. Dogs are not allowed on the course. The Sylvestercross is part of the National Cross-Country Circuit and gives athletes the opportunity to earn points in the World Athletics rankings. Various distances and categories, including a night run and relays; event on 30 and 31 December 2026; registration available via the website.

name: Katerloop
description: The Katerloop is a traditional running race organized by the Limmer IJsclub during the Limmer Kermis. The race attracts both children and adults and offers various distances, including 5 and 10 kilometers. The course passes through, among other places, the garden of the Cornelius Church and is known for its friendly, sporting atmosphere. The race starts in the morning, with the youngest children setting off at 10:00 and adults at 10:30. The Katerloop is an annual event with a warm community and enthusiastic participants.
course_highlights: Course through the garden of the Cornelius Church
Distances of 5 and 10 kilometers
Starts during the Limmer Kermis in Limmen
additional: Registration is handled via email confirmation. After confirmation, the site administrator will get in touch. There are separate start times for children and adults. The organizer is the Limmer IJsclub, founded in 1895. The Katerloop in Limmen is held during the Limmer Kermis and is known for its small-scale, welcoming atmosphere. The edition in Numansdorp on January 1, 2027, offers participants a race bib including a commemorative cup, and registration is open until December 28.

name: Florijn Winterloop
location: Sportpark De Koekel, Woudenberg, Utrecht, Netherlands
description: The Florijn Winter Run is an annual running and walking event in Woudenberg that has marked the athletic start of the new year for more than 30 years. The routes pass through the beautiful Den Treek Estate and the Utrechtse Heuvelrug, combining paved and unpaved paths. The event is suitable for recreational runners and experienced athletes alike, with several distances, including 5 km and 10 km forest runs. The atmosphere is sporty and friendly, with a rich tradition and a true Florijn spirit.
course_highlights: Routes through Den Treek Estate and the Utrechtse Heuvelrug
A mix of paved and unpaved paths
The private ‘Ravensloot’ path is accessible exclusively during the event

The event also includes a winter walk and features an extensive route at the sports park in Woudenberg.

description: The Nieuwjaarsloop De Wilp is a welcoming running event held annually in the picturesque village of De Wilp. With distances ranging from a youth run to a half marathon, it offers a suitable challenge for every level. The route passes through the beautiful Groningen-Frisian countryside, with wide-open views and a warm atmosphere at the start and finish. The event is known for its friendly, sporty character, bringing runners and spectators together to start the new year actively.

The race offers distances of 5 km, 10 km, and a half marathon (21 km), and is open to both those who wish to jog or walk, as well as to those who are well-trained and fast. There is also a children's race, where all participants receive ice cream. Race numbers can be purchased at Lier Station, and the race starts at 12:00 PM.

name: De Nieuwjaarsloop
location: Leiden Atletiek, Leiden, South Holland, Netherlands
description: The Nieuwjaarsloop in Leiden is an accessible running race and a sporty way to start the new year. Participants can choose from distances of 5, 10 or 15 kilometres, with the start and finish on the athletics track. The race is organised by Leiden Atletiek in collaboration with Currimus and Loopgroep Oegstgeest. It is part of the Zorg & Zekerheid Circuit, but taking part in the circuit is not mandatory. The race focuses above all on the enjoyment of taking part, with prizes for the fastest runners.

description: The Douwe Kleefstraloop is a recreational running race starting at Lionitas athletics track in Leeuwarden. It offers several distances: a 1 km kids’ run, 2 km, 5 km, 10 km and 16.1 km (10 English miles), with the routes measured exactly. The 10 km route passes through Goutum and Zuidlanden, while the 16 km route follows the same course with an extra loop via Bredyk, a tunnel under the railway and part of the Elfstedentocht route. After the race, all participants receive a cup of hot chocolate. The Douwe Kleefstra and Sietske Rijpstra trophies are awarded to the fastest man and woman in the 10 English miles, respectively.

10 km route through Goutum and Zuidlanden

With several distances to choose from, it’s a great opportunity to end the Christmas holidays actively, start the new year in a sporty way, and enjoy team spirit and a friendly atmosphere. The route runs through the sports park and the adjacent Brestbos. There are prizes for the winners—and, of course, eternal glory.

The race takes place on public roads and offers several distances: 5 km, 10 km and 16.1 km running, plus a 16 km walking route. After finishing, participants receive a bucket of snert, a traditional treat. Prizes are awarded to the top runners in each distance and age category, and race numbers also serve as raffle tickets. Registration is online only and closes a few days before the event.

description: The Sylvester Race in Gothenburg is a popular 10 km race held on New Year’s Eve, starting and finishing at Heden. The course is flat and spectator-friendly, and runs for two laps through central Gothenburg, including Avenyn, Ullevi, Gårda and around Svenska Mässan. The race is a perfect way for both elite runners and recreational runners to end the year. Everyone who finishes receives a medal and has a chance to win prizes in a prize draw. All classes start together at 12:00, with a warm-up 15 minutes beforehand. Registration is via MittLopp, with designated start groups based on expected finish time.

The competition consists of five races in the region, with participants competing in various age categories for the overall win.

The course runs through the countryside around Hengelo, with the start and finish at the same location in Woolderes. The races are open to various categories and offer cash prizes and gift vouchers. description: The Snøkuten Nordhagarunden takes place on October 17, 2023, and has a distance of 9.5 km. The race is part of the Snøkuten series and offers participants the chance to challenge themselves in beautiful surroundings. The course is quite demanding but takes you through stunning nature, and it is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners. This is a popular event in Veldre Athletics' schedule.
course_highlights: The Nordhagarunden was the second to last of the season's six Snøkuter, and only 24 participants raced for time, while many others jogged along the course with reflective gear.

We cheer just as much for the one who crosses the finish line first as for the one who completes their very first race.

The lap is just over 7 km, with six laps making up the full marathon. Refreshments are available along the route and at the finish, including water, tea, broth and sports drink, and changing rooms are available.

name: De Knikker Zegerplasloop

description: The Knikker Zegerplasloop is a series of three running races held in November, January and February around the beautiful locations of Zegerplas in Alphen aan den Rijn. The races offer running distances of 5, 10, 15 and 20 km, as well as special youth distances of 400 and 1,000 metres on the athletics track. There are also walking distances of 5 and 10 km, starting at the same time as the 20 km running race. The start and finish are always on the AAV'36 athletics track, where changing rooms, showers and a canteen are also available. The race features official timing and a nearly traffic-free course through the Zegersloot area and around Zegerplas.

Race bibs can be collected at the Berg en Dal tennis club, and parking is limited. The Leemkuilcross takes place annually on the third Sunday in January.

The event is organised by Atletiekvereniging Haaksbergen (AVH) and is a great opportunity for both recreational and competitive runners.

Awards ceremonies take place approximately 45 minutes after the finish in the marquee at Jahnstadion. The event comprises a series of three 10 km races held in Hamm’s natural landscape and spa gardens. Registration is online, timing is provided by Race Result, and awards are given to the top participants and series winners.

The series takes place on three dates in January and February and offers different series for various performance and age groups, including 5 km, 10 km, 15 km and half marathon, as well as walking and children’s races. The races run through the wintery Hilden City Forest and offer a family-friendly atmosphere, with the start and finish at the TC Stadtwald Hilden club grounds. Race numbers can be collected in advance at the HAT fit fitness studio, and late entries are possible on site.

description: Rondje Oeken is a welcoming, small-scale running event held in the beautiful countryside around Oeken and Brummen. The route passes along rural roads, woodland edges and quiet paths, and is fully marked and largely traffic-free. The event is open to all levels, from beginners to keen runners, and is known for its friendly, sporting atmosphere. The start and finish are at De Vroolijke Frans in Brummen, where ample parking is also available.
course_highlights: Beautiful scenery with rural roads, woodland edges and quiet paths
Fully marked and largely traffic-free course
Start and finish at De Vroolijke Frans, Knoevenoordstraat 51, Brummen
additional: There are two start times: 10:00 for the 21.1 km and 10:30 for the 12 km. Parking is available at De Vroolijke Frans and on the field behind it. You can register using the registration form on the website, either in advance or on the day. The event is welcoming and focused on a friendly atmosphere, sportsmanship and safety, with experienced volunteers and first aid on site. The course varies from unpaved paths to trail; there is a children's run, and registration is available on the day. The start is at De Vroolijke Frans.

name: Uithoorns Mooiste De Loop
description: Uithoorns Mooiste De Loop is a welcoming and well-organized running race in Uithoorn, known for its varied and safe course. The race attracts many participants each year, including long-distance runners and children, and is supported by a large group of volunteers and traffic marshals. It is part of the Zorg & Zekerheid Circuit and offers a festive day of sport, with a focus on participants and a special anniversary atmosphere.
course_highlights: Varied and safe course
Special atmosphere and good organization
Part of the Zorg & Zekerheid Circuit
additional: The race is supported by around 125 volunteers and more than 50 traffic marshals. Participants are catered for with water stations along the course, fruit and a memento at the finish. At the 40th anniversary, special treats were handed out, including cream cakes and flower bulbs. There are multiple distances, including a children’s race and special categories, with registration via www.inschrijven.nl; the course runs through Uithoorn and the surrounding area, with traffic marshals and measures to minimize disruption.

name: WoolderEsloop
description: The Wooldereslopen is a running competition organized by MPM in Hengelo for more than 45 years. The competition consists of four races held during the first months of the year, with distances of 1.4, 5.1, 10 and 15 kilometers. The course runs through the countryside around Hengelo, with the start and finish at the same location in the Woolderes. The races are open to various categories and offer a friendly, sporting atmosphere for runners of different levels.
course_highlights: Course through the countryside around Hengelo
Start and finish at the same location in the Woolderes
Distances ranging from 1.4 to 15 kilometers
additional: Pre-registration closes on 3 January 2027; late registration is available on race day from 9:00 a.m. until half an hour before the start at Semmelweisstraat 46, IKC De Wooldermarke. Race numbers can be collected on the preceding Saturday between 3:00 and 5:00 p.m. or on race day. The race number includes a timing chip and is valid for all four races. Shower and changing facilities are available in the small sports hall on Woolderesweg, which closes at 1:15 p.m. A running shirt and medal can optionally be ordered during pre-registration and collected with the race number or after the finish. The standings are based on at least 3 of the 4 races. Wearing earbuds/headphones is discouraged. Bringing pets, strollers, etc. is not allowed. Participants can register for different distances, with the start and finish at Woolderes. The event offers prizes such as cash and gift vouchers. The race takes place on 31 January 2027 and is suitable for both recreational and competitive runners.

The race offers a challenging course, with a short cross of approximately 5 km, a long cross of approximately 10 km, and several junior cross distances. The short and long cross start at 10:00, followed by the junior cross at 11:10. The race is open to both recreational and competitive runners and is part of a series of cross-country races in the Oss region.

Short cross of approximately 5 km and long cross of approximately 10 km
Junior cross with several shorter distances

The location is near the car park of the Hoessenbosch open-air theatre in Berghem. Start times: 10:00 and 11:10; location near the Hoessenbosch open-air theatre in Berghem

Participants can choose from several distances by running 1 to 4 laps, making it suitable for both recreational and advanced runners. The start and finish are at the same location, and chip timing is used to record accurate times. The event is exclusively for employees and family members of companies affiliated with Railsport.
course_highlights: Course through hilly woodland with winding sandy paths
Unpaved terrain with one lap of 2.5 km
Start and finish at the same location

description: The Midwinter Marathon in Apeldoorn is a three-day running event held on the first weekend of February. It offers several distances, including a marathon with a unique route through the Natura 2000 area and the Kootwijkerzand, a 10 English Miles through wooded, hilly surroundings, and shorter distances such as the Night Run and Kidsrun. The marathon route is partly off-road and passes iconic locations such as Apenheul and Radio Kootwijk. The Midwinter Marathon is known for its welcoming organisation, beautiful natural scenery, and a broad field of participants, from recreational runners to competitive athletes.
course_highlights: Marathon route with 900 metres off-road across the Kootwijkerzand
Route through a Natura 2000 area, passing Apenheul and Radio Kootwijk
10 English Miles through wooded, hilly surroundings, with its highest point at 100 metres above sea level
additional: The marathon starts and finishes at AV’34 in the Orderbos. There is a welcome with coffee or tea and a treat, followed after the race by pea soup with rye bread and bacon, or a vegetarian option. The 10EM starts and finishes on the Loolaan, with changing rooms and showers in nearby gymnasiums. Start corrals for the 10EM are assigned based on expected finish time. The marathon is limited to 700 participants and registration closes once this limit is reached. There is no on-the-day registration. The 10EM has a maximum of 4,200 participants. There are several refreshment stations and medical support. The Midwinter Marathon also offers an app for live runner tracking. Several distances, including the Kidsrun, 8 km and marathon; event in February 2027; registration opens in October 2026.

name: Blaauwbek Marathon
description: The Blaauwbek Marathon is an atmospheric winter marathon around Oldambtmeer in Blauwestad. The half and full marathons start in Bad Nieuweschans and finish at De Rietkraag, with bus transport from the finish to the start. There are also 5 km and 10 km distances that start and finish at De Rietkraag, featuring a unique course across the airfield. In addition to running events, there are 10 km and 20 km walking routes and special distances for children. The organizers provide warm refreshments along the way and a warm welcome at the finish.
course_highlights: Course around Oldambtmeer, with beautiful scenery and trails
Separate start and finish locations, with bus transport for marathon runners
Unique course across the airfield for the 5 km and 10 km distances
additional: The half marathon starts at 11:15 with bus transport from De Rietkraag. The full marathon starts at 9:45 with bus transport from De Rietkraag. The finish closes at 16:30 for both marathon distances. Children start the 5 km at 15:30. Walkers can start independently after receiving their route. The event offers various distances, including youth and walking routes, and bus transport for marathon runners. The event returns after several years’ absence and is marked by a winter theme and a convivial atmosphere.

name: Gletsjerkuil Ees Cross
organizer: Loopgroep SGO, Vomos UNESCO Geopark Hondsrug
description: The Gletsjerkuil Ees Cross is a challenging cross-country race set in the unique landscape of the Hondsrug UNESCO Global Geopark. The race takes place in Ees and offers two distances: a short route of approximately 5 km and a long route of approximately 9 km, both along unpaved paths through woodland and heathland. The route passes along narrow paths, several glacial pits and the storm-damaged forest with fallen trees, making for an adventurous run surrounded by nature. The cross is part of the Hondsrug cross-country circuit and is organised by Loopgroep SGO, Gieten and Vomos.
course_highlights: Entirely unpaved course, except for two crossings of cycle paths
Route through narrow heathland paths and several challenging glacial pits
Passage through the mysterious storm-damaged forest with fallen trees
additional: The cross is run without chip timing. No shower or changing facilities are available. The start location is Land van Bartje, Buinerweg 8, 9536 PG Ees. Public transport is available via Belbus line 59 from Borger. The cross is part of the Hondsrug cross-country circuit and is the 5th race in the circuit. Course through a nature reserve, starts at 11:00 and 11:10, registration via inschrijven.nl, no changing or shower facilities.

name: Kruikenloop
description: The Kruikenloop in Tilburg is an energetic and convivial race that traditionally marks the start of carnival in Kruikenstad. The course runs partly through nearby Stadsbos 013 and offers distances of 5, 10 and 15 kilometres, with the 5-kilometre loop available to run multiple times. There is a special 1,111-metre race for children, with fun and sportsmanship at its heart. After the finish, a festive after-party takes place in the Sarto clubhouse, and prizes are awarded for the best carnival outfits.

A 5 km loop that can be run 1, 2 or 3 times (5, 10 or 15 km)
Children’s race of 1,111 metres

Timing is recorded via a chip in the bib, with results available online shortly afterwards. Registration is via the website; the course runs partly through Stadsbos 013; expect a festive atmosphere with music and costumes; organised during carnival in Tilburg.

Alongside the half marathon, there are also 1 km kids’ run, 2 km, 5 km and 10 km distances, all measured exactly. After the race, all participants receive a cup of hot chocolate. In 2027, the event will be held for the eleventh time, offering participants not only a sporting challenge but also the opportunity to support a good cause. The start and finish are at Camping de Meene in Buurse, and the event is known for Twentish hospitality.
course_highlights: Run through the beautiful Twentse countryside
Start and finish at Camping de Meene in Buurse
Small-scale event with a maximum of 250 participants

name: Bocksten TrailRun Winter
location: Öströö fårfarm, Åkulla bokskogar, Varberg, Sweden
description: Bocksten TrailRun Winter is a scenic trail race held in the Åkulla beech forests, starting and finishing at Öströö Sheep Farm. The race offers several distances, from 5 km to the Ultra 44 km, and features beautiful forest trails, lake views and challenging elevation. With carefully planned routes through sensitive nature reserves and a strong sense of community among runners, this race is a unique experience for trail enthusiasts. Only 1000 race places are available, contributing to an exclusive and personal atmosphere.
course_highlights: Singing beech forests and enchanting spruce forests
Sparkling lakes along the route
Plenty of enjoyable elevation on beautiful trails
additional: Start times vary by distance: Ultra 44 km starts at 08:00, 12 km starts at 10:00, 5 km starts at 10:15 and 22 km starts at 10:30. Maximum 1000 race places in total. Startklar insurance can be purchased for a refund in case of illness or injury. The routes are not public in order to protect the nature reserves. Helping other runners when needed is mandatory. Littering results in disqualification. The event welcomes participants of all ages, celebrates 10 years, and is a community-oriented trail race in scenic surroundings.

name: Snapphane Race

description: Snapphaneracet is a challenging trail race that follows in the footsteps of the Snapphanar through the beautiful Ryssberget in Sölvesborg. The race offers several distances from 13 km to 50 km, with plenty of elevation and varied terrain, including beech forests and mossy coniferous forest trails. The winter edition offers an extra-tough challenge, with icy and muddy sections. The organizers look forward to welcoming runners for a tough and scenic experience in February.
course_highlights: Ryssberget, home to one of Sweden’s largest beech forests
Moss-covered, winding coniferous forest trails
Challenging hills and enjoyable downhill stretches
additional: Changing rooms, showers and toilets are available. Sweden Runners members and members of FysKompaniet Träningscenter receive a 15% discount on the entry fee. Startklar insurance can be purchased to receive a refund in the event of illness or injury. Name changes are possible for a fee up to 8 days before the race. The terrain is mostly unpaved and varied, making for a surprising and diverse running experience. The race is part of the MD Stoffering CrossCircuit van het Oosten and attracts both recreational and competitive runners.

Mostly unpaved, varied terrain
Changing surfaces make for a challenging cross-country race

Dogs and unregistered companions may not take part. In extreme weather conditions, the organisers may decide to cancel the race without refunding the entry fee. Cross-country race held at Het Lageveld recreational park in Wierden, with distances of 10 km and youth distances of 1.5 km and 2.5 km, usually in February.

name: Krokusloop
description: The Duinloop Circuit in Katwijk is a unique running series along the Dutch coast, featuring varied courses that combine challenging dune trails with fast beach sections. The Krokusloop, part of this series, offers a great atmosphere for both dedicated runners and recreational runners who enjoy running outdoors. With distances for different ages and ability levels, the event is open to everyone who wants to enjoy running at its best.
course_highlights: Varied courses with dune trails and beach sections
Unique running series along the Dutch coast
Suitable for all ages and ability levels
additional: Start times by distance: 500m Kids Run at 09:30, 1 km Kids Run at 09:35, 2 km Kids Run at 09:45, 5 km and 10 km at 10:00. Rankings are maintained for all distances, separately for girls/women and boys/men, based on the four best results in the circuit. Varied course with dune trails and beach sections, part of a series of running events along the coast.

name: Polderrun
description: The Polderrun is a sporting running event in the heart of Bleskensgraaf, bringing together participants from the region and beyond. The race offers several distances, including 3.5, 7, and 10 English miles, on a fast, fully paved course through the open polder. The Polderrun is known for its atmospheric start and finish in the middle of the village, and for the combination of nostalgia and renewal in the course. The event also supports a good cause, Stichting Moz Kids, making a meaningful contribution to vulnerable children in Mozambique.
course_highlights: Fast, fully paved course through the open polder

Start and finish in the middle of Bleskensgraaf
additional: Race numbers can be collected from 08:30 at the meeting area, De Spil. The meeting area also has a cloakroom, toilets, and limited shower facilities. Timing is provided by an Ipico chip in the race number, which measures net running time. There is a drink station at kilometer 8.1 of the 10 English Miles. Parking is available at three locations in Bleskensgraaf, with Melkwegplein and Weideweg preferred. Race-day registration is not possible. Registration for 2027 has not yet been announced, but the event is popular and sells out quickly. Facilities include parking, first aid, and Ipico timing. There is also an option to donate to a good cause.

There are several distances for both youth and adults, ranging from 1 km to 10 km. The Dinkelcross is suitable for both competitive runners and recreational participants and embraces the Olympic ideal that taking part is more important than winning. After the race, participants can enjoy a friendly atmosphere and homemade cake at the Zaandhoes, the start and finish location.

The course is almost entirely traffic-free and runs through the Zegersloot area and around Zegerplas, making it suitable for both beginner and experienced runners. A massage room offers free massages from Running & Walkingcenter Alphen aan den Rijn (bring your own towel). The cafeteria is open, and a limited number of lockers are available. Runners in the 15 and 20 km races pass a refreshment station on the track at the start of their second lap. On race day, registration is available in the cafeteria from 9:30 a.m. The races take place in winter conditions and offer options for walkers and young participants, with a maximum time limit of two hours for the walking distances.

The start and finish are at the same location in the Woolderes, creating a clear and friendly atmosphere for participants.

Distances of 1.4, 5.1, 10 and 15 kilometres
Start and finish at the same location in the Woolderes

The Wooldereslopen consists of four races held every three weeks during the first months of the year. Participants can enter the 1.4 km, 5.1 km, 10 km and 15 km distances. The organisers emphasise the friendly atmosphere and the course through the countryside around Hengelo.

The race is part of the Zorg en Zekerheid Circuit and offers distances of 5 km, 10 km and a half marathon of 21.1 km, as well as a 1 km family run. The half marathon takes you through woodland and dunes and along paved roads, bringing nature and sport together. The venue is Sportpark De Boekhorst, which has facilities including changing rooms, showers and a bag drop. The event is suitable for both recreational runners and competitive athletes looking to enjoy a challenging and varied course.

5 km and 10 km on fully paved roads alongside colourful bulb fields
Varied course through woodland, dunes and nature

Parking is available at several nearby locations, but cycling is preferred. The race is part of the Zorg en Zekerheid Circuit, with an attractive overall standings competition and prizes in every category. Course through dunes and bulb fields; registration via the website; start and finish at Sportpark De Boekhorst.

The race offers a challenging course, with a short cross of approximately 5 km, a long cross of approximately 10 km, and several youth cross distances. The venue is Strand TIEN at Gielekespad 10 in Oss, where runners can enjoy an off-road course. The short and long cross start at 10:00, and the youth cross starts at 11:10. The race is open to both recreational and competitive runners.

Short cross of approximately 5 km and long cross of approximately 10 km
Youth cross with several shorter distances

Venue: Gielekespad 10 in Oss; registration closes 30 minutes before the race; courses of approximately 5 km and 10 km.

name: Berden Voorjaarsloop
description: The Berden Voorjaarsloop in Venlo is a sporting event taking place on Sunday, 28 February 2027. The race offers a wide range of distances, from 500 metres for the youngest participants to 15 kilometres for experienced runners. A special feature is that participants in the 7.5 km and 15 km races run on Scopias’s professional 400-metre athletics track, adding a unique experience. The event is suitable for all ages and abilities and offers a fresh, energetic start to spring.

Safe and clearly laid-out courses past College Den Hulster and along Hagerhofweg
Routes through green surroundings, including the petting zoo and Vrijenbroek sports park

Distances range from 500 metres to 15 km, including youth races and a race on a professional athletics track; registration via inschrijven.nl; event in Venlo.

description: The 3bergenLOOP is an atmospheric running race in Driebergen, with three challenging courses: 6 km, 10 km and a half marathon. The routes follow unpaved forest trails, cycle paths and bridleways through the beautiful Bornia, Heidestein and Hoog Moersbergen estates. The race is known for its scenic, demanding courses and its focus on sustainability, with participants encouraged to bring their own reusable cups. The start and finish are at RCN Het Grote Bos, with refreshments available along the way and at the finish. The organizers provide a well-run event with chip timing and a welcoming atmosphere.
course_highlights: Routes along unpaved forest trails, cycle paths and bridleways
Half marathon through the Bornia, Heidestein and Hoog Moersbergen estates
Refreshment stations with water and sports drink along the route and at the finish
additional: Race numbers are sent to the home address provided. Start and finish at RCN Het Grote Bos. Refreshments at 9 km, 15 km and after the finish for the half marathon; at 4 km and after the finish for the 10 km; and after the finish for the 6 km. No medals are awarded. Racetimer chip timing is included. Race numbers can be transferred via the registration website. Participants are encouraged to use their own reusable cups to support sustainability. Routes have been adjusted due to area restrictions; registration opens in early December 2026; options are available to transfer race numbers and volunteer; the event takes an environmentally friendly approach with reusable cups and no medals; chip timing is included.

name: ACO van Elderen Crossloop
description: The ACO Van Elderen Crossloop is a challenging cross-country race organised by athletics club ACO Van Elderen in Ommen. The race is part of the Prins Sport-Vechtdalcrosscompetitie and takes place in the nature area around Ommen. The race starts on the athletics track, after which the course runs mostly off-road through the forest. There are three distances: 1.75 km, 5 km and 10 km, with participants running one or more laps through the forest. The cross-country race is known for its natural surroundings and varied course.
course_highlights: Start on the athletics track
Course runs mostly off-road through the forest
Three distances with different laps (blue and red)
additional: Registration is online only and open until 4 March 2027; no on-the-day registration is available. A lead cyclist will ride ahead of the runners during the race. For the 5 km and 10 km, day prizes are awarded to the first three women and men, provided by sponsors. For the youth distance (1.75 km), prizes are awarded to the first three in each category. Forest course, off-road terrain, online registration until 04-03-2027, prizes for the top three and course record

name: Halve Marathon van Haren
description: The RunX Haren Half Marathon is a spring classic, taking place for the 42nd time on Saturday, March 6, 2027, in Haren, Groningen. The event offers a sporty and enjoyable day, with distances of 21.1 km, 10 km, and 5 km recreational runs. The half marathon starts at 11:00 a.m. and the recreational runs at 11:20 a.m. By taking part, you support Jeugdfonds Sport & Cultuur Groningen, which helps children from families with limited means join sports or cultural clubs.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Sporthal Scharlakenhof in Haren
Route through the Felland Zuid industrial estate, 1,000 meters from the finish
Strict time limit of 2.5 hours for the half marathon

Medals are optional and cost an additional €2.50. The half marathon has a time limit of 150 minutes. The Road Traffic Act applies on the course. Registration opens on October 24, 2026; various routes are available for different levels; the event supports Jeugdfonds Sport & Cultuur Groningen.

name: Rondje Zwolle Marathon
description: Rondje Zwolle 2027 is the second edition of a small-scale marathon around the beautiful city of Zwolle, organised by Zwolselopers. The marathon is all about camaraderie, running together and enjoying the experience, without an emphasis on fast times or personal records. Participants can run the full marathon or sign up together and split the distance. Weekend long runs are organised to help participants train together. Fysiotherapie De Dobbe supports participants in getting fit for the start.
course_highlights: Marathon around the city of Zwolle
Small-scale event with a friendly atmosphere
Option to split the distance and take turns running together
additional: The marathon is intentionally small-scale, with a limited number of race entries. Friendly weekend long runs are organised in preparation. Fysiotherapie De Dobbe is a sponsor and provides support with injuries. The start is at Wijthmenerplas. The marathon is characterised by an informal atmosphere and training and running together with other participants.

The 10 km race is the official Open Frisian Championship and takes place on a unique, certified course through the beautiful countryside around Drachten. There are also 5 km and 1.5 km kids’ run distances, making the event suitable for runners of all levels and ages. The race combines a sporting challenge with a friendly atmosphere and offers prizes for the top runners and club champions.
course_highlights: The 10 km is the official Open Frisian Championship
Certified, fast course through the countryside around Drachten
Start and finish on the athletics track at AV Impala

Certified course, open to recreational and competitive runners, advance registration required, no on-the-day registration.

Participants can choose from a half marathon of 21.1 km, a fast 8 km, or youth races of 1 and 2 km. The paved course offers a lovely mix of nature and village scenery, with excellent facilities such as changing rooms, showers and parking close to the start. Organised by football club OVV and Voorne Atletiek, the event promises a safe, well-run day full of sporting fun.

Half-marathon course records: men 01:06.36; women 01:17.41. Parking is available close to the start, with several other parking options within walking distance. Paved course; facilities include changing rooms, showers and parking; registration is open.

The races offer a great atmosphere for both dedicated runners and recreational runners who enjoy running outdoors. The Noordduinloop, part of this series, takes place on 13 March 2027 and is one of a series of events held throughout the year.

A unique running series along the Dutch coast
Suitable for all levels and ages

The race is open to everyone who wants to experience trail running on lovely paths, with water available at two stations. It is a well-organised race with a long tradition and a friendly atmosphere for both beginners and experienced runners.

The course follows a marked hiking trail, with some sections additionally flagged
Water is available at approximately 9 km and in the start and finish area

name: WoolderEsloop
description: The Wooldereslopen is a running competition organised by MPM in Hengelo for more than 45 years. It consists of four races held during the first months of the year, with distances of 1.4, 5.1, 10 and 15 kilometres. The course runs through the countryside around Hengelo, with the start and finish at the same location in the Woolderes. The races are open to various categories and offer cash prizes and gift vouchers. Electronic timing is provided, and race numbers can be collected in advance or on race day.
course_highlights: Course through the countryside around Hengelo
Start and finish at the same location in the Woolderes
Distances of 1.4, 5.1, 10 and 15 kilometres
additional: Race numbers can be collected from 9:00 at IKC De Wooldermarke, Semmelweisstraat 46, 7555 NT Hengelo. The race number includes a timing chip and must be worn on the chest. A running shirt and medal are available as optional extras when registering in advance. Shower and changing facilities are available at Gymzaal Woolderesweg and close at 13:15. Race numbers can be collected on the preceding Saturday or on race day. Participants use the same race number for all four races. The standings are based on at least 3 of the 4 races. Bringing animals or pushchairs and using earbuds/headphones is discouraged or not permitted. Registration opens at 9:00, and the courses run through the countryside around Hengelo. Results from previous years are available, and the event has been organised for more than 45 years.

name: Equinox Adventure Ultra
description: Equinox Adventure Ultra is a unique trail-running race held during the spring equinox. The race is a long-distance experience in which teams of two runners navigate on their own and are self-sufficient through equal parts daylight and darkness. Participants can choose between a long distance of at least 100 km or a shorter distance of at least 50 km. The race starts on Saturday at 12:00 and runs until Sunday at 18:00, offering a challenging experience immersed in nature over a full day.
course_highlights: Long-distance trail running through forests and nature
Self-sufficient teams of two runners
Navigation through equal parts daylight and darkness during the spring equinox
additional: The race runs from Saturday at 12:00 until Sunday at 18:00. Each team consists of two self-sufficient runners who must navigate on their own during the race. The race is self-sufficient, with participants using a map and compass to navigate through forests, trails and open landscapes. The start location is secret, and the race takes place around the spring equinox in Nyköping, Sweden.

name: Vårtävlingarna
description: Vårtävlingarna is a classic running race in Gothenburg, held every year in early March. The race takes place on the well-known “grusåttan” course in Skatås, where participants can choose to run 8, 16 or 32 km. The event has a long tradition dating back to the 1960s and serves as a kickoff to the racing season in the Gothenburg area. The field is a mix of recreational runners and local elite athletes, and the race starts with a fast, lively surge. In 2026, Vårtävlingarna Trail will also make its debut.
course_highlights: The “grusåttan” course in Skatås, approximately 8 km per lap
Choose to run 1, 2 or 4 laps (8, 16 or 32 km)
Start and finish in Skatås, with a lively start reminiscent of calves let loose in a field
additional: 2026 start times: 32 km starts at 10:10, 16 km at 11:00, and 8 km at 13:00. The race is a mix of recreational runners and elite athletes. Vårtävlingarna Trail makes its debut in 2026. The start and finish are in Skatås. The race serves as a kickoff to the racing season in the Gothenburg area. The course is the “grusåttan” in Skatås. The race serves as a kickoff to the racing season in the Gothenburg area and has a strong tradition. This year’s edition includes a new trail race, offering participants additional variety.

name: Alfa Laval Stevensloop
description: The Alfa Laval Stevensloop is Nijmegen’s city run, taking place on 20 March 2027. The start is in the iconic Kronenburgerpark, and the finish is right in the centre of the oldest city in the Netherlands. The different courses offer varied routes through the city centre, past the city island, along Nijmegen’s skyline and through the natural surroundings of the Ooijpolder. The event is organised by Stichting Zevenheuvelenloop, which aims to get as many people as possible moving and provide a great running experience.
course_highlights: Start in Kronenburgerpark and finish at the Grote Markt
Climb up the Voerweg, featuring the Alfa Laval Cheering Zone
Varied routes through the city and nature, passing iconic sights such as the Stevenskerk and the Ooijpolder
additional: A supervised cloakroom for small bags is available at the start in Kronenburgerpark. The Voerweg is a challenging climb towards the end of the 5 km and half marathon, with a special Alfa Laval Cheering Zone where spectators and music provide extra encouragement. The Alfa Laval Hill Challenge rewards the fastest climb up the Voerweg with a €100 gift voucher for Runnersworld. Registration opens on 1 October 2026, race numbers can be collected in March 2027, and the event takes place on 20 and 21 March 2027.

description: The Midseumer Molnkoier is a unique evening walk that invites walkers to enjoy nature and culture in and around Vrouwenparochie. This walking event is made possible in part by many volunteers and sponsors, with the proceeds going to a good cause. The route passes the old grain mill and winds through the beautiful Frisian countryside, offering a special experience for lovers of walking and cultural history.
course_highlights: Evening walk past the old grain mill, De Vrouwbuurtstermolen
Natural and cultural surroundings of Vrouwenparochie
Unique atmosphere during midwinter and a scenic route
additional: Entry tickets can also be purchased at the start desk. The walking event is held at the old grain mill, De Vrouwbuurtstermolen, in Vrouwenparochie. Registration is available for several distances, and participants can enjoy a course through the beautiful countryside and mill surroundings.

name: Monnikenloop
description: The Monnikenloop is an annual running race held on the beautiful island of Schiermonnikoog. The race offers several distances, including a kids’ run, 5 km, 10 km and 10 English Miles, and attracts both recreational and dedicated runners. The event combines sporting spirit with a friendly atmosphere and invites participants to experience the island’s unique nature. The start and finish are centrally located, and there is plenty of opportunity to enjoy an atmospheric weekend with accommodation available on the island.
course_highlights: Routes across the island of Schiermonnikoog, through nature and dunes
Distances ranging from a 1 km kids’ run to 10 English Miles (16.1 km)
Start and finish in the village, in an atmospheric setting
additional: Kids’ runs start from 11:20, the 5 km starts at 12:40, the 10 km at 12:50 and the 10 English Miles at 12:30. The race pack includes a race number with chip and a bus pass for transport on the island. Participants must reserve their own ferry ticket. A running shirt can be ordered. Changes to registration can be made for a fee until the end of March. The start and finish are in the village, with changing and shower facilities. Several distances; registration opens on 1 October 2026; accommodation is available on the island; the event takes place in March.

name: Oldemeijercross
location: Recreatieplas De Oldemeijer, Hardenberg, Overijssel, Netherlands
description: The Oldemeijercross is one of the oldest running races in the region and is organized annually by AV Spurt'88. The race takes place around the De Oldemeijer recreational lake in Hardenberg and offers a challenging course with tough climbs, sand, and mud. This running event is for all ages, with the start and finish on the event hill at Oldemeijer. Spectators can cheer on the runners from several spots, adding to the lively, sporting atmosphere.
course_highlights: Tough climbs along the course
Route around the De Oldemeijer recreational lake
Sandy and muddy terrain
additional: Race-day registration is possible. The start and finish are on the event hill at Oldemeijer. The course is suitable for all ages, and there are several places for spectators to cheer on the runners. The 3 km course around Oldemeijer is challenging, with climbs, sand, and mud; the start and finish are at the event hill; registration via inschrijven.nl; no showers available.

name: Reeuwijkse Plassenloop
description: The Vosplan Reeuwijkse Plassenloop is one of the oldest running events in the Netherlands and has been held for more than 70 years. Each year, the event attracts runners from the region and beyond, who enjoy an active and sociable day. The course is completely flat and has little traffic. It runs through Reeuwijkse Hout and along the distinctive Reeuwijkse Plassen, making it an appealing and fast course. There are distances for all ages, from kids’ runs to 15 kilometres, including supervised youth distances.
course_highlights: Completely flat course with little traffic
Runs through Reeuwijkse Hout and along the Reeuwijkse Plassen
Clear kilometre markers and one lap per distance (5, 10 and 15 km)
additional: MYLAPS BibTag timing is used. The chip is attached to the back of the race number and does not need to be returned. Late registration is available on race day from 10:30 until half an hour before the start. The start and finish area is at Reeuwijkse Houtwal in the De Reeuwijkse Hout recreation area. Ample parking and toilets are available. There are no changing or shower facilities. Every finisher receives a commemorative medal. Cash prizes are awarded for the 5, 10 and 15 km races for men and women, plus an additional prize for a course record. Registration opens on 1 January 2027 via Inschrijven.nl. The event offers prizes and keepsakes for the winners, and preparation training sessions are available. Participants can register for different distances and age groups.

name: Marathon Alblasserwaard 750
description: The Alblasserwaard 750 Marathon is a unique, one-time marathon taking place on 20 March 2027 to celebrate 750 years of Alblasserwaard history. The 42.195-kilometre route runs from the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Kinderdijk, through characteristic polders, windmills, historic waterways and villages, to the finish at AV Typhoon in Gorinchem. The marathon offers runners a special experience through the open peat-meadow landscape and past iconic windmills and duck decoys, with the region’s landscape and history at its heart.
course_highlights: Start at Kinderdijk’s 19 windmills, a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Route along separated cycle paths and roads with limited traffic
Past historic waterways, polder windmills and characteristic villages
additional: Shuttle buses will run between Gorinchem and Kinderdijk for participants. Parking at the start is not possible and is discouraged. Bicycle parking is available at both the start and finish. The organisers aim to be sustainable by using biodegradable cups and cleaning the course after the event. Sweeper vehicles are available for runners who drop out. The minimum age to participate is 18. The marathon is a unique, one-time event celebrating the region’s history and beauty, with a maximum limit of 2,500 runners.

name: Dark Sky Trail Lauwersmeer

description: The Dark Sky Trail Lauwersmeer is a unique nighttime running and walking event held in the official Dark Sky Park Lauwersmeer, one of the darkest areas in Europe. The race offers three events: canicross, trail running and a walking tour, all approximately 10 km long. Participants run in the dark, with headlamps permitted only in emergencies, creating a special experience. Registration raises awareness of light pollution through a donation for each participant.

Approximately 10 km for canicross, trail running and the walking tour
Headlamps permitted only in emergencies
additional: The start location and meeting point is Activiteitencentrum Lauwersnest, De Rug 1, 9976VT Lauwersoog. A drink is available at the finish.
