description: The Sieber Mountain and Panorama Run returns on August 22, 2026, after a 14-year break, offering three challenging routes in the Harz with up to 900 meters of elevation gain. The event is handmade and welcoming, and challenges runners of all ability levels. From the family-friendly 4.5 km Nature Experience route and the 12.5 km Panorama Loop to the queen stage of 27.5 km with 900 meters of elevation gain, there is something for everyone. The runs take you through stunning natural scenery with panoramic views and offer an authentic Harz experience. Alongside the sporting challenge, there is a pasta buffet and a community village festival to round off the event.
course_highlights: Nature Experience: 4.5 km with 130 meters of elevation gain, family-friendly and ideal for beginners
Panorama Loop: 12.5 km with 500 meters of elevation gain to Großer Knollen, with impressive views
The Original: 27.5 km with 900 meters of elevation gain via Großer Knollen and Hanskühnenburg, challenging and legendary
additional: Race bib collection on August 21, 2026, from 16:00 to 21:00, and on August 22, 2026, from 07:00 at the Haus des Gastes in Sieber. Pasta buffet on Friday evening (available to book separately for €7.00). Participation in “The Original” and “Panorama Loop” is also possible outside the age categories with written consent from a parent or guardian. Children’s race for ages 6–12 on August 22, 2026, at 11:00. Awards ceremony and village festival afterward on the Großen Wiesen. Three routes: Nature Experience (4.5 km), Panorama Loop (12.5 km), The Original (27.5 km); up to 900 meters of elevation gain; family-friendly; advance booking with pasta buffet; communal carbo-loading; participation outside the age categories possible with parental or guardian consent.

name: THE HUMBLE CLUB Backyard Run IV
description: The Humble Club Backyard Run IV on August 22, 2026, on Oker Island in Braunschweig is a unique running experience that combines an athletic challenge with social commitment. The run supports the “Boxen gegen Parkinson” project and stands for exercise, community, and social responsibility. The event starts at 10:00 a.m., with entry from 8:30 a.m., and provides participants with still water and fresh fruit, as well as an exclusive finisher medal. Participants are asked to bring their own food and drink to ensure they are properly fueled.
course_highlights: Event on Oker Island in Braunschweig
Backyard Ultra format with loop running
Supporting the “Boxen gegen Parkinson” project
additional: Arrival is possible from 8:30 a.m. Basic provisions of still water and fresh fruit are included. An exclusive finisher medal is provided for all participants. Participants should bring their own food and drink. Event held in the Backyard Ultra format, starting at 10:00 a.m.; refreshments available on site; donations for “Boxen gegen Parkinson”; a sense of community in an ultramarathon format.

name: Arnstädter Bach-Ultra
description: The Arnstadt Bach Ultra is a 60-kilometer ultramarathon taking place on August 22, 2026, in Arnstadt. It was created in response to runners’ wish to run the 60 km relay leg as a standalone ultramarathon. The event is organized by SG Motor Arnstadt in cooperation with the Arnstadt city administration and offers a challenging course through the region. The race is an interesting initiative that will hopefully attract strong support and become part of Arnstadt’s diverse running tradition.
course_highlights: 60 km ultramarathon distance
Course runs around Arnstadt
Developed from the relay race into a standalone ultramarathon
additional: Electronic timing is provided by Sportident. Registration is via www.timing.sportident.com. The race is part of Arnstadt’s diverse running calendar, which includes several events throughout the year. Ultramarathon, 60 km, challenging course, in the Arnstadt region

name: Barumer Stick and Stone Run
location: Barumer Waldstadion, Barum, Lower Saxony, Germany

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Das Startgeld beträgt 25 € und beinhaltet eine Medaille und die Teilnehmerverpflegung im Zielbereich

description: The Barumer Stick and Stone Run is a challenging obstacle race taking place on August 22, 2026, at Barumer Waldstadion and in the surrounding wooded, hilly landscape of the Lüneburg Heath. The course follows sandy, muddy, and partly overgrown trails, with water obstacles such as ditches and a village pond. The event offers runners a varied challenge in a natural setting and is suitable for individuals and groups. Participants receive a medal and refreshments in the finish area.
course_highlights: Wooded, hilly landscape on the edge of the Lüneburg Heath
Sandy, muddy, and overgrown trails with water obstacles
4 km laps, run 1 to 3 times depending on the distance
additional: Individual start times between 2 and 4 p.m. will be sent to participants by email by August 21, 2026. The start and finish are at Barumer Waldstadion. Groups of 10 or more starters can take advantage of a discount promotion in which every fifth starter runs for free. Race packets are distributed at the race office 30 minutes before each start time. There is a wash area on site, and drinks and snacks are available in the finish area. The race takes place at Barumer Waldstadion and is suitable for all ability levels. Training plans and a family-friendly atmosphere also put the fun of obstacle racing first.

name: Jan Schüpp Bürgerlauf Wittmund
location: Stadion an der Breslauer Straße, Wittmund, Lower Saxony, Germany
description: The Jan Schüpp Wittmund Citizens’ Run is a running event organized by MTV Wittmund. It starts at the stadium on Breslauer Straße in Wittmund. The route runs through the town center, past the market square and Schlossplatz, and offers a challenging and varied course. Alongside the main races, there are also children’s and youth races, which are free to enter. The event is well organized with support from the police, fire brigade and German Red Cross (DRK), and is popular with runners and spectators.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the stadium on Breslauer Straße
Route through the town center, past the market square and Schlossplatz
Challenging course with a varied route
additional: Parking is available at the stadium and at the Schützenplatz on Auricher Straße. The event is medically supported by the police, fire brigade and DRK. Children’s and youth races are free to enter, while the main races have an entry fee. The event is hosted by an announcer and supported by local sports clubs. The race includes 5 km, 10 km and 1,200 m distances, with a supporting program, on-site registration and parking at the stadium and Schützenplatz. The event is very popular with participants and offers a festive atmosphere.

name: middenmang-Loop 2. Emder Vielfaltslauf
description: The middenmang-Loop is an inclusive diversity run in Emden, taking place for the third time on August 22, 2026. The run is for all age groups and people with and without disabilities, bringing everyone together to enjoy running. A range of events and distances—from the Kinner-Loop for children to the 10 km middenmang-Loop for experienced runners—offers something for everyone. The run is part of the Ostfriesische Sieben running series and promotes community, exercise and inclusion.
course_highlights: A range of distances for children, young people and adults with and without disabilities
An inclusive run focused on running together and overcoming barriers
Part of the Ostfriesische Sieben running series, with 5 km and 10 km distances
additional: The middenmang-Loop features a range of events and distances for all age groups and abilities. The event places particular emphasis on inclusion and community. The 5 km and 10 km runs are part of the Ostfriesische Sieben running series. Registration is online via the website. Contact person: Inga Weerts. An inclusive run with various distances for all age groups and abilities, and part of the Ostfriesische Sieben running series.

name: Sengbachtalsperrenlauf
location: Sengbachtalsperre, Leichlingen-Witzhelden, Rheinisch-Bergischer Kreis, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany

price_tiers.distance: Stadtwerke Solingen Familienlauf 1,2 km und 3,6 km

description: The Sengbach Reservoir Run is a traditional scenic race around the Sengbach Reservoir near Leichlingen-Witzhelden. The three main distances follow well-maintained forest trails and a paved section along the dam wall, on a loop of about 9.8 km with approximately 200 metres of elevation gain per lap. The course is traffic-free and runs through a protected landscape area. Families can take part in a separate race with shorter distances in the immediate vicinity of the event grounds. The event provides on-course refreshments and showers in nearby Kuhle.
course_highlights: Loop of approx. 9.8 km with 200 metres of elevation gain per lap
Well-maintained forest trails and a paved section along the dam wall
Traffic-free course in a protected landscape area
additional: Race packets will be available from 7:30 a.m. on race day at the registration tent. Showers are available at a school in the neighbouring village of Kuhle and are signposted. Refreshments including bananas, water, isotonic drinks and cola are provided about every 5 km; free tea and bananas are available at the finish. Certificates can be accessed online. The course is traffic-free, with two refreshment stations on the loop. A fundraising campaign for the Leverkusen Children's Hospice will be held. The course follows forest trails, with no roads. Donations to the children's hospice are welcome. Registration is open until race day; a late-entry fee of €5 applies from 11.08.2026.

name: Gladbecker Sparkassenlauf
description: The Gladbeck Sparkassenlauf is a traditional running event welcoming runners of all ages. It offers various distances, from the Bambini Marathon to the half marathon, as well as a team relay. All courses are DLV-certified and eligible for official rankings. Participants receive finisher medals and personalized race bibs bearing their names, making the running experience special. There is also a district championship classification and extensive award ceremonies.
course_highlights: DLV-certified courses: 1.5 km, 5 km, 10 km and half marathon
Personalized race bibs bearing participants’ first names
Live timing and net times for all races
additional: Finisher medals for all participants; personalized race bibs bearing first names; live timing with net times; changing rooms and showers at the stadium; valuables can be left at storage facilities; trophies and certificates for winners and age-group winners; team and club classifications; district championships with certificates and badges; no classification for the Bambini or walking events. Courses at Gladbeck Stadium; online registration; late registration available until 1 hour before the start; medical assistance provided by the German Red Cross; various course distances and categories.

name: ews Volks- und Spendenlauf
description: The 14th ews Volks- und Spendenlauf runs through Bad Segeberg, past scenic spots such as Kalkberg and the Great Segeberger Lake. Since 2011, the race has been a regular part of the city’s sporting calendar, combining athletic achievement with the enjoyment of exercising together and charitable engagement. The event supports selected projects each year, with donations divided among three projects in 2026. It is a community event that brings together exercise and social commitment.
course_highlights: Through Bad Segeberg
Past Kalkberg
Along the Great Segeberger Lake
additional: Team entries are only possible using a paper form, which must be sent by email to info@volkslauf-bad-segeberg.de by 02 October 2023. Race number collection takes place at the registration desk on 23 August 2026. Registration is online and requires agreement to the liability waiver and data protection terms. The focus is on enjoying exercise and charitable engagement. The race runs through Bad Segeberg and includes walking and Nordic walking. Donations support local projects. Registration is open until June 2026. Team and individual starts are possible.

name: TuS Hiltrup Halbmarathon
location: Stadion am Osttor, Münster, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The TuS Hiltrup Half Marathon is an established running event in Münster, starting and finishing at the Osttor Stadium. The course includes a lap of the stadium, runs along the canal promenade and through the Hiltrup residential area, offering a varied and attractive running environment. In addition to the classic half marathon, there is also a relay race, which is especially appealing to teams. The event is open to runners born in 2008 or earlier (individual race) and 2010 or earlier (relay), and offers a family-friendly atmosphere at a large sports club.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Osttor Stadium
Run along the canal promenade with views of the canal
Course through the Hiltrup residential area, with varied terrain
additional: Individual entries for the half marathon are sold out; only relay places are still available. The course closes at 12:00, after 3 hours of racing. The course is accessible, and detailed information is available for local residents about the route and traffic regulations on race day. Measured course, start at Osttor Stadium, individual and relay races, online registration, start times at 9:00 and 9:05, course closes after 3 hours.

name: Rotherbaum 10K Hamburg - K Rotherbaum
description: The 10K Rotherbaum is an officially measured 10-kilometer race in Hamburg, held in accordance with international competition regulations. The course is a loop registered with the German Athletics Association and AIMS, making finish times eligible for rankings. The event is open to runners of all age groups and offers a cup competition across all 10K Hamburg races, with attractive prizes. Registration is online only, and participants are asked to travel by public transport.
course_highlights: Officially measured 10 km loop course
Start and finish near Hallerstraße U-Bahn station
Finish times eligible for rankings under the IWB and AIMS
additional: A bag drop for personal belongings is available on the event day. The cup competition covers all 10K Hamburg events, with points awarded to the 30 fastest men and women. Official registration confirmation will be sent by email after registration closes. Travel by public transport is recommended, especially to Hallerstraße U-Bahn station. The race is part of the Hamburg 10K Series, which includes various running events in Hamburg. Registration is available online, and various categories are offered.

name: Der Alstertallauf
price_range: Halbmarathon: 40,00 € (Nachmeldungen 45,00 €), 10 km: 30,00 € (35,00 €), 4 km: 20,00 € (25,00 €), Kinder- und Schnupperläufe ab 10,00 €
description: The Alstertallauf is a family-friendly race on the upper Alster hiking trail, considered Hamburg’s most beautiful running route. It welcomes runners of all ages and recreational athletes and offers several distances. The event takes place near the Albert-Schweitzer-Gymnasium in Hamburg and is known for its friendly atmosphere. In 2022, more than 200 runners took part, with distances ranging from 410 m to 10 km.
course_highlights: Race on the upper Alster hiking trail, considered Hamburg’s most beautiful running route
Family-friendly race for all ages and ability levels
Several distances: 410 m, 1,500 m, 4 km and 10 km
additional: The start location is the Albert-Schweitzer-Gymnasium, Wellingsbütteler Landstraße 43, 22337 Hamburg; signs direct participants from U-Klein Borstel. The event includes several distances for different age groups and ability levels. Results and impressions from previous years are available online. The event is organized by Hamburger Turnerbund von 1862 e.V. Race on the Alster hiking trail, registration via www.davengo.com, start/finish at the Albert-Schweitzer-Gymnasium, no parking, public transport recommended, changing rooms and showers available on site.

name: Gettorfer Staffelmarathon
description: The Gettorf Relay Marathon is a team marathon taking place on August 23, 2026, at Sportpark Gettorf. The course is an approximately 4.2 km loop, run ten times. Teams consist of 5 to 10 people, who pass the chipped relay baton in the exchange zone. Alternatively, two people can take part in the Duo Marathon and divide the ten laps between them as they choose. Timing is electronic, using transponders and shoe chips, and split times are recorded for each runner.
course_highlights: Approximately 4.2 km loop at Sportpark Gettorf
Ten laps per team or duo
Electronic timing with a relay-baton transponder and shoe chip
additional: The finish cutoff for both events is 4:45 p.m. Each person may run a maximum of two laps. Team assignments (registrant changes) can be made online until registration closes. Bib numbers are mandatory and provided by the organizer. Online registration is available, with an early-bird discount. Support from local partners such as AOK NordWest, Zippel’s Läuferwelt, Förde Sparkasse, EGE.

name: Bielebohlauf
description: The Bielebohlauf Oppach is a running event in the Lusatian Mountains, offering a range of distances from 400 m to 20 km. The races follow forest, meadow and field paths, as well as minor roads around the Bieleboh. The longer routes are challenging and include steep climbs. Special Bambini and children’s races are available. Refreshments and entertainment are provided at Oppach Stadium, and finishers receive certificates and online clips.
course_highlights: Routes through the landscape of the Lusatian Mountains around the Bieleboh
Forest, meadow and field paths, as well as minor roads
Challenging longer routes with steep climbs
additional: Late registration is available on site for a €5 late registration fee. Dogs are allowed on the walking route; a leash and muzzle are required in the stadium. Trophies and gifts are awarded to route winners in distances of 4.9 km and longer, as well as age-group winners. Age-appropriate gifts are awarded to winners of the 1.5 km route. Results, finisher clips and certificates are available online immediately after the race. Food, drinks and entertainment are provided at the stadium. Routes include climbs; dogs are allowed on the walking route; food and drinks are available.

name: 1. Laufchallenge Mellendorfer TV
description: The 2026 Sparkassen-Laufpass of the Hanover Region features 43 running events, making it the largest series of its kind in Germany. Participants can collect stamps at events across the Hanover Region and discover the area on the run. Each successful participation earns a stamp, and frequent runners can earn attractive rewards in gold, silver or bronze. You can take part directly at the individual races, which take place at many beautiful locations and offer a variety of activities. There is also a Laufpass app with an event calendar and a digital running diary.
course_highlights: A variety of running events at beautiful locations across the Hanover Region
Collect stamps at a total of 43 running events in 2026
Exclusive gold, silver and bronze rewards for frequent runners
additional: The Laufpass is available both as a traditional fold-out booklet and digitally via the Laufpass app. In addition to the event calendar, the app includes a digital running diary. Participation takes place directly at the individual races held throughout the year. Take part in the Laufpass series and collect stamps; available digitally and in traditional format; part of Germany’s largest running series.

name: Die Generalprobe
description: Die Generalprobe is an urban road race in Berlin, serving as the perfect preparation for the BMW BERLIN-MARATHON. On August 23, 2026, runners can test their fitness on a super-flat circuit through the Berlin districts of Steglitz, Wilmersdorf, and Zehlendorf. Events include a quarter marathon, a half marathon, and races for children and teenagers. The event stands out for its lively atmosphere and a personalized medal for every finisher.
course_highlights: Super-flat circuit through the Berlin neighborhoods of Steglitz, Wilmersdorf, and Zehlendorf
Two race distances: quarter marathon (10.5 km) and half marathon (21 km)
The course passes through typical Berlin residential districts with an urban feel
additional: Timing is provided by a MIKA TAG transponder attached to the back of the race bib; it does not need to be returned. The Kids & Youth races start from 08:15, with distances from 200 m to 800 m. Late entries are possible on the day of the event. The start and finish for the main races are on Schlossstraße, Berlin-Steglitz. The participant limit is 4,000. The course passes through the districts of Steglitz, Wilmersdorf, and Zehlendorf; medals for all finishers; results and certificates available to download; age-group winners receive free entry for the following year.

name: IV BIEG PEŁNEJ MISKI
description: Bieg Pełnej Miski is a charity running event held in Szubin to support animal shelters through the “Pełna Miska” campaign. The race has been held annually since 2023, and the next edition is scheduled for August 23, 2026. The event combines sporting competition with the goal of helping homeless animals, bringing together the local community and running enthusiasts. The organizers encourage people to take part and work together to support animals.
course_highlights: 5 km main race
Children’s races and a dog walk
Virtual race, with participants able to take part from anywhere
additional: The event includes the main race, children’s races, a dog walk, and a virtual race option. Fees vary depending on the package and registration date. Proceeds support animal shelters, and participants can receive commemorative medals by post.

name: Biegi wokół Bursztynowej Góry
description: Runs Around Bursztynowa Góra is an annual running event held in picturesque Bąkowo and is part of the Kaszuby Biegają series. The races attract runners from various age categories, offering appealing courses and the unique atmosphere of Kashubia. It is a great opportunity to spend time outdoors amid beautiful natural surroundings and local culture. The organizers ensure professional event management and a welcoming atmosphere for participants.
course_highlights: The course runs around Bursztynowa Góra in Bąkowo
Picturesque landscapes of Kashubia
A course suited to runners in various categories
additional: The event is part of the Kaszuby Biegają series, which includes many races in the Kashubia region. It has a family-friendly, community-building character, with categories for children and young people as well as adults. The organizers provide electronic timing and medals for participants. The event also includes other races and accompanying activities, with opportunities for children and young people to take part. The course most likely passes through rural and natural areas, making for appealing running conditions.

name: XVI Festiwal Biegowy Dziki Weekend
description: The 16th Dziki Weekend Running Festival is an annual sporting event held in Police, West Pomeranian Voivodeship. Organized since 2010 by the DZIK Running Club Association, the festival is one of the region’s best-known running events. It promotes an active lifestyle, cross-country running, and sporting competition for children and young people, while also showcasing the natural attractions of the Wkrzańska Forest. All races start and finish at the sports clearing at 99 Piaskowa Street in Police.
course_highlights: Cross-country routes through the natural landscape of the Wkrzańska Forest
Obstacle races for children and young people (mud, tires, walls, water obstacles, ropes)
Start and finish at the sports clearing at 99 Piaskowa Street in Police
additional: Children’s and youth races take place on 22–23 August 2026. Children’s races on 22.08.2026 start between 10:35 and 11:20, with 5–10 minutes between age-category starts. The obstacle race on 23.08.2026 starts at 10:00, in waves of 10 every 3–5 minutes, divided by sectors and age. The race office is open on 21.08.2026 (14:00–21:30), 22.08.2026 (8:30–11:30), and 23.08.2026 (8:00–11:00). Awards ceremonies take place after the races at 12:30. Children’s race routes are approximately 200 m to 1 km long, while obstacle routes are approximately 600 m to 1 km. The event includes various race categories, online registration, charitable and sporting events, including the Nordic Walking Polish Cup final.

name: B2Run Hamburg
description: B2Run Hamburg on 25 August 2026 is a corporate run covering around 5.6 km, finishing with a spectacular entry into the Volksparkstadion. The varied route is mostly flat, making it ideal for beginners, walkers and experienced runners. The event promotes team spirit, motivation and a sense of community, and is perfect for companies and individual participants from Hamburg and the surrounding area. Alongside the sporting experience, the race offers a professional supporting programme with an MC and music.
course_highlights: A varied, mostly flat loop of around 5.6 km
Spectacular finish in the Volksparkstadion
Route suitable for beginners, walkers and experienced runners
additional: The event is a large team occasion, with plenty of opportunities for team building and networking. There is a professional supporting programme with an MC and music. Individual participants without a team are very welcome. The route is designed so teams can cross the finish line together. 5 km route, finish in the Volksparkstadion, team event, supporting programme with music, support for the “Menschen für Menschen” foundation

name: Blodomloppet Västerås
description: Welcome to Blodomloppet in Västerås at Rocklunda IP on 26 August 2026—a fun run for everyone, where you can walk, jog or run 5 km or 10 km. Lilla Blodomloppet offers two children’s races (approx. 1,400 m and approx. 500 m), with a warm-up and the finish under the finish arch. The event is held to raise awareness of the need for blood donation and traditionally ends with a picnic for teams and participants. You can register individually or as part of a team (3–5 people); information and event details are available on the event website.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the Rocklunda area (the football pitches north of the riding arena)
The 5 km and 10 km courses are marked, with course marshals positioned along the routes
Lilla Blodomloppet: two children’s distances (~1,400 m, starting at 17:15, and ~500 m, starting at 17:25), finishing under the finish arch
additional: You can register individually or as part of a team (3–5 participants; the fee is always for 5 participants and includes a picnic for 5). Teams can be topped up to a maximum of 5 people until Monday 24/8, and the final date for team registration is stated as 19/8; larger companies can arrange a customer page/discount code. Children taking part in Lilla Blodomloppet receive a medal and a finish-line bag from ICA Maxi Hälla. The warm-up is in front of the stage at approximately 17:00, and children choose their distance on site. Registration is binding, cancellations are not accepted, and registration is open until 26/8 at 17:30. Course and map materials are available on the event website (link to map/course map). Register via the website or on site at Rocklunda IP from 15:00; 25 August according to the information page; includes a technical T-shirt, race bib and medal. Team registration is available for 3–5 participants, with the regular registration deadline on 20 August. The course route and start times will be announced by the organisers.

name: Norrköpings Stadslopp (Nkpg City)
description: NKPG City Norrköpings Stadslopp is organized by Tjalve Friidrott Norrköping and starts and finishes on Olai Kyrkogata in the heart of Norrköping. The event offers 5 km and 10 km distances (10 km is 2 x 5 km), as well as the free children’s race, Lilla Lundbergsloppet. The course passes through classic Norrköping settings, with large crowds lining the route, several music stations, and a mix of elite runners and recreational runners. Finishers receive medals and sponsored products. Team registration is available, and runners can choose timed or untimed participation.
course_highlights: A city course through classic Norrköping settings, with large crowds lining the route
More than ten music stations along the course to keep runners motivated
10 km = 2 x 5 km; start and finish on Olai Kyrkogata
additional: Start and finish on Olai Kyrkogata by Hötorget. Start times: Lilla Lundbergsloppet from 17:00 (four starts 15 minutes apart), 10 km at 18:30, 5 km at 19:30. Timed or untimed participation is available for the 5 km and 10 km. Lilla Lundbergsloppet (approx. 1,000 m) is free and limited to a maximum of 1,100 children; all children receive a medal and a goodie bag. Bib pickup: XXL Ingelsta on Tuesday 26 August, 11:00–18:00, and in the partner village at the start and finish area on Wednesday 27 August from 15:00 (late registration for the 5 km and 10 km is possible at both bib pickup locations). Start lists and information about your bib number will be published from the afternoon of Monday 25 August. Distance options: 5 km and 10 km; Lilla Lundbergsloppet is a free 1 km race for children; start and finish on Olai Kyrkogata; the course passes Linden shopping centre and features music stations along the way; Lilla Lundbergsloppet is limited to 1,100 children; all participants receive a medal and a goodie bag; the official results page is available online.

name: GKN-stafetten 2026 (del av Trollhättan Action Week)
description: The GKN Relay is a team relay held as part of Trollhättan Action Week on Thursday, 27 August 2026. Each team consists of four participants, with each runner covering approximately 3 km on a flat course around the Trollhättan Canal. The event celebrates community and team spirit, welcoming both fast teams and those who prefer to jog or walk. After the finish, entertainment is offered on site, with live music and a picnic atmosphere.
course_highlights: Flat course along the Trollhättan Canal
Relay format: 4 x ~3 km (each participant runs approximately 3 km)
Start/finish at Hansenplatsen in Trollhättan
additional: Registration is via RaceID, where the team contact person creates the entry and provides the team name and the leg each team member will run; teams consist of 4 participants. The event encourages running, jogging or walking and offers entertainment after the finish (live music and a picnic basket). NearYou has a staffing pool on site at Hansenplatsen to help provide replacement runners in case of late withdrawals. Location: Hansenplatsen, Trollhättan; race format: 4 x 3 km relay. Teams require 4 people, each participant runs 3 km, for a total of 12 km; start time TBA; registration requires a team leader, booking code and personal details; payment via the Söderberg & Partner portal; other fees are covered by VIF-Tt.

name: 7. Ahnepark-Lauf der Laufgemeinschaft Vellmar
description: The 7th Ahnepark Run, organized by Laufgemeinschaft Vellmar, is a late-summer running event in Vellmar. This club race offers two distances, 200 meters and 17.3 kilometers, and is designed primarily as a community run. Registration and results are managed through my.raceresult.com. The race is listed in the laufen.de running calendar and features officially measured courses that are relevant for rankings.
course_highlights: Two distances: 200 m and 17.3 km
Event in Ahnepark in Vellmar
Officially measured courses for rankings
additional: Registration and results are handled through my.raceresult.com. The race takes place in typical August weather, with temperatures around 25 °C and mostly sunny days. It is a local club race without major branding or destination elements. Distances: 200 m, 17.3 km; registration and results through my.raceresult.com; listed in the laufen.de running calendar

name: Lemgoer Hanselauf

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Anmeldung am Veranstaltungstag ab 16 Uhr möglich

description: The Lemgo Hanselauf is a traditional running event held annually on the last or second-to-last Friday in August in Lemgo. The event offers 3.3 km, 6.6 km and 10 km courses along the city’s ramparts. Children and Bambinis can also take part over shorter distances, making the Hanselauf a family-friendly event. With around 1,000 participants, the Hanselauf is a sporting highlight in the region that brings together fun and community.
course_highlights: Course along Lemgo’s historic ramparts
Distances of 3.3 km, 6.6 km and 10 km
Children’s and Bambini runs over 1.5 km and 400 m
additional: Bib collection and late registration on the event day from 4 p.m. in the right-hand school wing of Engelbert-Kämpfer-Gymnasium. No timing or placings for the children’s and Bambini runs. Assemble at the start from 4:55 p.m. Participation is free. Run along the ramparts, children’s and Bambini runs, registration at Engelbert-Kämpfer-Gymnasium, late registration available on the event day.

name: Ibbenbürener Aaseelauf 2026
description: The Ibbenbüren Aasee Run is a long-standing running event taking place for the 41st time in 2026. The event offers races for children of kindergarten and primary-school age, as well as a 5 km fun run, a 5 km team run, and a 10 km main race for competitive and recreational runners. The course runs around Lake Aasee, with the start and finish at Stadion Ost in Ibbenbüren. The event is limited to 1,000 participants and is known for its family-friendly atmosphere and good on-course support.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Stadion Ost, Ibbenbüren
Loop course around Lake Aasee, with three laps in the 10 km main race
Drinks stations along the course and in the finish area
additional: Late registration is available on event day from 15:00 until 1 hour before the start of each race for a fee of €2.50. Changes to entries are also possible on event day for a fee. €1 per registration is donated to a charitable organization. Free parking is available at Stadion Ost. Race bibs can be collected on event day from 15:00. Timing is recorded using transponders on the back of the race bib. Registration is online only, with a limited number of places. Late registration costs €2.50; charitable projects can be supported.

name: Sparkassen-Abendlauf
location: Hohenhorster Wald, Recklinghausen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The Sparkassen Evening Run in Recklinghausen is a summer running event organized by Recklinghäuser Leichtathletik Club in cooperation with Sparkasse Vest Recklinghausen. Two distances are offered: 5 km (two laps) and 10 km (four laps) through Hohenhorster Forest. Both courses are officially measured and eligible for inclusion in rankings. The evening run also hosts the district championships over 10 km, for which a valid competition licence in the FLVW district of Recklinghausen is required.
course_highlights: 5 km and 10 km courses in Hohenhorster Forest
Officially measured courses eligible for inclusion in rankings
10 km district championships held as part of the evening run
additional: The 5 km course consists of two laps, and the 10 km course consists of four laps through Hohenhorster Forest. Participants in the 10 km district championships must tick the corresponding box when registering and hold a valid competition licence. Courses in Hohenhorster Forest, district championships held as part of the event

name: Straßenlauf Rund um den Holtenauer Leuchtturm
5. LSG-Waldauer-Wiesen-Lauf
location: Sportplatz Waldauer Wiesen, Kassel, Hesse, Germany
description: The 5th LSG-Waldauer-Wiesen-Lauf is an evening running event held at the Waldauer Wiesen sports ground in Kassel. The event offers various distances for all age groups, from a 500 m Bambini run to an 18 km run. The shorter children’s races start first, followed by the longer races in the early evening. The courses are well marked and run around the Bugasee and along the Wahlebach, among other places, with refreshment stations and childcare available on site.
course_highlights: 5 km out-and-back course
9.5 km loop around the Bugasee with a Wahlebach section
18 km course consists of two laps of the 9.5 km course
additional: Marked courses, two refreshment stations, catering and childcare are available. Online registration is possible via the event portal. Walking is no longer a separate category, but participants can walk the 5 km or 9.5 km courses. The running courses go around the Bugasee; registration is online via Raceresult. Parking is limited, so travel by public transport is recommended. The event also offers childcare and refreshments on site.

name: Leunaer Saaleanlagenlauf
description: The Leuna Saaleanlagen Run takes place on 21 August 2026 in Leuna and offers various race distances from 1.4 km to 9.6 km. The event is aimed especially at children and school students, creating a family-friendly atmosphere. The race runs through the Saaleanlagen and promises pleasant running weather, with mostly sunny conditions in August. Participants can look forward to a sporting challenge in beautiful surroundings.
course_highlights: Runs through the Saaleanlagen in Leuna
Distances from 1.4 km to 9.6 km
Family-friendly event focused on children and school students
additional: Typical August weather: approx. 25 °C, low of 14 °C, average precipitation of 60 mm, mostly sunny. The event takes place in August, with typical temperatures around 25°C. It offers a family-friendly atmosphere with various race categories.

name: Sparkassen-Tauchscher-Stadtlauf
description: The Sparkassen-Tauchscher City Run is a traditional running event organized by Leichtathletik Club Taucha e. V. in the town of Taucha on the Parthe. The 21st edition of this city run will take place on August 28, 2026, and also incorporates the State Championships in the 10 km road race. The event offers runners of all age groups an attractive opportunity to compete in a lively atmosphere. Registration opens in February 2026.
course_highlights: Integrated State Championships in the 10 km road race
City run through Taucha, the town on the Parthe
Traditional running event organized by Leichtathletik Club Taucha e. V.
additional: Registration opens in February 2026; the event also includes special categories and town festival elements.

name: Jönköping Marathon & Half Marathon
description: Jönköping Marathon & Half Marathon is a welcoming city race taking place on 29 August 2026, with beautiful views along Lake Vättern and through Jönköping and Huskvarna. The course has been redesigned to reduce the total elevation gain while retaining a varied profile with sections through nature, crowd support and several power zones; the marathon course finishes with a spectacular finish line right in the middle of Munksjö Bridge. The race attracts international participants and also features shorter races and a MINI children’s race, as well as offers for businesses and tent packages in the start/finish area.
course_highlights: Spectacular finish line right in the middle of Munksjö Bridge
Beautiful views along Lake Vättern and through Jönköping and Huskvarna, on a redesigned course with less elevation gain
Marathon: 42,195 m with 12 aid stations along the course plus 1 in the start/finish area, an interactive map and power zones
additional: Practical information from the website: up to five runners can be registered at a time; race bibs are not sent out. The marathon course has an interactive map and a downloadable PDF, power zones, and 12+1 aid stations. The organizer offers tent packages for businesses in the start/finish area and the option to use a wellness allowance. Distances: 21K (21,097.5 m) and 42K (42,195 m); includes a team relay and MINI Jönköping Marathon for children. Energy and aid stations along the course, chip timing, group registration for up to 5 runners, and a business village with tents in the start/finish area.

name: Trelleborgsloppet

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Klass 1-4, löpning 5 och 10 km : 195 kr vid föranmälan , 270 kr vid efteranmälan (efter 25/8)

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Klass 5, gång 5 km : 125 kr vid föranmälan 175 kr vid efteranmälan (efter 25/8)

description: Trelleborgsloppet is a classic city race in Sweden’s southernmost town, featuring certified, officially measured courses. The event offers 10 km and 5 km races for runners, as well as a 5 km walk/power walk, with the start at Östervångsstadion and the finish in Stadsparken. The race uses gun time with single-use chips and welcomes competitive runners, corporate teams and recreational runners. Everyone who finishes receives a medal, and there is a team competition for companies, associations and groups of friends.
course_highlights: Start at Östervångsstadion, finish in Stadsparken
Officially measured, certified city course (gun time)
Distances: 10 km and 5 km (plus a 5 km walk/power walk), with separate bib-number series for each category
additional: Timing with single-use chips (Neptron), gun time. Bibs must be collected no later than 45 minutes before the start at Östervångsstadion or in the foyer of Söderslättshallen on 28/8 from 17:00 to 19:00. Changing facilities are available at Söderslättshallen; clothing is transported to the finish in a vehicle (departing once, typically at 10:10). Late registration is available online until 45 minutes before the start and in person up to 1 hour before each start. Teams entering the “Fastest in Town” competition for companies/organisations/groups of friends can register online free of charge. The race is a city course in Trelleborg on gravel paths and pavements. Late online registration is available for an increased fee. Bib collection takes place at Söderslättshallen; timing uses single-use chips (Neptron), and results are published at trelleborgsloppet.se.

name: Festivalloppet
description: Festivalloppet is SK Graal’s annual running race in Strömsnäsbruk, following sections of the Lagan River. The race offers 10 km and 4.8 km distances, as well as children’s and youth categories, and passes through beautiful surroundings along the river. It has a friendly local atmosphere, with the club, spectators and volunteers helping to make it a great experience. Results, start lists and information are published on SK Graal’s website. The 2025 edition had 173 registered runners and 167 finishers.
course_highlights: Along the Lagan River in Strömsnäsbruk
10 km and 4.8 km distances
Children’s and youth categories, with a friendly local atmosphere
additional: Registration and information are available via links on SK Graal’s website, where results, start lists and photos are also published. The 2025 edition took place on 30 August 2025 in Strömsnäsbruk; 173 runners registered and 167 finished, with weather contributing to a higher number of late registrations. The website also links to an information sheet (PM Festivalloppet).

name: Midnattsloppet (Malmö)
description: Midnattsloppet Malmö is an evening celebration taking place on 29 August 2026. Choose between 10 km (first start at 21:00) and 5 km (first start at 22:00), starting and finishing at Stortorget. The race features late start times, music and activities along the course, and is suitable for competitive runners, teams and corporate groups. The event focuses on the atmosphere, spectators and experience rather than just performance results.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Stortorget in central Malmö
Urban asphalt course through Malmö, with music and activities along the route
Evening/night start with a festival atmosphere (10 km at 21:00, 5 km at 22:00)
additional: Practical information: the start and warm-up area are at Stortoget. The entry fee includes, among other things, an official Björn Borg T-shirt (the 5 km page mentions a shirt), chip timing, energy drink along the course, a bar/fruit at the finish and a digital diploma. A medal can be purchased when registering. Fitness benefit providers: Benifex, Epassi and Benefits (registration using a fitness benefit allowance is possible). Team registration and a corporate competition are available; there is also a costume category for 5/10 km. Course closure/cut-off: in Malmö, the course closes at 6.6 km at 22:26 (runners passing after that are redirected and their timing chip may be removed). Distances: 5 km and 10 km; start and finish at Stortorget; 10 km course around Malmö; start times: 21:00 for 10 km and 22:00 for 5 km; team and corporate categories; Costume theme; race pack includes a T-shirt (Björn Borg), chip timing, energy drink and fruit, and a digital diploma; medal available for purchase; fitness benefit allowance via Benifex, Epassi and Benefits; team registration offers a discount.

name: Rynningeviken Längre 2026

tiers.label: tier_1

description: Rynningeviken Longer is a timed race in the Rynningeviken Nature Reserve outside Örebro, where participants run as far as they can in either three or six hours. The course follows scenic trails along Lake Hjälmaren and the Svartån River. It is relatively technical but fast, and just a stone’s throw from the city centre. The race is open to all running styles and abilities—from walking to ultrarunning—and offers a community-focused day with support and aid stations. A separate KidsRun for the youngest participants is also part of the event.
course_highlights: 2,412.5-metre loop, mostly gravel paths
Two bridges account for the few metres of elevation; start/finish on cobblestones
Final 508-metre loop for the closing measurement, reducing wait time at the finish
additional: Start times and mandatory briefings: 6-hour race starts at 11:00 (briefing at 10:45); 3-hour race starts at 14:00 (briefing at 13:45); KidsRun starts at 11:30 (briefing at 11:15). Location: Gamla Oljehamnen, below Naturens hus; parking along Oljevägen. Timing uses a transponder borrowed at bib collection (a lost transponder incurs a charge of SEK 800); the final measurement is verified with a measuring wheel. There is no individual timekeeping—the result is the distance covered when time expires. Umara sports drink and water are provided, along with a well-stocked energy table (bars, fruit, crisps, pickled cucumber, Tosca cake and more). No changing rooms or showers are available. Public toilets are located at the start and about 1 km along the course. Registration is only through the partner AnmälMigNu (group and corporate registration via info@epictrail.se). Young people (born in 2008 or later) receive a 50% discount. KidsRun participants receive a medal, Festis and ice cream. The course loop is approximately 2,412.5 m, with two bridges and a final 508 m loop. Energy and fluids are provided (Umara). No changing rooms or showers are offered; toilets are near the start and about 1 km along the course. Registration window: 24–29 August. The 50% youth discount applies to those born in 2008 or later. Registration includes a place, bib, timing, a unique medal, sports drink and energy along the course. Register via AnmälMigNu; group/corporate registration via info@epictrail.se. Cancellation and insurance options are available; participation is at your own risk.

name: Midnattsloppet
description: Midnattsloppet Malmö is a festive, high-energy running experience taking place on 29 August 2026. Choose between running 5 km or 10 km in the heart of the city, with the start and finish at Stortorget. The race is known for its late start time, carnival atmosphere and the unique sense of community among runners, spectators and event staff. Midnattsloppet is more than a race—it’s a people’s festival and a memory for life.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Stortorget in Malmö
5 km and 10 km road races through the city streets
A high-energy festival with music and spectator support along the course
additional: Start times: 10 km starts at 21:00, and 5 km starts at 22:00. Start and finish at Stortorget. The entry fee includes a Björn Borg T-shirt, precise timekeeping, energy drinks along the course, a bar/fruit after the finish and a digital certificate. Registration through wellness benefit providers (Benifex, Epassi, Benefits) is available. Team and corporate competitions are offered. The time limit for the 10 km is 90 minutes, with a cutoff at 6.6 km at 22:26. The race starts at 22:00 at Stortorget in Malmö and includes a race kit, T-shirt, digital certificate, medal (available for purchase) and energy products and fruit along the course.

name: 32. Zeitzer Stadtlauf
description: The Zeitz City Run takes place in Moritzburg Castle Park in Zeitz and is organized by SG Chemie Zeitz. The event begins at 9:15 a.m., with the main races starting at 10:00 a.m. The race office is located in front of the main stage in the city park, and changing and shower facilities are available at the Klinkerhallen on Albrechtstraße. The park entrance is on Stephanstraße. The run is a great opportunity to get active and enjoy the atmosphere in the castle park.
course_highlights: Run through the historic Moritzburg Castle Park in Zeitz
Main races start at 10:00 a.m.
Changing and shower facilities at the nearby Klinkerhallen
additional: The race office is located in front of the main stage in the city park. Changing and shower facilities are available at the Klinkerhallen, Albrechtstraße. The park entrance is on Stephanstraße. The run starts at 10:00 a.m., with changing and shower facilities at the Klinkerhallen. The park entrance is on Stephanstraße. August weather is usually sunny, ideal for an outdoor run.

name: 37. Heideblütenlauf
description: The 37th Heideblütenlauf takes place on Saturday, August 29, 2026, in Schneverdingen. This traditional running event is held as part of the Heideblütenfest. Organized by TV Jahn Schneverdingen, it offers runners of all ages the chance to experience the beautiful heathland. The course passes through the picturesque surroundings, with numerous volunteers and supporters helping ensure that everything runs smoothly. Participants can look forward to a friendly, well-organized event.
course_highlights: Running routes through the heathland around Schneverdingen
Start in front of the town hall on Schulstraße
Event held as part of the Heideblütenfest
additional: The event is supported by numerous local partners and volunteers, including the City of Schneverdingen, the German Red Cross, Johanniter, the Volunteer Fire Brigade, and the Heide Queen. Certificates can be printed for all participants, including Bambini children. Registration is handled by TV Jahn Schneverdingen; further details are available on the website. Online registration opens on 01.04.2026. Start and finish are on Schulstraße in front of the town hall. Results and certificates are available online.

name: 39. Jever-Fun-Lauf
price_range: 4,00 € bis 36,00 € je nach Lauf und Anmeldung
description: The 39th Jever-Fun-Lauf on 29 August 2026 is a traditional running event in Jever that brings together people of all ages and ability levels. The route passes through the town centre and by well-known landmarks, with cheering spectators lining the course. The focus is on the enjoyment of exercise and community, not competition. There are various races for children, young people and adults, including walking, company and team categories, as well as a main race over 10 English miles.
course_highlights: A 2.864 km loop through Jever town centre
The route passes by well-known landmarks
Cheering spectators line the course
additional: The official technical T-shirt can be ordered until 07 June 2026 for 20.00 euros, and thereafter for 25.00 euros (while stocks last). Merchandise such as sports socks, caps and multifunctional scarves is also available and can be collected in Jever on Wednesdays. Late registrations are possible on the event day until one hour before the respective start. The time limit for the main race (10 English miles) is 150 minutes. Several race categories, registration deadlines, start times and further event details are available on the official website. The event takes place on 29 August 2026.

name: Edersee-Lauf
distance_verbose: Halbmarathon, 10 km, 5 km, 2 km, 1.2 km, 1 km, 0.5 km
description: The Edersee Run is part of the Waldeck-Frankenberg Running Cup and takes place on August 29, 2026, in Vöhl-Herzhausen on Lake Eder. The run is organized by SV 1921 Herzhausen, a club that promotes sport and community for all age groups. The event is very popular and offers runners an appealing opportunity to get active and enjoy the beautiful surroundings of Lake Eder. Pre-registration opens soon, and the club extends its heartfelt thanks to its supporters and sponsors.
course_highlights: A variety of running distances for all age groups
Flat, fast courses on Lake Eder
Family and children's races included
additional: The run is part of the Waldeck-Frankenberg Running Cup. The event is organized by SV 1921 Herzhausen, which also offers other sports activities and training groups. Race bibs are supported by sponsors. Pre-registration for 2026 opens soon. Various running distances, family-friendly, event held as part of the Waldeck-Frankenberg Running Cup, start and finish at the Herzhausen barbecue hut.

name: Mindener Volkslauf
description: The Mindener Volkslauf is SV 1860 Minden’s largest running event, with more than 1,000 participants every year. The 50th anniversary run takes place on 29 August 2026, featuring many new highlights along the course and in the stadium. At the same time, the club is celebrating the 10th anniversary of the merger that formed SV Minden, with numerous activities. The event offers a great atmosphere and an after-run party following the company run, inviting everyone to join in the celebrations.
course_highlights: A course featuring new highlights and varied sections
Start and finish in the stadium, with a special atmosphere
After-run party following the company run
additional: The 50th Mindener Volkslauf features an after-run party following the company run. Registration is expected to open in May 2026. In 2025, 1,467 participants crossed the finish line. The event also celebrates the 10th anniversary of the merger that formed SV Minden, with many individual activities through the end of the year. The event takes place in August, with registration opening in May 2026. It is the club’s largest event, with a special focus on community and anniversary celebrations.

name: Monte Sophia XXII und 65. HAG-Lauf
description: The Monte Sophia Mountain Run and the Heinrich-Antons Memorial Run (HAGL) are traditional cross-country races in the Rhenish lignite-mining region near Niederzier. The 25 km Monte Sophia Run, with 380 metres of elevation gain, takes runners across the Sophienhöhe, a former spoil heap with varied trails, distinctive natural and cultural landmarks, and beautiful views. The HAGL offers a shorter 10 km alternative, while the 5.3 km Broisterd Loop is also suitable for beginners. The event also includes children’s races and a 10 km walking route, making it ideal for cross-country runners and marathon trainees.
course_highlights: 25 km route with 380 metres of elevation gain across the Sophienhöhe
Distinctive landmarks including the Stone Compass, Celtic Tree Circle, Golden Meadow and Roman Tower
Varied gradients, from gentle to steep, on firm gravel paths and asphalt
additional: Changing rooms and showers are available in the gymnasium. Aid stations with water, tea, fruit and cola are located along the course and at the finish. Children receive medals and certificates; the top three in each age group receive prizes. Runners entering two races receive a separate bib for each race. Bicycle escorts, jogging strollers, dogs and headphones are prohibited. A challenging cross-country event in the Rhenish lignite-mining region, with a range of race distances, including children’s races and walking.

name: Bottroper Ultralauf Festival (BUF)
description: The Bottrop Ultrarunning Festival 2026 takes place on August 30 and 31 in Batenbrock Park in Bottrop, offering an unforgettable running experience for ultrarunning fans. Alongside the established 6- and 24-hour races, the Halden Backyard is once again a special highlight. The festival stands out for its great community, compelling challenges and unique festival atmosphere, shaped by hourly restarts and parallel competitions.
course_highlights: 6- and 24-hour races in Batenbrock Park
Halden Backyard as a special highlight
Hourly restarts and parallel competitions
additional: The festival features hourly restarts, a parallel competition and a walking event taking place at the same time, creating a unique festival atmosphere. Running event with 6-hour, 24-hour, relay and Backyard events; in Batenbrock Park; online registration; event in August 2026

name: 8. Stolberger Schloss-Lauf
location: Schloss Stolberg, Stolberg im Harz, Saxony-Anhalt, Germany
description: The Stolberger Schloss-Lauf 2026 is a charity run in the southern Harz region, starting and finishing right at the historic Stolberg Castle. The event offers various races for runners of all abilities, including a half marathon, relay, 10 km, 5 km, walking, and fun runs and children’s races. The varied routes pass through the historic old town, along forest paths and over the hills of the southern Harz, combining a sporting challenge with scenic and cultural highlights. By taking part, every runner supports regional projects in and around Stolberg, giving the event a special charitable character.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Stolberg Castle, with its historic setting
Varied routes through the old town, along forest paths and over the hills of the southern Harz
A special finish-line experience at the castle
additional: Alongside the main races, the event includes walking, fun runs, and children’s races. Participation supports regional projects in and around Stolberg. Accommodation is offered by Ritter von Kempski Private Hotels & Resorts directly in and around Stolberg. Some sections of the routes follow unpaved, natural forest paths and carry a corresponding risk of accidents. Multiple distances, children’s races, relay race, support for regional projects, accommodation nearby

name: SUNSET Wattenmeer
description: The Altra Sunset Wattenmeer is an extraordinary relay race covering approximately 250 kilometers from Hamburg-St. Pauli to St. Peter-Ording. The route passes through the Wadden Sea National Park UNESCO World Heritage Site and offers breathtaking natural scenery, idyllic towns, and marshland with a sea breeze. The event lasts more than 24 hours and challenges teams of 5 or 10 runners to complete the course together. Start times are assigned according to the average pace submitted, and digital maps are provided before the race.
course_highlights: Around 250 km through the Wadden Sea National Park UNESCO World Heritage Site
Start in Hamburg St. Pauli, finish on the beach in St. Peter-Ording
Diverse nature reserves, marshland, and a sea breeze
additional: Participants must be born in 2010 or earlier (Ultra teams: 2008 or earlier). Team sizes: 10-person teams (3 legs per runner) or Ultra 5-person teams (6 legs per runner). 5 Pack teams are paired with a similar 5 Pack team. Team categories are assigned automatically when members are entered (men, women, diverse, mixed). 10-person teams must arrange 2 vans as team vehicles; 5-person teams must arrange 1 van. Start times are assigned according to the average pace submitted. The event lasts more than 24 hours. Digital maps are provided before the event. Team relay race with various categories, participation for those born in 2008 or earlier, detailed information on registration, costs, and the event schedule, including navigation using maps.

name: Birklauf
description: The Birklauf hosted by MTV Gelting 08 is a traditional running event taking place on 29 August 2026 from 15:45 at Birkhalle Gelting. The event celebrates sport, fun and nature, and gives runners of various age groups the opportunity to compete. Timing is provided on all distances except the 750-metre Sprottenlauf, and all finishers receive a medal. Results are ranked by age group, and honorary prizes are awarded to the top three runners.
course_highlights: Timing on all distances except the 750 m Sprottenlauf
Results ranked by age group
Medal for all finishers
additional: Entries are accepted until 22 August 2026. The event is hosted by MTV Gelting 1908 e.V. All finishers receive a medal, and honorary prizes are awarded to the first three places. The 750 m Sprottenlauf is untimed. Courses through the Geltinger Birk nature reserve and Nordschauwald; registration until 22 August 2026; race materials available from 15:00; refreshments include fruit and drinks.

name: Elstertal-Lauf
description: The Elstertal Run, organized by 1. SV Gera, is a long-standing running event with a range of distances for runners of all ages. On August 29, 2026, individual races over 10 km and 15 km, as well as relay races for companies and school students, will take place. There are also children’s races and a challenging stair run with about 1,300 steps. The event is part of the Thuringian and Gera Running Cup series and offers a varied route through the region.
course_highlights: 15 km individual race for men, women and youth
Company and school relays over 5 x 3 km, with a flexible number of runners
2,500 m stair run with approx. 1,300 steps
additional: Children’s races as part of the Osterland Cross (600 m, 800 m, 1,000 m / 3 km). Relay teams may have 2 to 5 runners; with 4 runners, one runner covers 6 km. The individual races are part of the Thuringian and Gera Running Cup series. Several race formats, including a stair run; training plans and detailed information available.

name: Karlis Härtetest
description: Karlis Härtetest is a traditional race organized by the Pretzsch running team. Held annually in autumn near Leipzig, it features a challenging cross-country course that tests runners of all ages. The club SG Grün-Weiß 90 Pretzsch e.V. has a long history in running and uses this event to foster community and sporting ambition. The event is known for its special atmosphere and the chance to take on a varied course.
course_highlights: Challenging cross-country course at the canoe center near Leipzig
A variety of challenges for runners of all ages
Traditional event with strong ties to the club
additional: The event is organized by SG Grün-Weiß 90 Pretzsch e.V., which also organizes other running events and challenges. The pages reviewed do not provide explicit details about start times, pricing tiers, or registration procedures. The race takes place on 29 August 2026 and is known for its challenging course and friendly atmosphere. It is suitable for both recreational runners and competitive athletes.

name: Lauf rund um Tiefwarensee
description: The 20th Run around Tiefwarensee in Waren (Müritz) is a traditional running event taking place on 29 August 2026. Organised by Müritzer LSV, the course loops around the picturesque Tiefwarensee and offers runners an attractive and varied setting. The event welcomes runners of all ability levels and is a regular fixture on the regional running calendar.
course_highlights: Loop around Tiefwarensee
Start and finish at the sports field at Tiefwarensee, Güstrower Straße
Scenic route in Waren (Müritz)
additional: Registration address: Peter Hoffmann, Am Pappelgrund 10; Event number: 26V08000010060000; Category: event away from a stadium (6.5.1). Registration closes on 27 August 2026. The event is part of a regional running and nature experience programme highlighting the beauty of Tiefwarensee and the surrounding nature.

name: Panorama - Run - Bad Laasphe
location: Wabachstadion, Bad Laasphe, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The Panorama Run in Bad Laasphe is a varied race held as part of the SummerCityGames and organised by TV Laasphe. The course starts at Wabachstadion and follows paved paths and forest trails to its highest point, with a challenging climb and a second half that is mostly downhill and offers a lovely view. There is a 6 km youth/everyone’s race and a 12 km main race, which covers the course twice and is a real challenge. Changing rooms and showers are also available directly at the sports ground.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Wabachstadion Bad Laasphe
Paved paths and forest trails, with a tough climb to the highest point
The second half of the course is mostly downhill and offers a lovely view
additional: Late entries are possible 60 minutes before the start of the competition, subject to a €3 late-entry fee. Race numbers can be collected at the clubhouse on the sports ground. Changing rooms and showers are available at the sports ground. Course description: 6 km and 12 km races, uphill and downhill, on paved paths and forest trails; registration until 28.08.2025; late entry 60 minutes before the start for a fee; start/finish at the Bad Laasphe sports ground; changing rooms/showers available

name: Salzbergener Raffinerielauf
description: The Salzbergen Refinery Run is a popular road race in the beautiful municipality of Salzbergen, taking place on August 29, 2026. Various distances are offered for all age groups, including a children’s fun run, a school mile, a 5 km community race, and a 10 km main race. The event is part of the EL-CUP and, alongside exciting competitions, offers a varied program for runners and spectators. The races start at Oberschule Salzbergen and encourage both individual and team competition.

Team competition in the main races
additional: Start times: 14:30 first race; 14:45 school mile; 15:15 5 km community race; 16:15 10 km main race; 16:20 5 km walking/Nordic walking (no timing). Team competition for timed races; teams consist of 3 participants. Late registration is possible up to 45 minutes before the respective race, with a €1.00 late registration fee. Race materials are available from approximately 13:15 at the on-site race office. Races with team competition, online registration, supporting program, trophies and medals.

name: 4. S-RUN Sparkassenlauf "Rund um das Dünkreuz"
description: The 4th S-RUN Sparkassenlauf “Rund um das Dünkreuz” is a nature-focused popular race in the Eichsfeld, welcoming runners of all ages and fitness levels. The varied courses wind through the breathtaking natural landscape around the Dünkreuz and offer exciting challenges for both experienced runners and beginners. Alongside the sporting competition, community spirit takes centre stage, supported by an attractive programme at the sports ground. The race is part of the Eichsfeld Cup and is organised by SG Birkungen 07.

Part of the renowned Eichsfeld Cup
additional: There are 4 courses and 5 events: Bambini-Run (400 m), Youngster-Run (1.5 km), 6-K-Run (6 km run/Nordic walking) and 10-K-Run (10 km run). The event fosters community spirit and offers a programme at the sports ground. Results from previous years are available at my.raceresult.com. Forest trails, fields, elevation gain, Nordic walking, course signage, medical support, transponder timing, community programme

name: Mały Wielki Bieg

description: Mały Wielki Bieg is the largest race in the Pruszcz Gdański municipality. After a year’s break, it returns to Straszyn. It takes place on 29 August 2026 and is an important sporting event in the region.

Activities and fitness challenges for participants

name: NorDan RUN

description: NorDan RUN is a race held in picturesque Wolsztyn, with routes along paths in the town park beside Lake Wolsztyn. Participants can choose from several distances, from shorter races for children to challenging 48 km routes with checkpoint and refreshment stations. The start and finish are located at the “Fala Park” venue, providing comfortable event facilities and beautiful views. The race is a great opportunity to spend time outdoors and enjoy the natural surroundings.
course_highlights: Routes follow paths in Wolsztyn town park
Views of Lake Wolsztyn and the UMKS ZRYW kayak marina
Checkpoint and refreshment stations on the 10 km, 24 km and 48 km routes

Children’s races cover shorter distances from 300 m to 900 m, with different start times between 13:00 and 14:30. The event takes place in Wolsztyn, with online registration, an annual edition and a range of distance options.

name: VIII Dycha nad Wisłą
description: The VIII Dycha nad Wisłą is an annual road race held in Tczew and is part of the IX Kociewie Running Grand Prix. The event attracts runners from various regions and offers a scenic route along the Vistula. It has a sporting and recreational character, promoting physical activity and community integration.
