name: Krystallmarsjen
description: The Crystal March is a collaboration with Magnor Glassworks and was first held in 1982. name: Wings For Life Run
description: Wings for Life World Run is a unique race where participants run to support research on spinal cord injuries. The race does not have a fixed distance; instead, participants run as far as they can before being caught by a "Catcher Car." This creates an exciting and dynamic experience, as all participants start at the same time, but the goal is to run as far as possible before the car catches up with them. 100% of the entry fee goes directly to the Wings for Life Foundation to fund research.

The race brings together thousands of participants from around the world who compete simultaneously.

On Tuesday, May 13, 2025, the race will take place for the 43rd time, where runners can choose between distances of 6 or 12 km. The 12 km street race follows the classic route around Kanada, while the 6 km race follows the main course to the Kyllerud roundabout before returning to Syllinghallen.

The race has been a part of the running community for over 30 years and attracts both experienced runners and beginners.

Participants will experience varied terrain with both trails and gravel roads, offering an authentic nature experience.

The Ekeberg Run is a perfect chance to push your limits and enjoy the beautiful nature at Ekebergsletta.

Younger runners than 11 years can participate but will be counted as 11 years in the relay. All legs can be viewed from the spectator area northwest of the town hall, and the race has its start and finish at Hovsbakken, right behind the town hall.

description: On Saturday, June 17, the uphill race From Fjord to Hell is back in Hov. Runners pass through Hov center on their way up, and there are great opportunities to follow the runners from the spectator area. The race starts at 12:00 PM, and it is possible to register for both the timed running category and the non-timed recreational class.

name: Eikenosa Opp
description: Eikenosa Opp is a mountain race in Ålesund organized by Emblem IL. The race was first held in 2004 and starts at about 2 meters above sea level at the bottom of Eikenosvågen, 18 km east of Ålesund city center. The course is 4.5 km long and runs on asphalt and gravel roads, finishing at the west end of the dam at Røssevollsvatnet at 295 meters. The men's course record is 17 minutes and 55 seconds, set by Johan Bugge in 2019, while the women's record is 22 minutes and 3 seconds by Ingrid Festøs from 2017.

The race finishes at Røssevollvatnet, which is located 295 meters above sea level.

The purpose of Hamarløpet is to contribute to public health by motivating both young and old to lead active lives. The race aims to be an arena for both the fastest runners and those who typically do not participate in other racing events, encouraging a joy of activity without prestige. Organized by the Hamarløpet Association, this is an ideal initiative where any profits go to charitable causes.
course_highlights: The course for the Hamarløpet is a flat and officially measured 10-kilometer route that runs along beautiful paths by Lake Mjøsa, starting from Hamar city center.
The start and finish line are at Skibladnerbrygga, and the race goes through Koigen, Domkirkeodden, Strandveien, and the two railway underpasses.

name: Ulriken Opp
description: Ulriken Opp 2026 takes place on Saturday, May 30, and is a hill climb race that goes from the lower station to the upper station on Ulriken, the highest of the 7 mountains surrounding Bergen. The course has an elevation difference of about 405 meters from the starting area at 200 meters above sea level to the summit at 605 meters above sea level, and the distance is measured at approximately 1730 meters for the TRIM and MOSJON classes, while the COMPETITION CLASS has a distance of 3.6 km. The course offers varied terrain, from gravel to steep stairs, and provides a spectacular view of Bergen and the North Sea.

The start is from Montana (the gravel track) and the finish is at the top of Ulriken at 605 meters above sea level.

The race features a mass start for the timed category, while the recreational category starts two minutes later. Participants will experience varied terrain and a challenge after 1.5 km due to railway construction that makes the route a slight detour. The Ekholt Race is part of the Mossekarusellen 2025 running series and attracts many participants each year.

description: The Summer Night Run Bergen 2026 is a running festival where participants can choose between 5 km or 10 km. The race takes place in Nygårdsparken, which is centrally located in downtown Bergen, and it is easy to get there by public transport. All participants receive a great medal and refreshments at the finish line, and there is also a chance to win prizes from partners. This race is a fantastic opportunity to test your fitness or just have fun together with hundreds of other runners.

name: Austevollsløpet
description: Welcome to the 41st Austevollsløpet on Sunday, September 29, 2024, at Austevoll Sports Facility. At 12:45, the Mini-Mini marathon for the youngest participants (870 m) will start, and at 13:10, the 5 km race for participants aged 11 and up will take place. Austevollsløpet has been held since the early '80s, featuring a new course that is flat and officially measured, with a total elevation difference of 41 m. We hope to see many recreational runners and families, and we encourage everyone to bring the whole family, as strollers are allowed.
course_highlights: The Mini-Mini marathon is 870 m long for participants aged 0-10 years, starting at 12:45 PM.
The course for the 5 km is as flat as possible, with a total elevation difference of only 41m.

name: Birkebeinerløpet
description: The Birkebeinerløpet is a trail race of 21 km, known as Norway's largest trail race, and takes place in beautiful nature. The race, which has been held every year since 1999, starts at the Sjusjøen cross-country skiing arena and finishes in Lillehammer between Kristins Hall and Håkons Hall. With an elevation difference of 600 meters, the Birkebeinerløpet offers a varied and motivating training experience for both cross-country skiers, orienteers, and long-distance runners. In addition to the main race, the Halvbirkensom is also organized, which starts approximately halfway through the main course.
course_highlights: The Birkebeiner Race is inspired by the ski race Birkebeinerrennet and is organized by the same organizer.
The race has an elevation difference of 600 meters between the start and finish.
Participants can also choose the Half Birkebeiner, which starts at Sjøsætra approximately halfway through the main course.

name: 3 Toppsløpet Jeløya
description: The 3toppsløpet on Jeløy was held for the first time in 2014 and is a trail run that takes you through some of the most beautiful places on Jeløy. You can run four different distances: 1 km, 10 km, 20 km, or 30 km. The race is a true test of strength and a relatively challenging and technically demanding trail run, where runners alternate between running along the beaches and on forest paths. The goal of the race is to create as nice a route as possible around the entire Jeløy, passing over the three well-known peaks: Rødsåsen, Bjørnåsen, and Rambergtoppen.
course_highlights: The runners alternate between running along the beaches and on trails in the forest on beautiful Jeløy.
Every year, the organizers donate the profits from the trail race to charity and aid work.
The race is a true test of strength and a relatively demanding and technically challenging trail run.

This year, we will be part of Tanangerdagene, a festival over 4 days where Tananger showcases its very best for both children and adults, with activities such as Children's Day at Tananger Stadium, dock dancing, stalls, and sales of sausages, soda, and cakes.
course_highlights: Low-threshold recreational race around Tananger Ring.
Part of the Tananger Days, a festival over 4 days.

name: Besseggløpet
description: Besseggen is one of Norway's most beautiful hiking destinations. The Besseggen Race follows the regular T-marked route over the ridge. Start at Memurubu and finish at the Gjendeosen parking area. The terrain is rugged, mainly gravel and stone. There will typically also be some snow in parts of the trail. The start and finish are at about 1000 meters above sea level, with the highest point at approximately 1743 meters above sea level. The course is about 14 km long.
course_highlights: The course is approximately 14 km long, with an elevation difference of 1000 m.
The terrain is uneven, primarily gravel and stone, and there will usually be some snow in parts of the trail.
The Besseggløpet is held every last Saturday in June, offering opportunities for both recreational runners and competitive athletes.

name: Bamford Frontyard
description: Bamford Frontyard consists of a relatively flat 3 km loop, where the first lap must be completed in 30 minutes. The next lap must be run 1 minute faster, and you must have completed all previous laps to continue. The competition ends when only one person finishes the final lap, and if multiple participants start, the fastest to finish will win. Completing 15 laps or more qualifies for the Ultra distance, and a medal is awarded to everyone who completes the first lap.
course_highlights: The first lap must be run in 30 minutes, and for each subsequent lap, the time is reduced by 1 minute.

name: Ålgård-Sirdal 100K
description: Ålgård-Sirdal 100K is a challenging course of 100 kilometers that takes participants from Ålgård to Sirdal. The route is varied, featuring both mountains and roads, and the last aid station is at Lortabu (86 km). After this, the course follows the road to Gravassryggen, before ascending the steep trail to Storeknut. Towards the end of the race, participants will experience a fantastic view over Sirdal from the finish line at Slottet.
course_highlights: The last aid station is at Lortabu (86 km), where the route then follows the road to Gravassryggen.
After 90 km, the participants will understand why the trail gets its name from the 1800s, when shepherds had to herd their sheep from the coast to the mountain pastures in Sirdal.
About 1 km before the finish, there is a steep gravel path leading to the finish at the Castle, where you get a fantastic view of the entire Sirdal.

name: Preikestolen Trailrun
description: The Preikestolen Trailrun is an epic running journey where you follow in the footsteps of Rockman, the legendary figure who braved the rugged trails every weekend in pursuit of winning his beloved's heart, but without swimming. This race is not just a run – it is a mythical adventure where you battle against the forces of nature on some of the world's most spectacular trails. Prepare for a mix of skyrunning, technical trail running, and exhilarating climbing, as you run through mystical forests, cross boulder fields, and ascend to the mountain peaks above the Lysefjord. The route takes you on a secret path to the iconic Preikestolen, before descending into a playground of ancient, rugged terrain.
course_highlights: You will run through mystical forests, cross moors, and ascend to the mountain peaks above the Lysefjord, where the shimmering water is framed by majestic cliffs.
The route takes you along a secret outer trail to the iconic Preikestolen, before descending into a playground of ancient, rugged terrain – shaped by the gods themselves.
This race is extremely technical with an elevation gain of 1200 meters and a distance of 20 km.

name: Jomfrulandsløpet
description: The Jomfruland Race is open to everyone, including those who are not affiliated with a sports club. The "classic" race is 10 km long, consisting of two laps on a 5-kilometer course. It is also possible to participate in one lap, which is 5 km with timing. The course is on flat ground, gravel, and forest trails, and it all takes place on the beautiful island of Jomfruland off the coast of Kragerø.
course_highlights: The race is open to everyone, including those who are not affiliated with a sports club.
The "classic" Jomfrulandsløpet is 10 km long and consists of two laps in a 5-kilometer course.
The course is on flat ground, gravel, and forest trails.

name: Feriespretten
description: Feriespretten is a traditional trail race that has been organized by Hope IL for 34 years. The race features two distances: a long course of approximately 9 km and a short course of about 5 km, both set in varied, hilly terrain. It is scheduled for Tuesday, July 9, 2024, at 5:59 PM (GMT+2) in Sandnes, Norway, with a mass start and 135 participants. Feriespretten is known for its festive atmosphere, even in challenging weather conditions such as rain.
course_highlights: The race has attracted both young and experienced runners, and there has been a record number of participants this year.
Trim trail: If you don't want to be timed, you can still participate as a recreational runner in the short course.
The race is timed using RFID technology and utilizes Webscorer PRO 6.9 for the results.

name: Dream Challenge
description: The inspiring charity race Dream Challenge takes place in Lillesand on Saturday, July 13. Dream Challenge is not just a race, but also a fundraising campaign where all proceeds go directly to Star for Life's work with youth in South Africa – training with purpose. We encourage everyone to participate on this day, where we combine physical activity with support for a good cause. This is an event for the whole family! Bring friends and family and join as runners, support crew, or cheer squad.
course_highlights: All funds go directly to Star for Life's work with youth in South Africa – training with purpose.
This is an event for the whole family!
Together we can make a difference for youth in South Africa.

name: Oslo Bergen Trail
description: Oslo Bergen Trail is a trail ultramarathon from Oslo to Bergen, taking place from July 2-10, 2021. The course is approximately 515 km long with a total elevation gain/loss of 18,000 meters, and follows marked hiking trails (DNT trails) where possible and appropriate. In some short sections, the route goes through forest and mountain terrain without a trail or follows only a faint track. The organizer may activate alternate routes under difficult weather conditions.
course_highlights: The route follows marked hiking trails (DNT trails) where possible and appropriate.
The course is approximately 515 km long with a total elevation gain/loss of 18,000 meters.
This is a team competition where each team can consist of 2 or 3 people.

name: Brunlanesløpet
description: The Brunlanesløpet is organized by Brunlanes IL and starts and finishes outside Nesjarhallen in Helgeroa. The courses run through easy terrain, mostly on gravel roads and trails in beautiful natural areas near Nevlunghavn, Mølen, and Helgeroa. In 2025, the race will take place on July 12, with the children's race starting at 12:30, the Gåløypen at 13:00, the 4.6 km at 13:00, and the 9.0 km at 13:10.
course_highlights: The routes go through easy terrain, mostly on gravel roads and trails in beautiful natural areas.
The Brunlanes Race 2025 will be held on July 12, 2025.
The start and finish are outside Nesjarhallen in Helgeroa.

name: Kvasshovden Opp
description: Kvasshovden Opp is a mountain running race organized by Ulvik Idrettslag, which was first held in 2008. The race has since become a great success, with over 500 participants in 2009 and has been part of the Powerade Norwegian Cup in mountain running. The course starts in the center of Ulvik at about 10 meters above sea level and finishes at the top of Kvasshovden, 1030 meters above sea level, over a distance of 7.5 km. At the top, a fantastic view of the western Norwegian fjord landscape awaits.
course_highlights: The course has a length of 7.5 km and ascends from 0 to 1030 m.a.s.l.
The race is known for its steep and rocky terrain, and the record from the center to the top is under an hour.
Participants can enjoy a spectacular view of the fjord landscape from the top, as well as pass several beautiful mountain pasture areas and local farms along the way.

name: Risberget Rundt
description: Risberget Rundt is a trail run organized by the Risberget Hiking Association every year in July. The routes are well marked, so you can also walk Risberget Rundt on your own throughout the summer season. You can choose between a 5 km and an 11 km loop, making it an ideal family outing. The start and finish are at Kynnbrua.
course_highlights: The trails are marked in the spring so that you can also walk around Risberget on your own throughout the summer months.
You can choose between a 5 km and an 11 km loop.
The start and finish are at Kynnbrua.

name: Hardangerjøkulen Ultra
description: In just over three weeks, I will be running the Hardangerjøkulen ultra. It is a new race on the calendar and has only previously been held as a trial race in 2018. I included it in my race calendar for two main reasons: Hardangervidda is incredibly beautiful, and it is an area I have never run in before. The race is 100 km long with about 2500 meters of elevation gain, starting and finishing in Eidfjord.
course_highlights: The race is 100 km long with approximately 2500 meters of elevation gain.
There is a new race on the calendar, which was only previously held as a trial run in 2018.

name: Espe Rundt
description: Espe Rundt is a 7 km fitness run held every week from Easter to moose hunting season, with a mass start at 6:00 PM every Thursday from Nordåsveien 43 in Birkeland. The course goes up Nordåsstien, continues towards Haugevann, and around Espe before returning to the start. Participation is free of charge, but a small fee is required for prizes in the final race. All results are published on the Espe Rundt Facebook page and in Birkenesavisa.
course_highlights: The course is exactly 7050 m, and the record is held by Hans Gunnar Omdal from Vindbjart with a time of 28:51 set on July 1, 2004.
There is room for everyone who wants a nice trip on a very special course, and the race is best suited for the fit hiker or runner.
You must have completed 3 races to be counted in the final, which is a reverse chase start based on the average of your three best races throughout the summer.

Here, a welcoming environment is created for participation, top conditions, and a fantastic atmosphere. Join us and kickstart the running season indoors at the historic Bislett Stadium! Participants will enjoy a fantastic running experience with nuts and bars, sports drinks from Maxim, and the opportunity to run alongside others at their level.
course_highlights: A fantastic running experience at Bislett Stadium.
Nuts and bars for all registered participants.
The opportunity to run together with others at your level.

name: Skjernøyløpet
description: Welcome to Norway's southernmost race – the Skjernøyløpet – which takes place on Thursday, July 25, 2024, at 6:00 PM, with bib number pickup starting at 5:00 PM. The course is 6 km and runs around Skjernøy in Mandal. This race is for both young and old who want to challenge themselves on this tough and fun course.
course_highlights: The Skjernøy Race is an annual event on the 6 km course around Skjernøy in Mandal.
The race has a mass start and is a road race.
In 2017, 69 participants took part in the race.

name: Preikestolen Trailrun
description: Get ready for an unforgettable adventure at the Preikestolen Trailrun, organized by Rockman on Saturday, July 5, 2025, in the stunning location of Jørpeland, Strand. This epic trail race invites you to conquer a challenging 20 km route with an impressive elevation gain of 1200 meters, as you follow the legendary paths of Rockman himself. Participants will experience a mythical journey through the enchanting landscapes of the Lysefjord, with mystical forests, rock piles, and dramatic mountain peaks. The race culminates at the iconic Preikestolen, offering breathtaking views over the shimmering waters and majestic cliffs.
course_highlights: Participants will experience a mythical journey through the enchanting landscapes of Lysefjorden, with mysterious forests, stone piles, and dramatic mountain peaks.
The race culminates at the iconic Preikestolen, which offers stunning views over the sparkling waters and majestic cliffs.
This is not just a race; it is a test of endurance and spirit against the forces of nature.

name: Kvitfjell Opp
description: Kvitfjell Opp is one of the summer's most brutal uphill races, where we turn the Olympic course upside down and run from the finish at the bottom to the start at the top. The course is 3.2 kilometers long with an elevation gain of 838 meters, following the downhill track used during the 1994 Olympics. Participants will encounter challenging sections such as Mæhlumshenget, Tommy Moe, and Wintherhugget, and the feeling of reaching the top is indescribable!
course_highlights: The course follows the downhill track that was used during the 1994 Olympics and is currently used in connection with the World Cup.
The course features challenging sections such as Mæhlumshenget, Tommy Moe, and Wintherhugget, with inclines of up to 50%.
Kvitfjell Opp is a real challenge for most, but also a manageable task that provides a fantastic sense of accomplishment.

name: Blefjells Beste
description: Blefjells Beste is a social and informal race for everyone who enjoys training in forest and mountain areas. The race starts and finishes at the private cabin Bestebu, located by Klengstøl along Store-Bleveien. We offer several courses: Troll Course 57 km with 2000 m elevation gain, Storetroll Course 93 km with 3200 m elevation gain, Tusse Course 21 km with 750 m elevation gain, Småtusse Course 10 km with 340 m elevation gain, and Småtroll Course 5 km with 110 m elevation gain. The courses primarily follow trails.
course_highlights: We offer the following courses: Troll Trail 57 km, 2000 m elevation gain.
Storetroll Trail 93 km, 3200 m elevation gain.

name: Kvitfjell Stuttlaup
description: Stuttlaupet is a 13 km long race in varied terrain, taking place during the Kvitfjell Running Festival. The festival, which was established in 2022, also includes other races such as Kvitfjell Opp and Langlaupet. In 2024, the festival will expand with Stuttlaupet, which will provide participants with a fantastic experience in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: Stuttlaupet is a 13 km long race in varied terrain.
Kvitfjell Running Festival will be held on July 26 and 27, with the Short Run at 10:00 AM on July 27.
The festival also includes a banquet dinner and an afterparty following the race.

name: Kvitfjell Langlaup
description: The long run is a 25 km race in varied terrain, presenting an extra challenge for those who didn't get enough lactic acid from Friday's uphill race. The course mainly follows marked trails in the mountain area around Kvitfjell, and the race takes place both above and below the tree line, with the highest point at about 1100 meters above sea level. Even though it is mid-summer, it can be wise to be prepared for weather changes.
course_highlights: Kvitfjell Running Festival has been delivering legendary running experiences since 2021, featuring Northern Europe's steepest ski slope and prime trails in the heart of Norwegian nature.
The course is approximately 25 kilometers long, with 19 kilometers on trails and 6.5 kilometers on road.
In 2024, the festival will expand with yet another race, namely the Stuttlaupet.

description: The Strawberry Run and the Mini Run are two separate races taking place in Valldal. The Mini Run starts at 2:45 PM, while the Strawberry Run starts at 3:30 PM. Both races have their start and finish at Rådhusmarka, and there will be an awards ceremony at the pier after the race.

name: Sørlandstesten 11
description: The Sørlandstest is a low-threshold recreational race for everyone who wants a positive running experience, regardless of ambition level. Whether you are training for a bigger goal, feeling the competitive nerves, or just want a social and active day – this is the race for you! There is room for both beginners and experienced runners, and the most important thing is that you show up with a good mood and a desire to run. We cheer just as much for the one who crosses the finish line first as for the one who completes their very first race.
course_highlights: The Sørlandstest offers a flat and fast course up Setesdalsveien to Strai, before participants turn around and run back.
The race features distances of 5 km, 10 km, and a 600 m children's race, making it accessible for all ages and skill levels.
The start and finish are located on the opposite side of the road from Gumpens Auto, providing a simple and accessible location in Kristiansand.

name: Løp til Verdens Ende
description: Run to the World's End is a duathlon where teams of two run trail and swim in open water, without a break between the two disciplines. The running distance is longer than a full marathon, in addition to eight kilometers in the water. According to the organizer, this is a fantastic way to utilize the archipelago, but there is no room for transitions between the two activities, so participants must run and swim in wetsuits and running shoes. It is recommended to use flotation devices to make it easier.
course_highlights: Duathlon with trail running and open water swimming without breaks between the disciplines.
The race distance is longer than a full marathon, in addition to eight kilometers of swimming.
Participants must wear a wetsuit and running shoes, and it is recommended to use flotation devices.

name: Kongsvinger Skogsmaraton
description: Kongsvinger Forest Marathon is Inland's only and Norway's second forest marathon, taking place on August 3, 2024. Here you can choose from many different distances, including the full marathon, half marathon, and Kongsvingermila. Experience an unforgettable day filled with joy, community, and competition in a hilly and varied forest area north and west of Sæter farm. The marathon course follows forest roads and good trails, and there are 3 aid stations along the route.
course_highlights: Kongsvinger Forest Marathon offers distances of 42.2 km, 21.1 km, 10 km, and 4.2 km.
The marathon route runs through a hilly, varied, and beautiful forest area, with the main course following forest roads and good trails.
There are 3 water stations set up for participants during the race.

name: Gaea Norvegica Trail
description: Gaea Norvegica Trail is a multi-day, self-supported race, known as Norway's longest and toughest ultra. There are two routes: the first is 400 kilometers long and the second is 600 kilometers long, both completed over a 5-day period. The race is ITRA-certified and offers 6 UTMB points. Are you brave enough to take on nature and see how you fare? Join us and experience the stunning beauty of Norwegian nature while following the geological Oslo Rift formation from Oslo to Hamar.
course_highlights: The route follows the Akerselva river to Maridalsvannet, continues into Nordmarka up to Eidsvoll, and then heads northeast before ending at Hedmarksvidda.
The total elevation gain in the race is 8300 meters, and assistance is not allowed; participants must carry all clothing, food, and drink in their backpacks.
Gaea Norvegica Trail is ITRA-certified and offers 6 UTMB points, making it a challenging experience for ultrarunners.

name: Møkster Maraton
description: Welcome to Møkster Marathon! The race takes place on Saturday, August 9, 2025, and this is the 13th time the event is being held. Møkster is a beautiful, small island at the edge of the sea, located in Austevoll municipality south of Bergen. Here, participants can experience stunning nature, a guest harbor, a shop, and a restaurant. The routes traverse fields and roads, asphalt and gravel, through farmyards and along old farm roads, providing an absolutely extraordinary experience.
course_highlights: Møkster Marathon was held for the first time on Saturday, August 4, 2012, and it became an unforgettable day for organizers, spectators, and runners.
The race goes over fields and roads, asphalt and gravel, through farmyards and along old farm roads.
Møkster is a small island with about 35 permanent residents and a large group of cabin owners, all with a high percentage of passionate individuals.

name: Skeikampen Rundt
description: Skeikampen Rundt is a trail run set in scenic surroundings of small forests and bare mountains around Skeikampen. The course is approximately 12.2 km long and ascends to 347 meters, and it can be run in either direction, with a descent regardless of the route chosen. The run is moderately challenging and suitable for children, but everyone must enjoy downhill runs. It offers fantastic views of the mountain landscape, including Jotunheimen and Rondane, and concludes with waffles and coffee at one of the cozy mountain cafés.

The trip is moderately challenging and suitable for children, but everyone must enjoy downhill runs.

name: Trysil Trail

Trysil Trail is more than just a race – it’s a weekend filled with after-run activities, social runs, training sessions, and an equipment fair. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced runner, inspiring experiences and nature encounters await you in the spectacular mountain landscape.
course_highlights: Trysil Trail is not just race day – it’s a weekend of running, community, and incredible experiences.
The weekend offers camaraderie, after run, and memorable experiences, in addition to two races through beautiful terrain.
Trysil Trail 14K starts in Fageråsen and follows the Mountain Loop, while the 24K has an additional detour around Skrufjellet.

name: Bodøryggen
description: Bodø Run Bodøryggen, which takes place on Saturday, October 1st, is a majestic mountain race of approximately 21 kilometers from Skaug to Bestemorenga in Bodømarka. This race offers a beautiful trail with fantastic views of the Vestfjord, Lofoten Wall, and the city of Bodø. Bodøryggen is a challenging yet rewarding journey with about 1,000 meters of elevation gain, perfect for experienced hikers looking for a memorable experience.
course_highlights: Start at Skaug, steeply up to Skaugtuva before it levels out and the journey can be enjoyed along Bodøryggen / Løpsfjellet.
Bodøryggen offers a spectacular view of the Vestfjord, the Lofoten Wall, the city of Bodø, and Børvasstindan.
The trail is well marked, but sturdy hiking shoes and necessary equipment are recommended due to the length and elevation changes.

name: Navy Race OCR - Horten
description: Navy Race is an obstacle course that combines exciting land and water-based challenges with an atmosphere filled with community and joy. Whether you are an experienced athlete, a casual exerciser, or a beginner, there is a place for you here – alone or as part of a team. The 8 km course takes you through the old naval base with 30 obstacles, where you will tackle everything from climbing walls and crawling in sand to wading in water. Join for a weekend filled with adrenaline, laughter, and camaraderie, and experience something truly unique as you cross the finish line.
course_highlights: Navy Race presents you with challenges that test both physical and mental strength.

description: The ultramarathon Grue Backyard is completed over 12 laps of 6.7 km each, with a new start every hour. The first lap starts at 09:00, with 1 hour between each lap, and the twelfth and final lap starts at 20:00. If no one finishes the last lap, there are no winners. If multiple participants complete all laps, the winner is the one who crosses the finish line first in the last lap.

name: Mjøsen Backyard Race
description: With 12 laps and a total of 2856 meters of elevation gain, Mjøsen Backyard takes you through a challenge equivalent to running from the deepest point of Lake Mjøsa up to the water surface six times. This is the race for you who want to challenge both body and willpower, and experience the joy of mastering one of Norway's most unique racing concepts. How long can you keep moving? The laps start every hour on the hour, and your pace determines how long your break is before the next start.
course_highlights: Mjøsen Backyard is a backyard race consisting of laps of 6.7 km that are run up to twelve times.
The race starts and ends at a gathering place with a refreshment station, restrooms, and a chair to sit on.

A total of 25 runners and cyclists participated, but only four women lined up at the start, with Ingunn Monsen being the fastest among them at 1:45:46. The organizers describe the course as Norway's most beautiful half marathon route and believe the race has the potential to grow in size.

description: Welcome to the Sparebanken Sør Trail Series 2024! Everyone is welcome to the Trail Series – whether you want to walk, jog, or run. The races take place on Tuesdays with individual starts from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM, children's race at 5:30 PM, and mass starts on time from 6:00 PM. The week's course will be open and marked from Tuesday at 12:00 PM to Thursday at 7:30 PM, and the prizes in 2024 are beautiful glassware from Magnor Glassworks.

There will be 5 different courses in Grenland, all approximately 5 km, which will be run twice during the season, giving you the opportunity to focus on your own mastery and completion. Participation is possible without a time from 5:00 PM or in a mass start with timing at 6:00 PM. The courses vary between trail, gravel, and asphalt, and maps and descriptions will be provided well in advance of the race start.

Everyone can participate regardless of their level, and you can choose whether to run for time or not. The race starts and finishes near the football field, and it is a loop course that is run twice. The children's race starts at 5:30 PM, while the main race begins at 6:00 PM.

The routes mainly take place on gravel roads and trails in Bragernesåsen and Hamborgstrømskogen, and there are significant differences in levels among the participants. name: Lommedalen Løpskarusell
description: The Lommedalen Running Carousel has been held for 4 seasons now, and we will continue this great tradition in 2025. This is a low-threshold event suitable for all ages and ambitions, and it is very informal. No registration is required, just show up! The event is conducted according to five principles, including gathering for social interaction before the start and serving juice at the finish line. We hope to see you at the first race on April 23, and feel free to bring neighbors, friends, colleagues, or the whole family, including the dog! New this year is Kolsåsbakken Opp, a real hill race.
course_highlights: The race is free, and we will be accepting registrations from 6 PM on the race day.
No prizes beyond honor and glory, as well as the good feeling of having run a lap in the beautiful nature of Lommedalen.
We will conduct 6 Wednesdays (3 before and 3 after the summer break) with a defined meeting point.

name: Sørdalskarusellen Races
description: The Sørdalskarusellen consists of ten recreational races from April to September, where all happy participants are welcome to join. New for this year is the Tverrløpet, which replaces the Elvaløpet as the final race in the series, starting at Håkons Hall and finishing at the Engesvea ski jumping facility. The virtual part of the race runs from September 9 to 12, while the mass start takes place on Wednesday, September 13 at 18:30. The course follows the Tverrløypa and features an elevation difference of 59 meters.
course_highlights: The races are intended to be casually enjoyable exercise where you set the standard yourself.
Everyone who completes at least 6 races will receive a participant prize, which will be awarded at the prize ceremony at the end of October or the beginning of November.
The goal is joy in running, community, and challenge, and the races are organized as a mass start on Wednesdays and virtually from Saturday to Tuesday beforehand.

name: Twilight 5000
description: Tracksmith Twilight 5000 is a series of races that offers a unique blend of competition and community. Runners take to the track under the floodlights and compete in the 5K distance on iconic tracks around the world. New York City, with its rich history and diverse communities, provides the perfect backdrop for the Twilight 5000 series, which takes place at Icahn Stadium along the East River. This race is a celebration of speed, endurance, and the vibrant communities that running creates.
course_highlights: Runners line up on the track beneath the floodlights and race the 5K distance at iconic venues around the world.
Dedicated pacers and like-minded competitors are there to keep you on pace, and the constant support of your local community carries you throughout the race.
At Bislett Stadium, runners will have the opportunity to compete on the same track as Olympians, surrounded by the city's iconic landmarks.

name: Den Breiale Milen
description: The Breiale Milen kicks off on August 17 in Frognerkilen, and this year the very successful event is being held on a Saturday. The race, which spans 14.50 km, starts and finishes at Kongen Marina, taking participants on a loop around Bygdøy and Sollerud beach. The event is known for its jovial atmosphere and includes a unique category for nose breathing, as well as a festive afterrun at Oslo's coolest venue.
course_highlights: The race has attracted both elite athletes and recreational runners, and the winner of the men's category, Eirik Aabrekk, set a new course record with a time of 49:19.
Tiril Knudsen, a skier in Norway's elite, won the women's category and expressed excitement about the relaxed atmosphere and the afterrun celebration.
The Breiale Mile is the only race with a separate category for nasal breathing (unisex), which adds an extra dimension and fun to the event.

description: Haglebu Backyard Ultra is an ultramarathon event taking place on August 23, 2025, with the start and finish at Haglebu Feriesenter. Participants must complete as many laps as possible of 6706 meters each hour, with a new lap starting every 60 minutes. There is a maximum of 12 laps, and the first man and woman to finish the last lap win the race. Everyone who completes at least one lap will receive a medal, and there will also be raffle prizes.

name: Drøbakløpet
description: The Drøbak Race replaces the traditional Blomstermila and has changed both the course layout and the start/finish location to Drøbak Torg. The race takes place in August, after the school year begins, to avoid competition with the end of school and vacation plans. The course runs from Drøbak Torg, through Kirkegata and Badeparken, past Drøbak Church, and ends up in Storgata. Parts of the course will be closed off to ensure traffic safety, but arrangements will be made for the town center to remain lively that afternoon.
course_highlights: The race starts at Drøbak Torg and follows a varied route that includes Badeparken, the fjord, and several well-known locations in Drøbak.

The course follows the coastal path along the water, with a turnaround at the kiosk on Steinbrygga, before taking you out of the woods by the treatment plant and back to Horten via the coastal path. This race offers you the chance to experience stunning natural scenery while challenging yourself in a half marathon.

description: Vikerfjell Challenge is an exciting running experience with fantastic nature encounters and challenging courses. Participants can choose between three distances: 21 km, 11 km, and a 2.5 km children's race. The courses run on gravel roads, trails, and in terrain, so be prepared to get your feet wet. The longest distance starts from Ringerudsetra and ends at Skarrudsetra, while the 11 km course starts from Tossviksetra.
course_highlights: Fantastic nature, atmosphere, and trails – take the challenge!
The course runs on gravel roads, trails, and in terrain, so be prepared to get your feet wet.

name: Nipkollen Challenge
description: The Nipkollen Challenge is not just any race – it’s a raw experience through Nannestad's most beautiful and challenging terrain. This is not about fast asphalt kilometers, but about mastering technical trails, steep ascents, and undulating stretches that truly test you. Three distances – one common challenge: 14 km for all ages, 25 km for the tough, and 50 km for the truly dedicated, which is one of Norway's toughest ultramarathons. The race offers participants the chance to test their skills in a spectacular setting, with views that reward the effort.
course_highlights: 14 km – Perfect for those who want to experience the magic of trail running. Open to all ages!
25 km – A solid challenge for the tough. Age limit 14 years.
50 km – Ultra for the truly dedicated! This is one of Norway's toughest ultra distances, and we promise you'll feel it in both your legs and your mind. Age limit 16 years.

name: Østmarka Trail Challenge
description: Østmarka Trail Challenge – The Refugee Route is a tough trail race of about 37 km that follows blue-marked paths through Østmarka. The course follows a route that was used during World War II to help people escape the country, and runs between Enebakk/Øyeren and Skullerud in Oslo. This race is incredibly fun and challenging, providing participants with a unique experience in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: The course follows a route that was used during World War II to smuggle people out of the country.

description: Skåbu Fjellmaraton Ultra starts at Bygdin on Valdresflya, about 13 km from Beitostølen, and follows the Jotunheim Road past idyllic mountain farms along Vinstervatna. The race offers fantastic views of the peaks of Jotunheimen and beautiful mountains. From about 35 km, participants follow the marathon course all the way to the finish, with a tough ending up the notorious Kamfossbakken, which has an average incline of 10% over 3 km. This race takes place in the foothills of Jotunheimen and includes an incorporated uphill race.

name: Oppdalskarusellen 4. løp
description: Welcome back to the Oppdal Carousel 2026, when the snow has melted and the roads are clear! The Oppdal Carousel 2025 includes five events, with the first race taking place on May 4th. Results from previous races show strong performances, with Mads Berge and Bente Lien Hæhre as the winners in the men's and women's categories in the 4th race (Smerudsrunden) on August 24th. Join us for an exciting race series in beautiful Oppdal!
course_highlights: Congratulations to the winners Mads Berge (10:05) and Helle Kristensen (12:33) from the first race on May 4th!
Mads Berge and Bente Lien Hæhre won in the men's and women's categories in the 4th race (Smerudsrunden) with times of 9:58 and 11:19, respectively!
The Oppdal Carousel 2025 has five events, including the toughest race, Oppdal's Toughest - Koperud Uphill.

name: Eidsvoll Verk 6-Hour
description: Eidsvoll Verk 6-Hour is a unique ultramarathon that features a flat course with 550-meter laps on the roller ski track at Eidsvoll Verk ski stadium. This event, which was first held in August 2005, is considered the beginning of the Norwegian ultramarathon wave. The event is supported by Eidsvold Værks Skiklub, one of the world's oldest ski clubs, and the technical organizer is Feiring IL.
course_highlights: The course is a very flat loop - 550 meter long laps.
Eidsvoll Verk 6-Hour was first held in 2005 and is recognized as the beginning of the Norwegian ultrarunning wave.
The race is supported by Eidsvold Værks Ski Club, founded in 1881.

name: Bruvollenstafetten
description: The Bruvollen Relay is our longest-running event, having taken place for over 60 years. The relay is scheduled for May 1st each spring, but due to the construction of a new artificial turf field, there will be an exception this year with the event taking place on Sunday, August 24, 2025. This race is for both young and old, and there is no age limit for participation.
course_highlights: The two-and-a-half-year-old charmer Marius Weinholdt gave it his all on his 200-meter leg, and in the Bruvollen Relay, as is well known, no one is too small and no one is too big.
Marius Weinholdt, who is the youngest participant ever, completed the 200-meter long fifth leg in the open class with impeccable style.
We invite everyone with a heart for Blaker IL to join us for our first digital Bruvollen Relay, where you can contribute to the sports club and support the local community.

name: Høgåsen Rundt
description: Only 15 participants lined up for this year's Høgåsen Rundt, which has made a comeback after 14 years at the sports field in Oppstad. The bad weather in the days leading up, with a lot of rain and wind, must take some of the blame for the low turnout. Those who completed the race were very satisfied and thanked for the well-prepared and marked course! In the 17 km race, Lasse Ringkilen had the best time of 1:19:48 (men 17 years or older), while Serine Lilleseth Boisen had the best time of 1:11:31 in the 11 km race (women 16 years or younger).
course_highlights: In the 17 km course, Lasse Ringkilen had the best time of 1:19:48 (men 17 years or older).
In the 11 km course, Serine Lilleseth Boisen had the best time of 1:11:31 (women 16 years or younger).
Winners of the fruit baskets were John Iver Gaustad and Casper Eriksen.

name: Granestua Race
description: On Sunday, August 24, the traditional forest race "First to Granestua" will take place. The start is at Sparebanken Sør Amfi in Myra, Arendal, and the course follows beautiful forest trails up to the finish at Granestua. The distance is 10 km, and the event is organized by Agder Corporate Sports Association with 119 participants registered.
course_highlights: The course follows beautiful forest trails up to the finish at Granestua.
The event is organized by the Agder Business Sports Association in Arendal.
There are 119 participants registered for the race.

name: Mud Monkey 2025
description:
MUDMONKEY 2025

Welcome to the Jungle. Play Dirty. Laugh Louder.

Mud. Obstacles. Screams and laughter. This is not a race – this is the jungle's playground for adults (and teenagers who aren't afraid to slip in style).

MudMonkey 2025 invites you to a day of total bananas in nature: climbing, crawling, water, fire, and a bunch of race-crazy Monkeys who live to challenge you through the course. Forget asphalt and fences – here you face the jungle's resistance with a grin.

MUDMONKEY 5K – “Monkey Business in Battle Mode”

5 kilometers with 25 technical and natural obstacles. 
You climb, tumble, crawl, and laugh your way through the mud while unruly MudMonkeys try to block you – physically. 
Go solo or as a tribe – but one thing is for sure: You will emerge covered in mud and full of adrenaline.

Age limit: 13+

A parental declaration must be signed before the start (sent via email the week before the race).

MUDMONKEY 8K – “Mud Mayhem and Jungle Fury”

8 kilometers. 40+ obstacles.

When you think it can't get wilder, you arrive here. 
This is the highlight of the obstacle race: mud pits, zip lines, icy water, flames, slippery stones – and of course, crazy MudMonkeys trying to topple you with laughter and resistance.

Age limit: 16+

A declaration must be signed before the start (sent via email the week before the race).

____________________________________________________________________________________

COMING 2026 – MUDMONKEY EXTREME 21K

“For those who have never been dirty enough”

21 km. 70+ obstacles. Here you will meet your limits – and have them shattered.

Spectator-friendly, but participant-hostile course full of fire, ice, mud, and monkey madness.

Only for the most bananas among us.

Age limit: 18+
A declaration must be signed before the start (sent via email the week before the race).

EVERYONE GETS A MEDAL – NO ONE GOES HOME DRY OR CLEAN!!

Here, competition is held in individual classes and in tribes (teams). 
The fastest will be celebrated with honor and glory – but everyone who finishes gets a medal and the right to call themselves a true MudMonkey.
additional: Feel free to call us at 95961803 or send an email to hei@xchallenge.no.
course_highlights: Varied terrain with natural obstacles that makes the race both exciting and challenging.
Opportunity to enjoy beautiful nature and landscapes along the way.
Open to both beginners and experienced runners, creating an inclusive atmosphere.

name: Terrengkarusellen Kvinesdal
description: Welcome to the Terrain Carousel Kvinesdal/Flekkefjord 2024! The carousel consists of 7 races held on Tuesdays from April 30 to September 17. Distance: 4 - 12 km. The Terrain Carousel is suitable for everyone, whether you want to walk, jog, or run at your own pace through the trails. It is an inclusive and social meeting place where friends, colleagues, and acquaintances come together for shared exercise – regardless of ambitions or prerequisites.
course_highlights: The Terrain Carousel offers eight fantastic courses.
In 5 of the races, you can choose whether you want to run the regular distance or the double distance (Milsluker).
Mass start at 6:00 PM, with a warm-up starting from 5:00 PM.

name: Tromsøkarusell 12. løp
location: Idrettens Hus / Alfheim stadion, Stadionveien 3 (søndre inngang, 3. etg.)
description: The Tromsø Carousel 2025 is a race that will be held from Tuesday, May 6, 2025, to Tuesday, September 23, 2025. It is open to participants aged 15 to 100 years, and companies can obtain a corporate agreement for registrations. In 2012, 16 races were held during the period from May to September, ranging from 3,000 meters to half marathon, on track, asphalt, and nature trails. We encourage all Northern Runners to participate!
course_highlights: The Tromsø Carousel 2025 is open to participants aged 15 to 100 years.
In 2012, 1,434 participants took part.
The races range from 3,000 meters to half marathon, on track, asphalt, and trail.

name: Holavatnet Rundt 13
description: Holavatnet Rundt 13 is an exciting running event that takes participants around the beautiful Holavatnet. The course, which was first held in 1983 and is now in its 41st season, offers scenic views of the lake and its surroundings, with varying terrain that challenges both beginners and experienced runners. On average, about 130 people show up every Wednesday to exercise or test their fitness in this picturesque course, which runs on asphalt and gravel paths, and it's easy to bring a stroller along.
course_highlights: The course goes around Holavatnet on asphalt and gravel paths, and it's easy to take a stroller along for the loop.
The race has a friendly atmosphere, where both locals and visitors can come together to share their passion for running.
The course is 3.1 km long, featuring a nature trail for children in the hiking class and a prize awarded at the cabin (approximately 450 meters above sea level).

name: Kambomila
description: Kambomila (mass start) will take place on Wednesday, August 27 at 18:30 at Noreødegården. Participants can choose between the distances of 10.2 km and 5.8 km. OK Moss encourages our active members to test their form against themselves and other local runners in this race series, which consists of 4 races over the summer season in Moss and the surrounding area. With many dressed in yellow of all ages, this is a great platform to promote the club and our inclusiveness.
course_highlights: Participants can choose between the distances of 10.2 km and 5.8 km.
The race has previously resulted in a new record at Kambomila, and there is always full speed through the courses.
Kambomila is part of a running carousel that spans the summer half of the year.

name: Kodalmila
description: Kodalmila, which will take place on Saturday, August 30, 2025, is Vestfold's oldest fun run and is being held for the 47th time. Participants can choose between a 10 km road race (start at 14:00) and a 5 km trail run (start at 14:05), both for NOK 300 + license fee. There is also a 2.5 km trail run (start at 14:10) for NOK 100 and a children's race (start at 13:30) for NOK 50. Registration takes place at www.eqtiming.no, and race numbers can be picked up at Kodal IL's clubhouse at Rismyrveien 10b from 12:00 on race day.
course_highlights: Vestfold's oldest recreational race, established in 1978, featuring a 10 km asphalt course and a 5 km trail.
The starting location is the bus pocket in Kodal center, with the pickup of race numbers at the Kodal IL clubhouse on race day.
Children's race available for young participants at a price of NOK 50.

name: Stavanger Marathon
description: The last Saturday in August is a festival in downtown Stavanger. Our routes run along lakes and fjords, with a delightful combination of asphalt and gravel. Whether you want to run long or short, we have a distance for you; choose from a children's race, 5 km, half marathon, marathon, and marathon relay. Stavanger Marathon is a well-organized event with a great atmosphere, where you meet enthusiastic volunteers cheering you on. Experience the excitement before the start, the joy of overcoming yourself during the race, and the rush of crossing the finish line.
course_highlights: Stavanger Marathon offers you a unique opportunity to explore the Stavanger region, running around picturesque lakes and along beautiful fjords.
The event has a great atmosphere, where you meet many dedicated volunteers who guide you and provide you with drinks.
Experience the thrilling atmosphere before the start and the joy of surpassing yourself during the race.

name: Sognefjord Trail Run
description:
Join the Sognefjord Trail Run 2025! A spectacular trail race set in the majestic landscape of the Sognefjord - Norway's longest and deepest fjord.

Choose between 13, 23, or 43 km and experience technical trails, flowing paths, and stunning surroundings. The race is suitable for both experienced runners and beginners – big and small.

You will become part of an inclusive community, with social activities in the mountain sports village of Sogndal on both Friday and Saturday evenings.

Sign up now – and be part of an extraordinary racing experience! 🏃‍♀️⛰️🌟
course_highlights: The route passes Fanaråken, home to the highest cabin in Norway (2068 m a.s.l.).
On clear days, the summit of Galdhøpiggen offers a fantastic view of the western part of Jotunheimen.
Choose between distances of 13KM, 21KM, 42KM, or join the kids' race.

name: Lyderhorn Opp
description: Lyderhorn Opp is a combination of a social outdoor event for the whole family, an informal fun run, and a mountain running competition. The starting point is at Falck Nutec in Gravdal, with the finish line at the top of Lyderhorn, 396 meters above sea level. The course is approximately 3.8 km, and all school students in the Laksevåg district are offered the opportunity to participate for free.
course_highlights: Lyderhorn Opp is a social outdoor event for the whole family.
The starting point is at Falck Nutec in Gravdal, with the finish line at the top of Lyderhorn, 396 meters above sea level.

name: Ragnarok OCR
description: Ragnarok OCR is an obstacle race that will test your physical and mental limits, and is being organized in connection with the 10th anniversary of Achievers Multisport Team. The race takes place on September 28th in Bygnes, Karmøy, and has a Norse mythology theme. There will be an adult race, a family race, and a children's race, and the event is designed to be accessible for everyone, from beginners to elite athletes. Corporate teams, sports clubs, and bachelor parties can also register.
course_highlights: The race has a Norse mythology theme.
There will be an adult race, a family race, and a children's race.
Everyone should be able to participate, whether they are completely untrained or an elite athlete.

name: Dogrun Ridderdagene
description: Vom Dogrun is for everyone who wants to join in a pleasant activity with their dog. You can choose to participate with or without timing, and it’s a social and fun outing with your dog, in the company of other dog lovers. VOM PUPPY WALK is a separate activity for puppies – which is free to sign up for. Additionally, Vom Dogrun is free for all participants under 18 years old, and every participant receives a medal.
course_highlights: VOM PUPPY WALK is a special activity for puppies – which is free to sign up for.
The Vom Dogrun is free for everyone under 18 years old.
There is a participation medal for everyone.

name: HOKA-mila Moelv
description: The HOKA Mile is a 10,000-meter track race held on the new blue track in Moelv, Skarpsno Arena, on Saturday, August 31. This race is for everyone, and participants are divided into heats based on their expected finish times, providing a golden opportunity for fast times, whether you are chasing a personal record or the national championship requirement. With 25 flat laps without a single meter of elevation, the organizers promise a fantastic day dedicated to running and community, with a great atmosphere and festive surroundings.
course_highlights: The HOKA Mile is held on the new blue track in Moelv, Skarpsno Arena, and is a race for everyone, with heats tailored to "your" pace.
This race is a golden opportunity for fast times, whether you run the 10K in just over an hour or under half an hour.
The organizers promise a great atmosphere and a festive environment around this new, audience-friendly race.

name: Hessjøen Rundt
description: Hessjøen Rundt is a race featuring a recreational course. The course for the competitive class and the longest recreational route is approximately 12 km long, while the recreational course is about 6 km with a relatively flat profile, suitable for the whole family. The race takes place on Saturday, August 31, 2024, with the start and finish at Stevneplassen. Participants can register from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM for the recreational class, while the competitive classes start at 12:00 PM.
course_highlights: Everyone receives a participant badge, and the top three in each competition class are rewarded with gift cards.
There is a kiosk at the start and finish area that sells coffee, soda, hamburgers, hot dogs, cake, and more.
To drive on Hessjøvegen, one must pay a fee of 70 NOK.

name: Hardangervidda Marathon
description: Welcome to the Dynafit Hardangervidda Marathon! This is not an ordinary marathon where you run on asphalt in a flat course profile. Here, the keywords are mountain plateaus and grand nature experiences. You will run in mountain terrain in spectacular surroundings on Hardangervidda, with two grueling climbs that are guaranteed to burn. On this day, you will use all your strength and experience a nature adventure you will not soon forget.
course_highlights: You run in mountainous terrain in spectacular surroundings on the Hardangervidda.
The course has both technically demanding sections and nice fast trails.
An enthusiastic crew will cheer you on, and you might need that.

This race is an excellent chance to experience nature while you train.

name: Porsgrunn Halvmaraton
description: Experience the news of the Porsgrunn Half Marathon 2025, a community celebration in Porsgrunn City Center. The start and finish line is at Franklintorget outside the Down Town shopping center, where there will also be entertainment, booths, and a free children's race. The Porsgrunn Half Marathon is an accessible race for everyone, regardless of skill level, and there is the option to participate alone or with family, friends, and colleagues. We look forward to creating an unforgettable community celebration for both runners and spectators!
course_highlights: There will be entertainment and a great atmosphere along the course for both runners and spectators.
Participate alone or with family, friends, and colleagues and have fun together.

name: Grensetrimmen
description: The Grensetrimmen is a recreational race that takes place on runner-friendly trails and gravel roads, with some asphalt sections on the Swedish side. The course features a few moderate inclines in the middle section but is relatively flat and easy to run. The distance is stated to be 10 km (but was measured at 9.3 km) and has remained the same since its inception in 1983. The race takes place on the first Saturday in September at Støa in Trysil.
course_highlights: The course has some moderate inclines in the middle section, but is relatively flat and easy to run.
The distance is stated as 10 km (but was measured at 9.3 km).

name: Kolbotnvannet Rundt
description: Kolbotnvannet Rundt features a course in scenic surroundings on terrain, gravel, and asphalt. You can participate with or without timing, with distances of 5 km and 10 km. The start is at Kolbotn Torg, and the route includes asphalt, forest trails, and gravel, with a finish line after 5 km. There is also a family event with a shorter loop of about 2 km, perfect for strollers.
course_highlights: Race with timing: Compete for the best possible time, with course lengths of 5 km and 10 km (two laps).
Run without timing: Complete at your own pace and enjoy the surroundings around Kolbotnvannet.
We also have a family event in the vicinity of Kolbotn Torg, with competitions along the route.

name: Styrkeprøven Rett Vest
description: Styrkeprøven Rett Vest is an ultramarathon held in the mountains of Bergen on the last weekend of August. The course, which stretches approximately 45 km from Gullbotn to Kjøkkelvik, has a total elevation gain of over 3000 meters and includes several peaks such as Gullfjellstoppen and Ulriken. Since its inception in 1984, this event has become an annual tradition for many running enthusiasts, with course records of 4 hours and 40 minutes for men and 6 hours and 3 minutes for women. In 2023, Styrkeprøven Rett Vest celebrated its 35th anniversary.
course_highlights: The route starts at Gullbotn and ascends to the summit of Gullfjell, which is the highest point of the route at 987 meters.
The course has a total elevation gain of over 3000 meters, providing a challenging and scenic experience.
Styrkeprøven Rett Vest is composed of volunteer members focused on creating a healthy and motivating activity event.

description: The Ledenløpet 2025 is a race through the cultural landscape in the heart of Gudbrandsdalen. Four distances are offered: Long Trail 27 km (Black), Middle Trail 17 km (Red), Short Trail 7 km (Blue), and Raspberry Trail 1 km. All distances finish at Nermo Hotel, and the race follows the Pilgrims' Trail from Fjøssystemer (Sør-Fåvang) to Øyer.
course_highlights: The Leden Race 2025 is a race through the cultural landscape in the heart of Gudbrandsdalen.
Four distances are offered: Long Trail 27 km (Black), Medium Trail 17 km (Red), Short Trail 7 km (Blue), and Raspberry Trail 1 km.

name: Hodlekve Fjelløp
description: Join the mountain race of a lifetime! Hodlekve Rundt takes place on Saturday, September 24, and offers distances of 21 km, 10 km, and 6 km in beautiful terrain. This is the fourth year the race is being organized, and the routes follow marked trails. The activity day in Hodlekve will have offerings for both young and old, with a junior race, a treasure hunt, and sales of coffee and food at Dalalåven, which is open from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM.
course_highlights: The starting gun for the 21 km race goes off at 10:00, while the 10 km and 6 km races start at 10:30.
Dalalåven will have open coffee with food and drink service, as well as bike rental available on this day.
There will be activities for the whole family, including a junior race and a treasure hunt from Sognenett.

name: Oslo Løpsfestival - Fornebu Rundt
description: The Oslo Running Festival consists of eight races along the capital's beautiful trails and scenic roads. You can run whenever you want – alone or together with others, either in the SOLO category or in the team competition as a DUO or TRIO. Each race is announced on Friday at 12:00, and the course is open until Sunday at 11:00 the following weekend, with a mass start precisely at 11:00. The course is certified to be as close to 10 km as possible.
course_highlights: You can participate alone in the SOLO class, or in the team competition as a DUO or TRIO.
Each race is scheduled to be announced on Friday at 12:00 PM, and the course is open until Sunday at 11:00 AM the following weekend.
The course has been officially measured to be as close to 10 km as possible.

name: Røykenmila
description: The Røykenmila is a race that aims to create value in the local community and serves as an activity day for the whole family. The event has three goals: to create a festive day for everyone together with businesses and local associations, to motivate people to start training, and to raise money for good causes in the local community. There is an inclusive atmosphere with awards for participants in the 5 km and 10 km distances, as well as activities, booths, and entertainment for the entire family.
course_highlights: Røykenmila aims to create value in the local community and motivate people to start training.
The event includes activities for the whole family, with booths and entertainment.
There is an inclusive atmosphere with awards for participants in the 5 km and 10 km distances.

name: Puttekollen Opp
description: Puttekollen Opp is a family-friendly summit hike in Begnadalen with a great view towards Sørum. The trail goes through easy forest terrain and is approximately 1.5 km one way, with an elevation gain of about 200 meters. It takes about 45−60 minutes to complete and is suitable for children from around 5 years old.
course_highlights: Family-friendly summit hike in Begnadalen with a nice view towards Sørum.
The route goes through easy forest terrain.
Suitable for children from about 5 years old.

During the journey across the mountain, you can expect both a thrilling sensation in your stomach and lactic acid in your legs, but above all, a fantastic experience with magnificent peaks like Vengetindene, Romsdalshorn, and Trolltindene surrounding you. The course is 8.6 km long, with 970 meters of positive elevation gain and 700 meters of negative elevation, and features exciting and challenging sections equipped with safety measures for secure passage.

The course includes 4 different secured sections with chains to help participants navigate the challenging areas.

name: Blodslitet
description: Blodslitet is an orienteering race, long-distance, ultra-long-distance, organized every year by Fredrikstad Ski Club. This race is the oldest local race still held in Ålesund and takes place early in the fall, usually in September. In 2025, the race will take place on Wednesday, September 10 at 6:00 PM, starting at the top of Fagerlia with a total length of 6.71 km. The course includes tough uphill sections but becomes easier towards the end, and trophies are awarded to the best female and male runners.
course_highlights: The race has a long history dating back to the early 1980s, with the first event in Blodslitet in 1982.
The course record for men is 23:07, set by Lars Roger Lundanes in 1985, while the women's record is 24:35 by Live Johannessen Solheimdal (2023).
Around 2000 participants from all over Scandinavia take part, and Blodslitet has established a strong reputation as a top-quality event.

name: Grimstad Marathon

description: The Airport Mile 2025 will be held on Saturday, September 20, 2025, and is known for having the "world's fastest course" on the runway of Stord Airport, Sørstokken. The course is almost completely flat and has a straight direction, providing optimal conditions for setting personal records. Participants can choose between the distances of 5 kilometers and 10 kilometers, with certified and officially measured courses.
course_highlights: The course layout is on the runway at Stord Airport, with turns resembling an indoor athletics track, 11m radius/22m diameter.
One lap is 2.5 kilometers, and the course shows a total elevation gain of 7 meters on Strava.
Race numbers can be picked up at the terminal at the airport from 10:00 AM, so please be there in good time!

name: Trail Monkey
description:
Unleash your inner TrailMonkey! 

Are you ready to play through nature like a true TrailMonkey? Monkeytrail is not like other races – it’s a celebration of freedom, movement, and playfulness. Here, it’s not just about kilometers and seconds, but about muddy shoes, grins under fir trees, and the feeling of being wildly alive.

Your adventure awaits...

Choose between two epic courses:

    6KM Trail – perfect for those who want to challenge themselves in hilly, playful terrain.

    12KM Tough Monkey Edition – for those who can’t get enough of hills, slopes, and forest magic.

    18KM MonKey Banan – for those who want to go all in: more running, more mud, more madness. And maybe a banana at the finish line.

Run, climb, laugh – and become part of something bigger...

MonkeyTrail is made for both everyday heroes and wilderness veterans. Here we celebrate movement in nature – whether you leap over roots like a ninja monkey or take your time while inhaling forest air like a Zen monk on caffeine.

You don’t need top speed; you need a sense of adventure. And maybe a little balance.

Nature's superpowers (and why you become magical by participating)

    You get a better mood just by tying your shoelaces.

    The trees give you a free mental reboot.

    Every hill you conquer grants you +10 self-respect and +5 smiles.

    And mud? Well, it’s nature’s beauty treatment for the soul.

Medal for EVERYONE – Because you are a true TrailMonkey

Everyone who finishes receives the legendary TrailMonkey medal – proof that you master the terrain and dare to play. The winners are rewarded with honor, glory, and prizes – but everyone is rewarded with nature’s applause and a solid sense of achievement.

Join us!

Become part of the pack. Run and laugh. 
Monkeytrail – it’s not just a race. 
It’s the freedom in a pair of trail shoes.
course_highlights: Our events are made for everyone - from 5 km beginners to ultra marathon warriors - and are designed with inclusivity and boundary-breaking ideas in mind.
Navigate our well-marked trails safely with support from our experienced team, and feel the energy from our close-knit, supportive running community.
At the finish line, you celebrate your achievements not only with a medal but with a warm welcome from the community, and yes, some good old tea and cake!

name: Hauernløpet
description: The Hauernløpet is a trail race of 19 km that mostly takes place on paths, with sections of gravel, through beautiful areas in Drammensmarka. The first five kilometers have an approximately 50/50 distribution between paths and gravel, while the next segment is almost exclusively on paths until 15 km. From 15 to 17 km, there is more gravel than path, before it returns to paths for the final stretch to the finish line. In total, there is about 75% path and 25% gravel.

The race goes through beautiful areas in Drammensmarka.
Overall, about 75% of the route is on trail and 25% on gravel.

name: Fædrelandsvennen Stafetten
description: The FVN Relay 2025 is organized by the Agder Corporate Sports Association in collaboration with Fædrelandsvennen. There will be competitions in mixed, women's, and men's categories, focusing on the joy of running, community, and team building. Each category consists of three legs, with each leg being approximately 2.2 km. The event will take place on Saturday, September 20, in Tresse, Kristiansand, and there will also be a separate active category for the fittest women and men participating in the mass start.

Each leg is approximately 2.2 km, and there are three legs per team.

name: Stjernemila
description: The Stjernemila is a running event that starts in the center of Flekkefjord, right in the middle of the festivities! The course is approximately 10 kilometers long and follows a star-shaped route from the finish area, with six "arms" that take you to iconic locations in the center. The course is well-marked, and participants can have their leg times recorded on the big screen, providing the audience with a good overview. The event includes both the main race and a relay, as well as free children's races for the age groups 3-7 years and 8-12 years.
course_highlights: The runners take off in a star shape from the finish area, heading out into the 6 "arms" of the star, each of which is an iconic location in the center of Flekkefjord.
The course includes quite a few hills to reach the viewpoints, but it's no more than about 200 meters of elevation.
The Star Mile is more than just a race; the center will be buzzing with life and activities for both young and old, with exciting menus at the city's many outdoor venues in the evening.

description: The traditional Oppdal Race kicks off on Saturday, September 21 at 1:00 PM! The Oppdal Race is a 3.5 km long trail run, along gravel roads and paths, with the start and finish at the NOIL square. There is an opportunity to both run and walk, and the race is suitable for all ages. Pre-registration is possible until midnight on September 20, while late registration takes place on Saturday, September 21 between 12:00 and 12:30 at NOIL. Registration is free, and a trophy will be awarded to the fastest woman and man. Welcome!

name: Kristiansand Backyard Ultra
description: The laps start every full hour, and your pace determines how long your break is before the next start. Although the ultimate goal is to reach 80.4 km, you are warmly welcome to run as many laps as you wish – or can manage. For us at Backyard Norway, running is not about showing off or the pursuit of being the best, but about overcoming oneself and pushing new boundaries. Regardless of whether this boundary is at 10, 25, or 80 km, all runners are welcome, and the last participant to finish has performed just as strongly as the first.
course_highlights: The laps start every hour on the hour, and your pace determines how long of a break you get before the next start.
Even though the ultimate goal is to reach 80.4 km, you are warmly welcome to run as many laps as you want – or can manage.
Running is a lifestyle and a leisure activity, and we want to challenge ourselves and push new boundaries.

name: Kongeløpet
description: The King’s Race is a recreational run that goes from Byrknesøy to Skjerjehamn. The race covers a distance of 13 km, over bridges and islands, on asphalt in beautiful coastal scenery. Just hilly enough to be challenging.

There are 3 water stations along the route. Organizers assist with the transport of equipment from the starting point to the finish line.

name: Skeikampen Opp
description: Skeikampen Opp is a mountain race from the base of Skeikampen to the stone hut at the top. The race is suitable for both active athletes and recreational runners of all ages, so there's no excuse not to participate. It is 2.9 km long and consists of 340 meters of elevation gain. You can choose which category you want to compete in, with a recreational category for those who do not wish to be timed. The competitive categories start in waves according to age from 12:00 PM.

You can choose to start between 11:00 AM and 11:30 AM if you are participating in the recreational class.

description: The wait is over! VOM Dogrun is returning to Kristiansand and hosting a real dog party at Tresse outside Christiansholm Fortress. course_highlights: The event offers a unique combination of elite competition and the joy of running in fantastic surroundings.

name: Stavanger Backyard
description: Backyard Stavanger is a backyard ultra that takes place in late September each year. It follows the classic backyard formula where all participants run laps of 6.7 km every hour, and you must be ready for a new lap before the next one starts in order to continue. A maximum of 12 laps can be run, which corresponds to 50 miles or 80 kilometers. The fastest runner on the 12th lap is considered the winner of the race, and the times before this do not matter. The course is partly gravel and partly asphalt, so it is important to dress appropriately and be prepared for changing weather conditions.

description: PB Milå is a Kondis Quality Event street race with the start and finish in Randaberg City Center, organized by Grødem Runners. The course is certified and nationally approved by a certified course measurer. The race takes place on Saturday, September 26, 2026, and offers distances of 5 km and 10 km.

Start and finish in Randaberg Center.

name: Birken Gateløp
description: Birken is expanding its portfolio with a brand new event: a full-fledged street race in beautiful Lillehammer! This street race, taking place on September 27, 2025, will go through the center of Lillehammer with the start and finish at Lilletorget. It is an accessible opportunity for everyone, whether you are a recreational runner, an experienced athlete, or just want to challenge yourself. The event offers a unique chance to experience the city's streets, set a training goal, and build community, while a portion of the profits will go back to the local community.
course_highlights: The course will go through downtown Lillehammer, with the start and finish at Lilletorget.
Distances: 10 km (160 meters of elevation), 5 km, and 300 m (children's race).
There will be entertainment, cultural performances, "afterrun," and great deals in stores and restaurants.

name: Gruemila RE-MILA
description: Join us and run in Norway's fastest half marathon course! The maximum time for the half marathon is 2:30 hours due to train crossings. There will be pacers for finish times ranging from 1:10 to 2:15. All participants will receive a finisher medal, and there are cash prizes sponsored by Grue Sparebank for the top three places in both the women's and men's categories, as well as a prize for the course record.

name: Bjoa Halvmaraton
description: Bjoa Half Marathon is an annual event that follows the same course and setup as in previous years. This is the fifth year, and extra attention will be given to runners who have participated all five years. New this year is a prize of 5000 NOK for the course record, with the current record for men at 1 hour 13 minutes 49 seconds and for women at 1 hour 24 minutes 16 seconds. The race starts at 11:00 from Bjoa stadium, and the course is certified and measured by a certified course measurer. Medal to all finishers.
course_highlights: There will be special recognition for runners who have completed all 5 years.
New this year is 5000 NOK for the course record.
The course is officially measured and approved by a certified course measurer, and a medal will be awarded to all finishers.

name: Gaular 3000
description: Gaular 3000 is a race that takes place around Sande, starting at the Spar store, heading towards the stadium and Døskeland Marine. The course goes over the bridge and back past the church, finishing at the bus stop. The loop is officially measured at 3 km and starts at 3:30 PM, open to everyone aged 11 and older. Additionally, there will be a children's race at Øyra, as well as activities on the new running track at the stadium with various athletics events before the main race.
course_highlights: The race is officially measured at 3 km.
Start at 3:30 PM and open to everyone aged 11 and older.
There will be a children's race held at Øyra or activities on the new running track at the stadium.
