name: Hydro Rundt Øvre Årdal
description: The athletics group invites you to Hydro Rundt on Saturday, September 14. The recreational class starts at 12 PM, while active runners begin at 1 PM. Both races have their start and finish at the square in Øvre Årdal, with an entry fee of 100 NOK for the recreational class and 200 NOK for the active class.
course_highlights: Recreational class from 12 PM and active participants starting at 1 PM.
Start and finish at the square in Øvre Årdal.
Participant fee of 100 NOK for recreational and 200 NOK for competitive.

name: Årefjorden Rundt
description: Årefjorden Rundt will be held on Saturday, September 28, starting from Rygge Youth School at 1 PM. The race features distances of 13 km and 8.3 km and is part of the Mossekarusellen, which includes several other races. The terrain for Årefjorden Rundt is primarily off-road and gravel, with some asphalt. The best way to view the race map is on a PC, as there are issues with mobile devices and tablets.
course_highlights: Årefjorden Rundt is part of the Mossekarusellen, which consists of 4 races: the Albyløpet at 3 km, the Ekholtløpet at approximately 7 km, the Kambomila at approximately 10 km, and Årefjorden Rundt at 13 km.
The race takes place in both Moss and Rygge, and the terrain is mainly trail/gravel, but with some asphalt around Årefjorden.
There is a mass start for the participants, which provides an exciting and social experience.

name: Gaia Backyard Hafjell
description: Gaia Backyard Hafjell is a scenic and hilly course that starts from the sports store at Gaia, goes out on Nysætervegen, and then into the ski trail towards Pellestova. The course climbs towards the weather radar located 1080 meters above sea level, goes around the radar, and continues to the cairn at Hafjelltoppen. The race is 6.7 km long, and the start is every full hour – you must return before the hour is up to continue. In 2024, there were nearly 30 runners who started on lap 12 and thus ran a total of 80 km.
course_highlights: The course goes around the radar and then towards the cairn at Hafjelltoppen.
The race takes place on a scenic, hilly course of 6.7 km featuring grass, gravel, and trails.
The start is every full hour – you must return before the hour is up to continue.

name: Nattland Backyard Ultra
description: Nattland Backyard Ultra is a challenging ultramarathon where participants run a lap of 6.7 km (6706 meters) within an hour, with new laps starting at the top of every hour. The race continues until there is only one participant left who completes a lap. Although the ultimate goal is to reach 80.4 km, everyone is welcome to run as many laps as they wish – or can handle. In 2026, the race will take place at Nordre Nattlandsfjellet in Bergen, Hordaland.
course_highlights: Backyard running is a loop of 6.7 km that is run up to twelve times.
The laps start every hour on the hour, and your pace determines how long of a break you get before the next start.
Participants can run as many laps as they wish, with one participant needing to finish in order to win.

name: Lierløpet 10 km
description: Lierløpet is one of Norway's fastest courses, and the race takes place on a wide pathway that is well-used by runners and joggers in the Drammen area. With a distance of 10 km, this race offers a great opportunity for both experienced runners and beginners to test their skills.
course_highlights: Lierløpet is one of Norway's fastest courses.
The race takes place on a wide pathway.
The race is well-utilized by runners and recreational athletes in the Drammen area.

name: Ørsjødilten
description: We warmly welcome everyone to this year's "ØRSJØ-DILT". The race takes place at Prestebakke and has been organized for 40 years, attracting participants of all ages. The participants run the first 2.5 km together with the 8 and 21 km routes, around the football field and the lit trail, before continuing on gravel and finishing with 1.5 km in terrain. There is a lot of beautiful nature along Ørsjøen, and it is a fantastic opportunity for both locals and visitors to take part in an inclusive and enjoyable event.
course_highlights: The runners start with a lap around the football field and then 1.9 km of hilly terrain in the lighted trail.
There is an elevation gain of 60 m at the end of the 5.5 km gravel section.
Drinks and bananas are available at 6, 12, and 15 km.

name: Loddefjordløpet
description: The Loddefjord Race is an annual event that takes place in Bergen, Hordaland, and has been organized by Loddefjord IL Athletics for over 40 years. This year's race event will be held on Sunday, September 22, starting at 10:00 in Alvøen Sports Park. The race offers a varied and scenic route suitable for both beginners and experienced runners, with distances of 5 km, 2 km, and a free children's race of 400 m for grades 1-4. We aim to create an inclusive low-threshold running festival that inspires physical activity for children and families throughout western Bergen.
course_highlights: The Loddefjord Race has been held for over 40 years and offers a scenic route through beautiful areas in Loddefjord.
The children's race of 400m for grades 1-4 is completely free to participate in, and all children receive a medal for their effort.
The event has distances of 5 km and 2 km, making it accessible for both experienced runners and beginners.

name: Borredalsløpet
description: Borredalsløpet is a 10 km race that takes place on gravel roads and some on mountain trails in Fredrikstadmarka. The first race was held in 1988, and since then the courses have remained the same, although the names of the races and the locations for the start and finish have varied. In 2014, the first race that went in the opposite direction was organized. The best man ran it in 21:40, while the best woman completed the 5.6-kilometer stretch in 29:41.
course_highlights: The first race was held in 1988.
The courses have been the same, but the names of the races and the locations for the start and finish have varied.
The next race is on May 6, 2025, at 6:30 PM.

name: Oslo Trail Challenge
description: Oslo Trail Challenge is a trail ultramarathon in the forest areas of Nordmarka, Lillomarka, and Romeriksåsen north of Oslo city center. Welcome to the Oslo Trail Challenge from September 27-29, 2024. The trails are unmarked, and you are responsible for navigating to stay on course, either by using GPS tracks or paper maps. Participants can choose between distances of 200 km, 100 km, and 55 km.
course_highlights: The trails are not marked, and you are responsible for navigating to stay on course, either by using a GPS track or a paper map.
Oslo Trail Challenge takes place in the beautiful forest areas of Nordmarka, Lillomarka, and Romeriksåsen.

name: Tekna Veldedighetsløp
description:
The charity run is being organized for the second year in a row and will take place on September 28th. This year, just like last year, we want to highlight the importance of students' mental health. Mental health is a topic that never goes out of date, and we must continue to work on it so that we can constantly improve our ability to tackle the challenges that everyday life presents to us.

We want to support and shed light on the services provided by Mental Helse Ungdom with the funds we manage to raise. The registration fee paid upon signing up goes entirely to Mental Helse Ungdom.

Although we are running to benefit students' mental health, we want to invite adults of all ages to join in and run. The course will be set around the large Lungegårdsvann – a distance that is manageable regardless of fitness level. Participants can choose whether they want to run, walk, or contribute as cheerleaders.

Join us and use your legs for a good cause!
course_highlights: The charity run brings together students and other fitness enthusiasts for a race to support Mental Health Youth.
The event emphasizes the importance of students' mental health.
Join a meaningful running experience in the beautiful surroundings around Store Lungegårdsvann.

name: RE-MILA
description: RE-MILA is a fun run for absolutely everyone, with distances of 2.5 km, 5 km, and 10 km. The race starts at 2:00 PM with a children's race for the youngest, followed by the 2.5 km at 2:30 PM and a mass start for the 5 km and 10 km at 3:00 PM. Participants receive a medal upon finishing, and there are prizes for category winners and the best runners in each distance. All distances start and finish in Revetal town center, and parking is free.
course_highlights: RE-MILA follows Kondis' recommended class division for all distances.
The secretariat will be near the park/parking lot by the Sport1 store.
Registration for RE-MILA 2025 – Children's Race (600m and 2.5 km) opens in August.

name: Øygardskarusellen 6
description: Welcome to the race carousel taking place in beautiful Øygarden. The race is suitable for children and adults of all ages, where you can be active together, be social, win cool prizes, and have fun. The races will take place over 6 Mondays, with three races in the spring and three in the fall. In 2025, a total of 6 race carousels will be held, starting at 7:00 PM, and the 900-meter race will start at 6:30 PM for children born in 2017 and later.
course_highlights: The race is suitable for children and adults of all ages.
The races take place over 6 Mondays, with three races in the spring and three in the fall.
Stay in shape throughout the year with us!

name: Hønefoss 5 km
description: Hønefoss 5 km is an easy and fast course, officially measured by Kondis in June 2018, where many participants achieve personal records. The route mostly runs along the picturesque Storelva, with its highest point in Søndre Park, where runners are greeted by lively music from Hallingby School Band. The course consists of approximately 3 km of trail/gravel road and 2 km of asphalt, making it ideal for both beginners and experienced runners.
course_highlights: The course was officially measured by Kondis in June 2018.
It is an easy and fast course where many achieve personal bests.
Most of the route runs along the idyllic Storelva and has its highest point in Søndre Park.

name: Sjusjøløpet
description: On Saturday, August 9th, the Sjusjøløpet will take place from the Sjusjøen Cross-Country Arena, and many cross-country skiers are expected at the starting line. This race, which is being held for the second time after a successful debut in 2013, offers two distances: Sollifjellet Rundt at 21.5 kilometers and Sjusjøvannet Rundt at 10.5 kilometers. The courses traverse scenic areas such as Sollifjell, Mostefjell, and Snørrvillen, with the start and finish at the Sjusjøen Cross-Country Arena. The organizing committee wishes everyone good luck and hopes for high participation.
course_highlights: The Sjusjøløpet offers a choice between two distances: Sollifjellet Rundt at 21.5 kilometers and Sjusjøvannet Rundt at 10.5 kilometers.
The trails traverse some of the mountains surrounding the sports venue; Sollifjell, Mostefjell, and Snørvillen, offering fantastic views.
Many strong cross-country skiers are expected at the start, and last year's race had a great atmosphere despite manual timing.

name: Hanatrappene Opp
description: Hanatrappene Up is a mountain race taking place on Sunday, October 27th at 12:00 in Sandnes. The race ascends the 306 steps to Hanafjedle, which is likely Northern Europe's longest outdoor staircase and a popular training destination. The staircase was completed in 1955 and connects the old Hana school with the sports facility. Sandnes Idrettslag is proud to invite you to this unique race in the historic stairs.
course_highlights: The race goes up 306 steps straight up to Hanafjedle.
The stairs are a popular target for training sessions and are defined as a school route.
The record for the race, set by Torbjørn Fjeld eleven years ago, is 0:52.8 and still stands.

name: Nesbyen Backyard
description:
Nesbyen Backyard 6- and 12-Hour  
Detailed info at runnershei.com  

Date and location: October 4, Nesbyen, Hallingdal. Start at Nesbyen Sports Hall at 10:00 AM.  

Format: 6 or 12-hour Backyard run. Participants must complete a 6.7 km loop every hour to continue. The course is flat and fast, primarily on asphalt with sections of gravel and trail.  

Registration:  

- 490 NOK until April 30, 2025  
- 590 NOK until June 30, 2025  
- 690 NOK until August 31, 2025  
- 750 NOK until registration closes on September 15, 2025  

Transport:  

- Car: Via national road 7. 2 hours drive from Oslo and Drammen, 1 hour 15 minutes from Hønefoss and Fagernes, 1 hour from Rødberg and Geilo  
- Train: Bergen Line, 20-minute walk from the station to the sports hall  
- Bus: Check VY for timetables  

Prizes:  

- Prize for all who complete one loop, and the seventh loop (optional for 6 hours)  
- The three best in each category + top 3 overall (last loop and average speed)  
- Drawing of 20+ raffle prizes from local sponsors  

Contact:  

- Phone: +47 400 98 514  
- Email: hei@runnershei.com
course_highlights: October in Nesbyen provides a fresh and exciting backdrop, with temperatures ranging from 0-15 °C.
For those participating in the 12-hour format, the final hours of the race will take place in twilight and darkness, providing a magical experience under the starry sky.
Headlamps and reflective gear are mandatory for the darker hours, which both ensures the safety of participants and adds an extra dimension to the running experience.

name: Bèrghem Ultra Marathon
description: Bèrghem Ultra Trail is our classic trail running event, offering a range of trail running distances, all set against the stunning backdrop of Hedmarksvidda. This area is home to some of Norway's untouched forests and a well-known witch mountain. Runners can expect a mix of marked trails and marked/unmarked gravel roads, but the real challenge lies in the bogs and wetlands that dominate the entire region. Don't be fooled by the low profile - this terrain is some of the toughest in Norway.
course_highlights: Hedmarksvidda is home to some of Norway's untouched forests, as well as a famous witch mountain.
Runners can find a mix of marked trails and marked/unmarked gravel roads.
The real challenge is the bogs and wetlands that dominate the entire area.

name: Tyin Filefjell Extreme
description: The mountain race Tyin Filefjell Extreme 2024 takes place in majestic surroundings with a route over the mountains Skørsnøse, Støgonøse, and Børrenøse. The race has a total distance of 21 km and an elevation gain of 1050 meters, with the highest point at 1455 meters above sea level. This event is part of the Mountain Festival at Tyin Filefjell, where there will also be an exciting program with activities and experiences for both young and old. The mountains are at their most beautiful at this time of year, so bring your friends and family for a weekend filled with nature experiences, play, and fun.
course_highlights: The extreme distance takes place in majestic surroundings with a route over the mountains Skørsnøse, Støgonøse, and Børrenøse.
A total of 21 km and 1050 meters of elevation gain, with the highest point at 1455 meters above sea level.

course_highlights: Enjoy Gausta's beautiful autumn colors in this 6 km race around Kvitåvatn.

name: Sørfjorden Halvmaraton
description: The Sørfjorden Half Marathon is one of the nicest races to participate in Norway. Join in on the great atmosphere as 800 runners head out to race along Sørfjorden. The course is on smooth, newly laid asphalt in beautiful surroundings and is relatively flat and easy to run. You'll be cheered on along the route by many spectators with flags and music, making it perhaps the most enjoyable race of the year to be a part of.
course_highlights: The course runs on nice newly laid asphalt in beautiful surroundings and is relatively flat and easy to run.
You are cheered on along the course by many spectators with flags and music.

description: Flisa Backyard in Flisa, Innlandet, was a success, with participants running lap after lap in gusty winds and rain. At 5:40 AM on Sunday morning, Glenn Hjortefot (45) crossed the finish line after an impressive 21 laps. This event attracted significant interest and proved to be a challenging experience for all participants.

name: Norgesløpet - UKI 6. løp
description: Welcome to the Norway Race on Sunday, October 4, 2026, in Jessheim. The course was updated in 2025 with a flatter route and fewer elevation meters, making it faster with fewer turns. It consists of two loops of 5 km each, providing a more spectator-friendly and traffic-safe course. The start for the Norway Race 5 km is at 11:00, while the 10 km starts at 12:00, followed by the children's race at 12:10.

Faster course with fewer turns.

name: Norgesløpet
description: The Norway Run takes place on Sunday, October 4, 2026, in Jessheim. The race starts with the Norway Run at 5 km at 11:00 AM, and there will also be a children's race and entertainment for the kids! Don't feel like running? Then you can enjoy a day of good vibes with the family, featuring visits from Fantorangen and the NRK Super Bus. In collaboration with the family festival A Walk in the Park, we offer free childcare for children aged 4 to 12 while the adults run, with children's races available at 11:30 AM and 2:00 PM.

The race courses in and around Jessheim city center are flat and easy to run on, primarily consisting of asphalt.

The course is well-suited for strollers and motorized wheelchairs.

description: The Autumn Personal Record Marathon takes place on October 5, 2025, starting at 10:00 AM. The race offers several distances: 5 km, 10 km, Half Marathon, Marathon, and 50 km. The course is fast and flat, designed for records, and is AIMS-certified. The core idea of the race is that you compete against yourself and your own personal record, with a personal record percentage typically ranging from 30-40%.

name: Sørlandstesten Løp 2
description: The Sørlandstest is a new low-threshold offering for happy recreational runners of all levels. The start and finish are on the other side of the road from Gumpens Auto, along Setesdalsveien in Kristiansand. Participants follow a flat and fast course up Setesdalsveien to Strai, turn around, and run back the same way. For those running 5 km, the turnaround point is after passing 2.5 km.
course_highlights: The Sørlandstest is a new low-threshold offering for happy recreational runners at all levels.
The participants follow a flat and fast course up Setesdalsveien to Strai.
For those running 5 km, you turn around after passing 2.5 km.

images.alt_text: Runners in the Sørlandstesten race.
Runners preparing for a race.
Runners training together on a paved road in fine weather.
Runners in the Sørlandstest, a road race in Kristiansand.

name: Kristins Runde
description: Kristins Runde (Oslo 50 Miles Trail Run) is a race that takes place in Norway and was rediscovered by an enthusiast in 2005. The race, which spans 81.5 km, offers a scenic route with varied terrain and beautiful views. It is a unique experience for both experienced runners and beginners in ultrarunning, providing participants the opportunity to experience one of the most impressive trails in the region.
course_highlights: The race is known for its scenic course that stretches over 50 miles.
Participants will have the opportunity to experience varied terrain and beautiful views.
Kristin's Loop has a total elevation gain of 1,742 meters, providing a challenging experience for the participants.

images.alt_text: Scenic landscape with trees and water, perfect for trail running.
Runners gathered before the cross-country race. Clothing and gear indicate ultrarunning. A watch in the background shows the time.
Running on a trail with poles and a backpack. Perfect for Kristin's Round trail race.
Runners in Kristins Runde trail race in Norway, with forest and weather.

name: Furumomila
description: This year, Furumomila is being held for the 41st time, and we hope that as many people as possible want to participate. There are great cash prizes, gift cards, medals, and pins distributed to all our participants. Furumomila is not just a 10 km trail run, but also includes MiniMil, a hiking march, and SpareBank1 Modum's trail run.
course_highlights: Great cash prizes, gift cards, medals, and pins awarded to all our participants.
Furumomila includes several distances such as the 10 km trail run, MiniMil, and hiking march.
The event is a family event that attracts participants of all ages.

images.alt_text: Furumomila 2025: Children are running in a cross-country race. Beautiful autumn weather.
Two trail runners. Good quality of the image.
Runners in action during the Furumomila cross-country race. Many participants of different ages.
The start of the Furumomila cross-country race. Many runners in action.

name: Kystløpet
description: Kystløpet 2023 will take place on Saturday, October 11 at 2:00 PM, starting from the old railway path in Egersund. This is a popular race that attracts both experienced runners and beginners, and participants will experience beautiful coastal landscapes while competing. The event aims to include more women, which has been a success, and the proceeds go to good causes such as the Fyrlyssenteret.
course_highlights: Around 150 participants ran the "Kystløpet" on Saturday.
11 km challenging course in beautiful coastal landscape, a race known for its excellent homemade baked goods.
The entry fee goes to charitable purposes.

images.alt_text: Runners in the Coastal Run. Great atmosphere and beautiful nature.
Runners at the Kystløpet 2023. Beautiful autumn weather.
Coastal Race 2025: Runners in action, sponsor logos, and race information.
Runners at the Coastal Run. Great atmosphere and a beautiful course.

name: Hamar Backyard Ultra 50M
description: Hamar Backyard Ultra 50M is a running competition organized according to the "Backyard" principle, originating from Big's Backyard Ultra in Tennessee, USA. The course is 6706 meters long and must be completed once every hour; anyone who fails to meet the deadline for the next start is out. The competition has a maximum duration of 12 hours, allowing for a maximum distance of 80467 meters, equivalent to nearly two marathons. The winner is determined by the fastest time on the last lap if multiple participants finish.
course_highlights: The course is 6706 meters long, and it is necessary to complete one lap every hour in order to continue in the competition.
The maximum distance in the Hamar Backyard Ultra 50M is 80,467 meters, which is just over 8 miles.
The winner is determined by the fastest time on the last lap if multiple participants complete the same number of laps.

images.alt_text: Runners at Hamar Backyard Ultra 50M are racing towards the finish line, with a HOKA arch in the background.
Runners in a race through the forest.
Runners on the trail in the forest with race numbers on their chests.
Runner on a trail in the forest.

name: Ivar Formos Minneløp
description: Ivar Formo's Memorial Run is a sweaty delight for everyone in the best that Nordmarka has to offer in nature. This race is for both children and adults, featuring a new 10 km course on beautiful trails in the woods that are both gentle and challenging. The start and finish for the courses are at Sognsvann Snow Park, where participants can choose between distances of 17 km, 10 km, 3 km, and a children's race.
course_highlights: The trails include scenic paths from Sognsvann Snow Park, through Båntjern, Vettakollen, and several other beautiful locations in Nordmarka.
It is possible to register for the race on the day, and timing will be conducted for most distances, except for the children's race.
Participants must have a license from the Athletics Federation or purchase a one-time license, and there is a chip in the bib number for timing.

images.alt_text: Children are running in a cross-country race on grass.
Runner in cross-country race, visible bib number, running in Nordmarka, Ivar Formo's Memorial Run.
Runners in cross-country running in Nordmarka, with race numbers and nature.
Children in the starting area for a cross-country race, ready to run and smiling.

name: Kruke's Ultra-Trail Challenge
description: Kruke's Ultra-Trail Challenge (KUTC) challenges you to run a loop from Saksvik to Solemsvåttan as many times as possible within given time limits. Test your own limits! Complete it 4 times to participate in the 'fun run', 7 times to become a true ultra-runner (> 42.2 km), and 8, 12, or 15 times to reach classic ultra distances of 50 km, 50 miles, or 100 km. Do it 24 times to run 100 miles, climb Mount Everest... and become a legend! The race takes place on the third Saturday in October, but deviations may occur.
course_highlights: Test your own limits! Do it 4 times to participate in the 'fun run'.
Ready 7 times to become a true ultra-runner (> 26.2 miles).
Ready for 25 laps to achieve the maximum six ITRA points!

images.alt_text: Trail runners. Forest and terrain. Running competition.
Course map with distance and elevation for a trail race.

name: Nøklevann Rundt
description: Nøklevann Rundt was held for the 43rd time on Saturday, October 12, 2024. The race has usually been blessed with brilliant weather, but this year, the weather gods were not on the organizer's or participants' side. The rain started around the same time as the 5-kilometer race, and the cold downpour only intensified throughout the afternoon. However, the racing conditions were OK with the right gear, and many strong times were achieved. As usual, the event was smoothly guided to port by the experienced and friendly staff.
course_highlights: Nøklevann Rundt is a short, easy, and child-friendly hike in a popular outdoor area in Østmarka.
The race takes you past beautiful swimming spots like Ulsrudvannet and Rustadsaga, where there are opportunities to enjoy the sun and water.
It is a beautiful route with historical roads such as Sarabråtveien, established in 1856, and Korketrekkeren, which provides a unique experience of the Marka.

images.alt_text: Runner on the trail by the water in Nøklevann Rundt.
Runners in full speed during the Nøklevann Rundt trail race.
Runners with bib numbers and race gear from Nøklevann Rundt.
People gathered at a running event, with a building in the background and children on bicycles.

name: Bergensløpet Høst
description: Bergensløpet Høst is a beautiful autumn race in picturesque surroundings. The course runs through the stunning landscape of Bergen, featuring both forest and open fields. Participants can expect a varied and challenging route, suitable for both beginners and experienced runners.
course_highlights: The course runs through the beautiful landscape of Bergen, with both forest and open fields.
Participants can expect a varied and challenging course.
The race is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners.

name: Perseløpet Maraton Høst
description: The Perseløpet Marathon Autumn takes place on October 4th in Ringerike and offers several distances for participants, including 3 km, 5 km, 10 km, half marathon, and marathon. The race features a fast and flat course designed for records and is AIMS certified. This event provides both beginners and experienced runners a great opportunity to challenge themselves in a beautiful autumn setting, with scenic areas along the route.
course_highlights: Fast and flat course, designed for records.
AIMS-certified course.
Results available immediately after finishing.

images.alt_text: Runners in the Perseløpet marathon autumn.
Runners in the Perseløpet marathon autumn. Men are running on paved roads with nature in the background.
Runners at a marathon in Lillestrøm.
Running on an asphalt road, smiling and waving at the camera.

name: Nesodden på langs
description: Nesodden Long Run is a trail race that takes place annually on Nesodden in early October. In 2025, the race will be held on October 12, with the starting gun at 12:00 for all distances. Participants can choose between three distances: Hardhausen (approximately 13.4 km from Myklerud to Berger Stadium), Styrkeprøven (approximately 6 km from Gaupefjell to Berger Stadium), and Bånn pine (approximately 3 km from To gård to Berger Stadium). This race is known for its fantastic conditions and a really tough course.
course_highlights: NPL is a race that people love, with nearly 500 participants who enjoyed a wonderful journey along the route.
Fantastic conditions along Nesodden make it a popular event.
There is expected to be fierce competition in the toughest part of the course, which adds extra excitement to the race.

images.alt_text: Runners in cross country with bib numbers and smiles.
Runners in cross country, crossing a finish line. Several participants with bib numbers on their chests.
Runner in trail running, Nesodden lengthwise.

name: Rosa Sløyfe Løpet Oslo
description: The Pink Ribbon Run is returning to Tiger City to paint the town pink in October! The start and finish are at the square in Nydalen for the short course of 2.2 km, while the long course of 5 km starts in Vaterlandsparken and follows the scenic stretch along the Akerselva river. For the tenth year, this run aims to raise awareness for breast cancer, and the proceeds go to the Pink Ribbon campaign and their research on breast cancer. It’s not about how fast you run, but about spreading awareness for an important cause and showing solidarity with those affected.
course_highlights: Join us and experience the sea of pink together with thousands of others who want to support the good cause.
Half of the entry fee goes directly to the breast cancer cause, and the race is a powerful symbol of solidarity and unity.
Even though breast cancer is a serious matter, this day is one where we can celebrate life and show that we are there for each other.

images.alt_text: Participants in the Pink Ribbon Run in Oslo run with their arms in the air.
Two men at the Pink Ribbon Run with medals and smiles, to support the breast cancer cause.
Pink Ribbon Run Oslo. Nighttime image of the event with pink decorations and people.
Map of the Rosa Sløyfe Run Oslo short course shows the start and finish and the route along the Akerselva.

name: Fevik Løbestævne
description: Fevik Running Competition is an annual race event held at Fevik Stadium, offering distances of 3,000, 5,000, and 10,000 meters. Everyone is welcome to participate, regardless of their level, and the event is known for its friendly atmosphere and good organization. The race provides a great opportunity for both beginners and experienced runners to compete in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: Everyone is welcome to run 3,000, 5,000, and 10,000 meters on Sunday, October 12 at Fevik Stadium.
The race features a beautiful course that takes participants through scenic areas, and it is known for its friendly atmosphere and excellent organization.
Registration takes place before the start and is free, and everyone receives an official time.

images.alt_text: Runners ready for the start of the Fevik half marathon.
The runner receives flowers after the Fevik Half Marathon. Congratulations!
Runners at the starting line of the Fevik running competition.

name: NM Terrengløp Lang Løype
description: We welcome you to the Norwegian Championships in cross-country running long course at Nordbytjernet, Jessheim! The course consists of a 1.5 km loop that will be run multiple times depending on the distance. This championship has showcased a high level in most categories, with exciting competitions, especially in the senior classes.
course_highlights: It was delivered at a high level in most categories, and it was exciting in both senior classes.
Strindheim's Hanne Mjøen Maridal pulled ahead of Ina Halle Haugen from Runar and Tjalve runners Maria Sagnes Wågan and Ingeborg Østgård.
There were favorite victories at today's Norwegian Championship in long-distance cross-country running in Skien, with clear wins for Filip Ingebrigtsen and Karoline Bjerkeli Grøvdal.

name: Vinterkarusellen 1.løp
description: Necon Winter Carousel has reached the final race of the season, and it looks like there will be good conditions this evening. Ålesund Winter Carousel consists of 5 races held during the winter months, featuring varied distances; the main course is 10 km, while the 5 km distance turns around halfway. The races are tailored for both beginners and experienced runners, providing a great opportunity to stay active throughout the winter.
course_highlights: Remember to collect your medal after completing a minimum of 5 races.
The courses are tailored for both beginners and experienced runners.
There are varied distances; the main course is 10 km, while the 5 km distance turns around halfway.

images.alt_text: Runners in winter races with bib numbers, snow on the ground.
Runners in winter races with bib numbers.
Runners at the starting line for a winter race.
Runner in winter race.

name: Vorlauf zum Harz-Gebirgslauf
description: The warm-up for the Harz Mountain Run is a free test run held one week before the main race. It gives runners the opportunity to check their fitness and get to know the Harz Mountain Run courses. Everyone starts together at 9:30 a.m. in Himmelpforte, Wernigerode, with distances of 2 km, 5 km, 11 km and 22 km. Participants are welcomed at the finish with tea and lard bread. No registration is required, but the courses are not yet marked.
course_highlights: Mass start at 9:30 a.m. in Himmelpforte, Wernigerode
Distances: 2 km, 5 km, 11 km and 22 km
Free entry; no registration required
additional: Participation is free and registration is not required. The courses are not yet marked. Tea and lard bread are served at the finish. Courses not yet marked, free participation, no registration required, including children's and family runs during the main race weekend.

name: 25. Volkslauf um den Altwarmbüchener See
description: The Volkslauf around Lake Altwarmbüchen is part of the Sparkassen Laufpass of the Hanover Region, one of Germany’s largest running series, with 43 events in 2026. The race gives runners the opportunity to discover the Hanover Region on foot and take part in a varied range of running events. Every participation is rewarded with a stamp in the Laufpass, which is available in both digital and traditional formats. The event is aimed at recreational runners and promotes active movement in the region.
course_highlights: Loop course around Lake Altwarmbüchen
Scenic route in the Hanover Region
Part of a large running series with a wide range of events
additional: Participation is rewarded with a stamp in the Laufpass, also available digitally via the Laufpass app. The app offers an event calendar, a digital running diary and further information. The Volkslauf is part of a series of 43 running events in the Hanover Region. Running event in Altwarmbüchen; on-site registration possible; race on 01.03.2026; part of the Laufpass series; various distances, including 1.6 km, 3.6 km, 7.2 km and 10.8 km.

name: Brakelsieker Volkslauf "Am Fuße des Mörths"
location: Sportplatz Brakelsiek, Schieder-Schwalenberg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The Brakelsieker Volkslauf “Am Fuße des Mörths” is a traditional local running, walking and Nordic walking event in Schieder-Schwalenberg, held on a Saturday afternoon in October. It offers a range of distances for adults and young people, including 5 km, 9 km and 15 km runs, as well as 5 km and 9 km walking and Nordic walking. The start and finish are at the Brakelsiek sports ground, and the course runs around the village sports ground, with a gently rolling, rural profile at the foot of the Mörth. The event is a lovely opportunity to enjoy the autumn scenery in a relaxed atmosphere.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the Brakelsiek sports ground
Loop around the village sports ground; not a point-to-point course
Gently rolling course with a rural profile at the foot of the Mörth
additional: Running, walking and Nordic walking distances are offered for adults and young people. Typical October weather is around 14 °C, with a low of 6 °C and mostly cloudy skies. The course is not considered a tough mountain route, but has moderate elevation gain. Running and walking events; start and finish at the Brakelsiek sports ground; gently rolling course; rural profile.

name: Parforceheide Crosslauf
location: Sportplatz an der Heinrich-Zille-Straße, Stahnsdorf, Brandenburg, Germany
description: The Parforceheide Cross-Country Run has been organized by RSV Eintracht 1949 in Stahnsdorf since 2008, giving recreational runners from the region the chance to discover the varied landscape of the Parforceheide. The course starts at the sports ground on Heinrich-Zille-Straße and passes the Südwestfriedhof cemetery, winding through woodland and natural terrain with small climbs, sandy sections, and stretches of asphalt and cobblestones. Races are offered over 1 km (Bambini), 3 km (schoolchildren), 5 km, and 10 km for young people and adults. After the race, the organizer provides refreshments, and football matches often take place at the sports ground, making for an enjoyable day of sport for participants and spectators.
course_highlights: Course through the Parforceheide, with woodland and natural sections
Varied surfaces: sand, asphalt, and cobblestones
Small climbs add challenge and variety
additional: Races are available for various age groups and distances: Bambini race (1 km), schoolchildren’s race (3 km), and 5 km and 10 km races for young people and adults. Refreshments are provided at the sports ground after the race. The event is part of the Mittelmark Cup and is supported by many volunteers. Football matches are often played on the artificial turf afterward, rounding out the day for families and spectators. Terrain with climbs, sandy sections, asphalt, cobblestones. Registration at www.ziel-zeit.de

name: Solvay Lauf
description: The Solvay Run Bernburg is a 5 km race in Bernburg, Saxony-Anhalt, taking place on October 10, 2026. The start is at Krumbholzallee 8 at 10:00 a.m. The race is part of the Solvay Cup and combines cross-country and road running, so it is not a simple, flat city course. It is aimed mainly at local clubs and usually attracts 100 to 300 runners. The event offers professional timing, online results, certificates, showers, changing rooms, parking, free bag drop and refreshments at the finish.
course_highlights: 5 km course combining cross-country and road running
Start at Krumbholzallee 8 in Bernburg
Local race with a manageable field of 100–300 runners
additional: Registration is available online, in person in advance or on site on race day. Chip timing by race result, online results and start lists, photos and reports, printed and online certificates, showers, changing rooms, parking, free bag drop and refreshments at the finish. Typical October weather: around 14 °C, mostly cloudy with 40 mm of precipitation. This is not a major event, but a local race that typically attracts 100 to 300 participants. In addition to the race, it offers a friendly atmosphere with refreshments, showers and parking.

name: Viersener Herbstwaldlauf Rund um den Bismarckturm
description: The 79th Viersen Autumn Forest Run Around the Bismarck Tower takes place on 10 October 2026 in Viersen. The event offers a 5 km run for adults on a hilly course, with a time limit of one hour. There is also a 7.25 km Walking & Nordic Walking event. The age limits are 14 to 99 for the run and 10 to 99 for walking. This traditional event is aimed at runners and walkers looking for a challenging course through autumn woodland.
course_highlights: Hilly course
Around the Bismarck Tower
One-hour time limit for the 5 km run
additional: There are events for children and young people; further information is available in the organiser’s official race announcement. All events share the same start and finish, but the exact locations are only shown with RUNME Premium. Results are listed by age category, with categories assigned according to year of birth. There are several events with different distances, age categories and start times; young people aged 14 and over may participate. Results will be published on the website.

name: Volkslauf mit Walking um den AWB See
description: The 25th Volkslauf with walking around the AWB Lake is a local running and walking event in Altwarmbüchen, a district of Isernhagen. The event offers short, flat distances around Altwarmbüchener See, with one lap measuring approximately 3.66 km. There are various running and walking routes for adults, as well as races for children and young people, making it a community running experience for the whole region. The start and finish are at Seestraße 23, and the races take place in the afternoon.
course_highlights: Flat route around Altwarmbüchener See
Lap of approximately 3.66 km
Running and Nordic walking options
additional: The races start in the afternoon in the following order: first the 3.6 km run, then the walkers, followed by the 7.2 km run for adults. The event is more of a community running day for the town than a single main race. Typical October weather is around 14 °C, with a low of 6 °C and mostly cloudy skies. Distances range from 1.6 km to 10.8 km; flat terrain; running and walking events; races for children and young people; date: 10 October 2026.

name: Berliner Morgenpost Great 10K
price_range: 25,00 € bis 70,00 € je nach Strecke und Anmeldedatum
description: The Berliner Morgenpost Great 10K is Berlin’s fastest 10 km race, starting in front of Charlottenburg Palace. The route passes through Berlin Zoo and offers a unique running experience in the capital. In addition to the classic 10-kilometre race, there is also a 2 x 5 km relay and a 4.2 km short course from the zoo to Charlottenburg Palace. The event is suitable for all abilities and age groups, offering a large running festival for the whole family.
course_highlights: Start in front of Charlottenburg Palace
The route passes through Berlin Zoo
Running festival on the forecourt of Charlottenburg Palace
additional: Chip timing with a transponder attached to your shoe, refreshment stations and toilets along the route, pacemakers for the 10 km and short course, online certificate with your personal result, BVG tickets for relay runners, bag transport from the start to the finish, medal engraving and event shirts available as add-ons, HD finish-line video available to purchase, children’s and Bambini races for those born between 2014 and 2021. Distances: 10 km, 4.2 km, children’s and Bambini races, relay events; registration until 20.10.2024; start in front of Berlin Zoo, finish at Charlottenburg Palace; event extras such as medal engraving, photos and videos available.

name: 19. Burger-Rolandlauf
description: The Burger Roland Run is a traditional race that normally takes place in Burg and is jointly organized by Rolandgymnasium Burg and LG Ihleläufer Burg. The course runs through the town along the Ihle, through the forest and past the Bismarck Tower, finishing in the school courtyard. Alongside the competition, participants can enjoy a varied supporting program with music, activities for children and refreshments. In 2026, the event in Burg was canceled because the necessary permit was not granted; a replacement event will instead take place in Tangerhütte Town Park.
course_highlights: The course runs through the town of Burg along the Ihle
A forest section with views of the Bismarck Tower
Finish in the courtyard of Rolandgymnasium
additional: The traditional course in Burg was not approved for 2026. A replacement event will instead take place in Tangerhütte Town Park. Entry fees already paid can be refunded. After the race, there will be a supporting program with music, activities for children and refreshments. Cancellation in 2026, replacement event in Tangerhütte, course through Burg, activities for children, bouncy castle, refreshments

name: Frühstückslauf
description: The breakfast run in Wernigerode is a group run without timing, starting at the market square and climbing to Wernigerode Castle. The route is about 3 kilometres long with 100 metres of elevation gain. The run takes place as a group and is free of charge. A small snack is served afterwards, making the run a sociable event.
course_highlights: Route about 3 km long
About 100 m of elevation gain
Group run uphill to Wernigerode Castle
additional: The run is free of charge, takes place as a group and is not timed. A small snack is served afterwards. Group run, no timing, snack afterwards.

name: H/21 Halbmarathon
description: The H/21 Half Marathon Hannover is a new event on the national running calendar, combining urban flair, modern beats and green stretches. The start and finish are in the heart of Hannover, and the route passes notable hotspots across the state capital. The event takes place in autumn and offers a unique running experience in a lively urban setting. Be there for the prologue as Hannover opens a new chapter in running history.
course_highlights: The route combines urban flair with green stretches
Start and finish in the heart of Hannover
The route passes notable hotspots in the state capital
additional: Check-in takes place on October 10, 2026, and the starting gun goes off on October 11, 2026. The event is an autumn highlight with urban flair and modern music. There are attractive side events, and the route is secured by course marshals. Participation is at your own risk, and DLV and IAAF regulations apply. Course in 2026: the 10 km route is run twice, followed later by the full half-marathon distance; registration is open until race day; a run with a modern atmosphere and music

name: Bad Hersfelder Lollslauf
description: The Bad Hersfeld Lollslauf is a traditional running event held annually in Bad Hersfeld, welcoming runners of all ages and ability levels. With distances ranging from the Bambini Run to the 10 km individual race, the Lollslauf offers a sporting challenge in beautiful surroundings. Alongside the competition, the event emphasizes community and the joy of running. It is a fixture on the running calendar and attracts participants from across Germany.
course_highlights: 500 m Bambini Run around the market square and Germany’s oldest folk festival
A range of courses from 500 m to 10 km, starting and finishing at Linggplatz
Run through the historic old town of Bad Hersfeld
additional: Start times: 1.3 km school race at 09:35, 5 km individual race at 10:00, 5 km team race at 10:10, 5 km Nordic walking at 11:30, 10 km individual race at 11:45, 500 m Bambini Run at 11:15. Certificates available as digital downloads; drinks in the finish area. Teams of 5–7 people can enter the team race. Prizes in kind for the overall winners. Multiple race categories; on-site registration available. Scenic course in Bad Hersfeld.

name: Burscheider Stadtlauf
location: Burscheid, Rheinisch-Bergischer Kreis, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The Burscheid City Run takes place on October 11, 2026, in the town center of Burscheid and offers an ideal setting for runners of all ability levels. There are several distances: the 10-kilometer main race, a 3-kilometer run, and an 800-meter run that serves as a qualification for the Sports Badge. The event has a friendly, family atmosphere and welcomes both competitive runners and recreational athletes. All finishers receive the traditional Kretzer City Run bread, and the top finishers are awarded special trophies.
course_highlights: 10-kilometer main race through the town center
3-kilometer run for recreational athletes
800-meter youth run as a qualification for the Sports Badge
additional: Late entries are possible at the registration office on race day for an additional fee of €5.00, but late registrants will not receive Kretzer City Run bread. Race packets will be distributed from 10:30 a.m. at the Protestant church. Changing rooms and showers are available at the “Auf dem Schulberg” sports hall. Free drinks are available along the course and at the finish. Age-group rankings follow DLO regulations. First aid is provided by the German Red Cross, Burscheid branch. Bib numbers must be worn on the chest. The event also includes children’s races, race-packet distribution from 10:30 a.m., online results, age-group rankings, medals, and trophies. October weather is usually mild, making participation comfortable.

name: Laubacher Ramsberglauf
price_range: bis 20. September vergünstigtes Startgeld, danach zzgl. Nachmeldegebühr
description: The Laubach Ramsberg Run is a traditional running event that starts and finishes in the picturesque castle park in Laubach. The event offers various distances for different age and ability groups, including a 10 km main race, a 5 km fun run, and races for schoolchildren and Bambini. The races feature a varied course through the beautiful countryside around Laubach. The organizers provide a welcoming atmosphere, with refreshments, changing facilities, and an awards ceremony right in the castle park.
course_highlights: Start and finish in Laubach Castle Park
A varied course through the countryside around Laubach
Refreshments and changing facilities at the Sports and Cultural Hall
additional: Registration is via RACERESULT, with a reduced entry fee available until 20 September; a late registration fee applies thereafter. Changing and shower facilities are available at the Sports and Cultural Hall. The awards ceremony takes place right in the castle park. Distances: 10 km main race, 5 km fun run, children’s races over 1500 m and 300 m; registration via Raceresult; start and finish in the castle park; refreshments, changing and shower facilities on site; October weather: approx. 14°C, cloudy

name: Porta Volkslauf
organizer: SC Nammen / SC Porta Westfalica Nammen e.V.
description: The 2026 Porta Fun Run is a long-standing running event in Porta Westfalica and has been a fixture on the regional running calendar for more than three decades. The event attracts runners of all ages, from competitive athletes to recreational runners. The route follows roads and field paths around the Nammen sports ground and through the Nammer Unterholz nature reserve, offering varied, flat sections with beautiful panoramic views of Porta. The race is part of the Mühlenkreisserie and takes place at the local sports facility in Nammen. The warm atmosphere and sense of community make it a special day.
course_highlights: Route along roads and field paths around the Nammen sports ground
Sections through the Nammer Unterholz nature reserve
Flat, varied sections with panoramic views of Porta

Courageous current and former cancer patients run 5 or 10 kilometers alongside their loved ones and healthcare providers to raise money for groundbreaking cancer research. Everyone is welcome to take part or support the participants, including people who have not had cancer themselves. The event combines an athletic challenge with a powerful message of hope and involvement.

The shorter distances (500 meters and 2 kilometers) take place on the grounds, while the longer distances (5 and 10 kilometers) go through the forest. Each distance has its own start time, and participants are advised to arrive at least half an hour before the start to collect their race bib.
course_highlights: 500-meter and 2-kilometer courses on the grounds of Parc Spelderholt
5- and 10-kilometer runs through the forest
Start and finish on the grounds of Parc Spelderholt
additional: Each distance has its own start time. Arrive at least half an hour before the start to collect your race bib. Parking is available at the entrance to the grounds. All ages can participate. Registration is available in advance and on the day; parking at Parc Spelderholt.

name: Vestingloop Edam
location: Vestingwerken Edam, Edam, North Holland, Netherlands
description: The Vestingloop Edam is a traditional running race held along Edam’s old fortifications. Since the first edition in 1954, when the distance was 5 kilometres, the route has remained a fixed feature despite changes to the distances. The race offers several distances, including children’s races, a 3-mile fun run and a 10 km race. The finish is on Baandervesting near the chain bridge, while the longer distances start on Noordervesting. The Vestingloop is known for its changeable weather and friendly atmosphere for both recreational and competitive runners.
course_highlights: Route along Edam’s old fortifications
Finish on Baandervesting, near the chain bridge
The 10 km and 3-mile races start on Noordervesting
additional: For the 10 km and 3-mile races, times are recorded using a chip attached to the race number. Children’s races use shoe chips. OJC participants can take part for free, but must report to registration to collect a shoe chip. Free parking is available, and showers are available in the changing rooms. Medals are awarded to the first three boys and girls in the children’s races. Cash prizes can be won in various age categories in the 10 km. Course along the old fortifications, registration via an online platform, free parking and showers available.

name: Culture Run Woerden
description: The Culture Run Woerden celebrates its fifth anniversary and is a unique fun run bringing together sport, culture and Woerden’s rich history. During this enjoyable run, you’ll discover the city centre in a surprising way, not only passing well-known places but also going right through iconic and cultural buildings. The combination of exercise, culture and Woerden’s characteristic sociable atmosphere makes this event popular with both residents and visitors. With two distances of 5 and 10 kilometres, suitable for walking or running, it’s accessible to all ages. The start and finish are at Technohub Woerden, and the course is made extra festive with acts and entertainment.
course_highlights: Course through Woerden city centre
Right through iconic and cultural buildings
Surprising acts and entertainment along the route
additional: The Culture Run is a fun run where participants can choose between 5 or 10 km, walking or running. The event is suitable for all ages, families and groups of friends. The number of race entries is limited due to capacity constraints at various locations along the route. The start and finish are at Technohub Woerden. The event is made extra festive with surprising acts and entertainment along and on the route. Course through the city centre and cultural buildings, entertainment along the route, two distances (5 and 10 km), walking or running.

description: De 15 van Wassenaar is an atmospheric running event taking place on Sunday, 11 October 2026. Participants can choose between a distance of 15 kilometres or 7.5 kilometres, both of which run through Wassenaar’s village centre, estates and villa neighbourhoods. The event combines a sporting challenge with a festive atmosphere, including refreshments along the way, a medal and an after-party to celebrate the achievement. The race is organised with a focus on charitable causes and an engaged crowd along the scenic course.
course_highlights: Route through the village centre, estates and villa neighbourhoods
Refreshments along the way, with 2 drink stations and a fruit point
Enthusiastic crowd along the scenic course
additional: All participants receive refreshments along the way, a race bib, a medal, fruit and their first drink at the finish. There is a staffed cloakroom and an after-party. The minimum age is 16 for the 7.5 km and 18 for the 15 km. There are 2 drink stations and a fruit point along the way. The route will be closed to traffic, with traffic marshals and temporary closures. Registration via the website; donations to charitable causes are possible. Start time is 14:30. Minimum age is 16 or 18. A medal and after-party are included.

name: Rondje Bussloo
description: Rondje Bussloo is a welcoming running event around the Bussloo recreation area, organised by the team behind Rondje Oeken. The courses for both distances follow paved paths through varied scenery of water, woodland and open fields, and are suitable for both recreational and experienced runners. The start and finish are at Strandhuys De Enk in Wilp, which also has a welcoming hospitality venue. The event is known for its sporty, friendly atmosphere and takes place on Sunday 11 October 2026 at 10:30.
course_highlights: Course on paved paths through varied scenery of water, woodland and open fields
Start and finish at Strandhuys De Enk, with a beautiful view over the water
Suitable for recreational and experienced runners
additional: Race numbers will be available at the race office on the day and will not be sent out in advance. Parking at Bussloo costs €3.50 and must be paid digitally when driving out through the barrier. Toilets are available at Strandhuys De Enk. There is a welcoming hospitality venue at the start and finish where supporters can cheer on runners. Fun for all ages, a route with different starting points, route markers, and use of the Strava app for route tracking.
